articles.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
articles.authors: Yue Lin, Yusi Huang, Junming Zhou et al.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

articles.title: The So-Called "Vastus Lateralis Obliquus" is the Most Distal Part of the Vastus Intermedius.
articles.authors: Takafumi Ono, Mio Imai, Yuto Kawasaki et al.
articles.abstract: The vastus lateralis (VL) has long been described as comprising a longitudinal part (vastus lateralis longus, VLL) and an oblique part (vastus lateralis obliquus, VLO), the latter inserting onto the superolateral border of the patella and traditionally regarded as a component of the VL that stabilizes the patella laterally. However, the anatomical relationship between the VLO and the remainder of the VL has never been rigorously defined, and electromyographic studies have independently regarded the muscle belly emerging at the distolateral thigh as the "superficial region of the vastus intermedius (VI)." To address this discrepancy, we re-examined the structure and innervation of the VLO in five thighs from five embalmed cadavers by gross dissection. The belly conventionally identified as the VLO was present in all specimens and inserted onto the superolateral patella. When the VLL was reflected, this belly was continuous with the VI, which arose broadly from the anterior surface of the femoral shaft; thus, the VLO was the most distal portion of the VI protruding lateral to the lateral border of the VL. Consistently, this region was supplied by the terminal twigs of the lateral branch of the VI (femoral nerve), whereas the branch to the VL did not reach it. We conclude that the so-called VLO is not part of the VL but the distal part of the VI. This reinterpretation reconciles the anatomical convention with electromyographic findings and has implications for anatomical nomenclature, interpretation of VI surface electromyography, and understanding the traction source in painful bipartite patella.

articles.title: Conservation of a synaptic blueprint across the animal kingdom.
articles.authors: Aiden J Houcek, Ege T Kavalali
articles.abstract: Chemical synapses are fundamental computational units of the nervous system that enable rapid and precise information transfer through the nanoscale organization of presynaptic and postsynaptic components. Despite hundreds of millions of years of animal evolution and extraordinary diversity in nervous system architectures, the core physiological principles of chemical synaptic transmission remain remarkably conserved. Studies across Drosophila melanogaster, zebrafish, Caenorhabditis elegans, frogs and mammals reveal recurring principles governing active-zone organization, synaptic vesicle exocytosis, calcium signalling and postsynaptic specialization. Here, we examine the evolution of chemical synapses across the animal kingdom, focusing on the relationship between molecular diversification, nanoscale organization and functional conservation. We propose that the evolutionary stability of synapses reflects, in part, a stringent biophysical constraint imposed by the requirements for rapid chemical communication. We further consider how these conserved synaptic operations are assembled into neural circuits of dramatically different complexities, as well as the ctenophore nervous system as a critical test case for distinguishing molecular conservation from architectural and functional convergence. Across species, the emerging picture is that evolution has adhered to conserving the geometry and organizational principles of chemical synapses more stringently than a precise molecular composition. Synapses thus represent stable yet adaptable information-processing architectures in which conserved nanoscale constraints coexist with molecular flexibility and extensive diversification of neural circuits.

articles.title: Food as Biological Information: A Testable Dietome Framework for Precision Nutrition and Whole-Food Meal Design.
articles.authors: Mohammad Nazrul Islam Bhuiyan
articles.abstract: Nutrition science has established the importance of energy, essential nutrients, dietary patterns, and food matrices, yet researchers often study these dimensions separately from the biological systems that transform and interpret a meal. This Perspective proposed the Dietome as a testable, systems-level description of food-derived inputs and the Informational Nutrition Framework (INF), comprising encoding, transmission, decoding, execution, and biological memory. The framework integrates sensory perception and eating behaviour with digestion, microbial metabolism, host signalling, and context-dependent responses. Its novelty is not the claim that food contains a literal code, but the proposal to connect food composition and structure to measurable, falsifiable predictions about meal-level responses. Evidence from personalized postprandial prediction, foodome network analysis, microbial short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-associated chromatin regulation, and computational diet modelling illustrates both opportunity and limitations. A worked meal example shows how to evaluate minimally processed foods and their combinations before considering engineered formulations. The Perspective also identifies sustainability, developmental nutrition, and food-allergy prevention as domains requiring cautious, evidence-specific application. Dietary microRNAs and long-term nutritional memory remain less established than conventional nutrient and microbial-metabolite pathways. The framework should therefore be judged by prospective validation, causal evidence, clinical utility, cultural acceptability, and environmental performance, not by terminology alone.

articles.title: Effect of Energy Restriction Combined with Probiotic Supplementation on Body Weight and Adiposity-Related Parameters in Adults with Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.authors: Marcus V L Dos Santos Quaresma, Camila Guazzelli Marques, Ana Carolina Oumatu Magalhães et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Gut microbiota modulation has been proposed as an adjunct strategy for obesity management, but the additional effects of probiotics during energy restriction (ER) remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether probiotic supplementation combined with ER improves body weight and adiposity-related outcomes in adults with overweight or obesity compared with ER alone. DATA SOURCES: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and LILACS were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing ER plus probiotics with ER alone or ER plus placebo. DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently screened the studies and extracted the data. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was body weight (BW); secondary outcomes were Body Mass Index (BMI), fat mass (FM), body fat percentage (BF%), waist circumference (WC), and fat-free mass (FFM). DATA ANALYSIS: Nineteen randomized controlled trials involving 1343 participants were included, of which 16 contributed to the meta-analysis. Interventions lasted 3-20 weeks, probiotic doses ranged from 1.8 × 106 to 1.5 × 1011 colony-forming units / day, and ER ranged from fixed deficits of 300-1000 kcal/day to relative reductions of 20% to 30%. Random-effects models showed no additional effect of probiotics on BW (mean difference [MD], -0.41 kg; 95% CI, -1.21 to 0.40), BMI (-0.12 kg/m²; -0.39 to 0.15), BF% (-0.63%; -1.52 to 0.26), WC (-0.33 cm; -1.06 to 0.39), or FFM (0.03 kg; -0.18 to 0.24). A small reduction in FM favored ER plus probiotics (-0.34 kg; -0.60 to -0.08; P = .016) and remained significant after excluding high-risk-of-bias studies. CONCLUSION: Adding probiotics to ER does not meaningfully enhance weight loss or body composition outcomes. Although FM was modestly reduced, the magnitude of the reduction was small, and its clinical relevance remains uncertain across the included randomized clinical trials overall. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. CRD42024619326.

articles.title: Layered anatomy of the greater and lesser occipital nerves with photogrammetry-based three-dimensional models: a cadaveric study.
articles.authors: Wei Zhou, Haosu Zhang, Lean Sun et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The superficial neurovascular anatomy of the posterior occipital region is important for occipital nerve block, greater occipital nerve (GON) decompression, and posterior fossa incision planning. However, the continuous layered relationship between the medial GON-occipital artery (OA) region and the lateral lesser occipital nerve (LON) channel remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: This cadaveric study examined 10 formalin-fixed specimens (20 sides). Layer-by-layer dissection documented nerve courses, emergence points, diameters, terminal branches, neurovascular relationships, GON-LON communications, and relationships with the OA and adjacent muscles. Photogrammetry-based three-dimensional models were constructed for visualization, not quantitative measurement. RESULTS: The GON and LON were identified on all 20 sides. The GON had 6.0 ± 1.4 terminal branches. Its trapezius muscle/fascial emergence point was located 25.4 ± 3.2 mm horizontally from the posterior midline and 14.0 ± 2.2 mm vertically from the external occipital protuberance (EOP) level. GON-OA relationships comprised a single crossing on 3 sides, multiple crossings on 8 sides, continuous contact on 5 sides, and coiling on 4 sides. The LON traversed a trapezius muscle-related plane on 9 sides and followed a posterior sternocleidomastoid muscle-border course on 11 sides. In descriptive side-level comparisons, the trapezius muscle-related emergence point was closer to the posterior midline and EOP level but farther from the mastoid reference line than the posterior sternocleidomastoid muscle-border emergence point. GON-LON communications were observed on 17 sides. CONCLUSION: These findings support a layered, pathway-based, and conceptual zone-based model of posterior occipital neurovascular anatomy, rather than localization based only on isolated surface landmarks.

articles.title: Facial artery morphology assessed by computed tomography angiography: a mixed-effects morphometric analysis of age, sex, and laterality.
articles.authors: Sindy Melissa Sanchez-Romo, Adrian Manuel Verdines-Perez, Mario Campos-Coy et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The facial artery is the principal arterial supply to the midface and is among the most frequently encountered vascular structures during facial reconstructive, aesthetic, and minimally invasive procedures. Precise knowledge of its anatomical course and morphometric characteristics is essential to minimize vascular complications. However, previous morphometric studies have largely been descriptive and have rarely accounted for bilateral anatomical correlation or simultaneously evaluated the independent effects of age, sex, and laterality using appropriate multivariable statistical models. METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using computed tomography angiography (CTA) examinations from 103 adults, yielding 201 evaluable facial arteries. Standardized three-dimensional morphometric measurements were obtained at the inferior border of the mandible and the lateral alar base. Linear mixed-effects models incorporating patient-specific random intercepts were used to evaluate the effects of age, sex, side, and CTA diagnostic category while accounting for within-subject correlation. Measurement reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Bland-Altman analysis, and Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: Type III, according to the Furukawa classification, was the predominant anatomical pattern (67.2%). Among 98 patients with bilateral visualization, Furukawa type showed complete right-left concordance (100%; κ = 1.00). In an additional patient-level logistic model, neither age (OR 0.992 per year; 95% CI, 0.965-1.020; P = 0.584) nor female sex (OR 1.793; 95% CI, 0.767-4.191; P = 0.178) was significantly associated with Type III versus Type II. For continuous morphometric variables, no systematic laterality effect was detected, although individual-level bilateral agreement varied across parameters. After Holm correction across morphometric outcomes, women had a smaller facial artery diameter at the inferior border of the mandible and a shorter zygomatic arch-facial artery distance than men, while increasing age was independently associated with a shorter oral commissure-facial artery distance. Quantitative morphometric measurements demonstrated good-to-excellent observer reproducibility (intraobserver ICC: 0.900-0.960; interobserver ICC: 0.760-0.860), whereas categorical assessment of facial artery position relative to the nasolabial sulcus showed perfect intraobserver (κ = 1.00) and substantial interobserver agreement (κ = 0.79). CONCLUSIONS: CTA provides a reproducible morphometric assessment of the facial artery. No systematic laterality effect was identified for continuous morphometric variables, although individual bilateral agreement varied by measurement, while Furukawa type showed complete bilateral concordance in patients with both arteries visualized. Age and sex were not significantly associated with Furukawa Type III versus Type II, but they influenced selected continuous morphometric parameters. These findings characterize facial artery anatomy in a Mexican clinical cohort and may inform individualized anatomical assessment and preprocedural planning; they do not establish procedural risk thresholds.

articles.title: The paracondylar process: anatomical relationships and clinical implications.
articles.authors: Beitris Chiu, Nigel Williams, Hong Kuan Kok et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The paracondylar process (PCP) is a rare and infrequently reported anatomical variant, where the incomplete separation of the lowest occipital sclerotome (proatlas) and uppermost cervical sclerotome results in a complete bony projection that meets with an epitransverse process of the atlas. We report a case that highlights the imaging and anatomical relationships of the PCP, particularly with the vertebral artery (VA), which has been given little attention in literature despite its important symptomatic and neurosurgical implications. CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old male presented with longstanding limitation to neck movement, left‑sided headaches and occasional dizzy spells. Cervical computed tomography (CT) imaging demonstrated a bony strut projecting inferiorly from the skull base, laterally adjacent to the left occipital condyle, articulating with the epitransverse process of C1. Though CT angiography was not performed, close examination of the course of the left vertebral artery on the soft tissue CT windows demonstrated an intimate relationship of the artery coursing immediately medial to the bony process in its V3 segment. We present a three-dimensional reconstruction prepared via segmentation and close reading of the soft tissue CT to illuminate the expected course of the vertebral artery and its' relationship to the PCP. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates the anatomical and clinical significance of the paracondylar process (PCP), with a particular focus on its relationship with the vertebral artery. Whilst rare, this finding carries important clinical implications if surgical resection is to be contemplated.

articles.title: Cortical bone geometry and static gravitational loads in neosauropod dinosaurs: Implications for biomechanical constraints on terrestrial gigantism.
articles.authors: Tito Aureliano, Aline M Ghilardi, Holly N Woodward et al.
articles.abstract: Sauropod dinosaurs achieved unprecedented terrestrial gigantism, raising questions about the biomechanical limits of bone under extreme gravitational loads. We estimated static gravitational pressures (Pg) on appendicular cortical bone in neosauropods, including diplodocoids, brachiosaurids, and titanosaurs. We did this by measuring cortical thickness, estimating body masses, and calculating pressures on limb bones. We compared the results with the theoretical fracture thresholds of composite cortical bone (~150-200 MPa) and pure crystalline hydroxyapatite (~1000 MPa). In the largest specimens, Pg remained two orders of magnitude below the compressive strength of hydroxyapatite. These estimates are a conservative lower bound because they assume simultaneous four-limb support. They are also substantially lower (>15 MPa) than the functional failure threshold of composite cortical bone. Dynamic behaviors raise these values: during slow locomotion, a single hindlimb may briefly support the entire hindquarter load, and the weight distribution between fore- and hindlimbs varies markedly with center-of-mass position. Even so, rearing on the hindlimbs in the largest titanosaurs (>25 metric tons) would remain within safe limits defined by composite-bone failure thresholds. Neosauropod lineages show distinct biomechanical strategies. Diplodocoids kept a posteriorly positioned center of mass compatible with facultative bipedal rearing. Brachiosaurids shifted it cranially through neck and forelimb hypertrophy. Titanosaurs reached extreme sizes through enhanced secondary bone remodeling and extensive postcranial pneumatization. Cortical thickening is consistently associated with increasing gravitational loads across Neosauropoda. However, this static model does not test whether it was the primary evolutionary response, compared with other strategies such as trabecular densification and postcranial pneumaticity.

articles.title: Electrophysiological properties of mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive.
articles.authors: Stijn Voerman, Xiang Wang, Xiaolu Wang et al.
articles.abstract: The neocortex has the largest volume, whereas the cerebellum houses the most neurons of the mammalian brain, underscoring paramount functions for interactions between them. Neocortical projections to the cerebellum involve both the mossy fibre and climbing fibre systems; mossy fibres find their origin predominantly in the pons, whereas the climbing fibres are relayed via subnuclei of the inferior olive (IO) that receive cortical input via the mesodiencephalic junction (MDJ). Given that climbing fibres regulate cerebellar plasticity in a timing-dependent manner, the MDJ-IO pathway probably contributes to both sensorimotor and cognitive learning. However, the physiological properties of IO-projecting MDJ neurons remain largely unknown. Here, we made targeted whole-cell recordings in brain slices of the mouse MDJ, separating IO- from non-IO-projecting neurons following retrograde tracing. We show that IO-projecting neurons are, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, highly spontaneously active and capable of high-frequency bursts of ≤350 Hz during current injections. Optogenetic stimulation shows that excitatory neocortical inputs to IO-projecting MDJ neurons can be integrated directly with excitatory inputs from the cerebellar nuclei. Moreover, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, IO-projecting MDJ neurons depolarize and repolarize quickly, and hyperpolarizing inputs consistently trigger rebound action potentials upon stimulus offset. This hyperpolarization is probably induced predominantly by inhibitory inputs from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey, which provide prominent bilateral inputs to MDJ neurons, as revealed by viral tracing in Gad2-Cre mice. Our results highlight how neocortical inputs to the MDJ can be transformed into diverse IO firing patterns and thereby contribute to the required specifics of cerebellar learning. KEY POINTS: The mesodiencephalic junction is an important brainstem region connecting the cerebral cortex with the cerebellum through its projection to the inferior olive, the sole source of the climbing fibres that drive cerebellar learning. We find that mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive represent a population of physiologically distinct neurons, capable of high firing frequencies and rebound activity following hyperpolarization. We reveal that mesodiencephalic junction neurons receive prominent excitatory inputs from neocortex and cerebellar nuclei, whereas their main inhibitory inputs are derived from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey. These findings shed light on how the activity of neurons in the mesodiencephalic junction can be regulated and how these neurons might influence activity in the inferior olive, and thereby cerebellar learning.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation as a contemporary antioxidant intervention in myocardial infarction.
articles.authors: Gabriel Matheus Da Silva Batista, Ighor Luiz Azevedo Teixeira, Ednei Luiz Antonio et al.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a complex cascade of structural and functional alterations that frequently culminate in adverse cardiac remodelling and heart failure. Central to this process is the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt mitochondrial function, impair calcium handling, and activate pro-apoptotic and pro-fibrotic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged as a non-invasive therapeutic approach capable of modulating several key biological processes involved in post-infarction remodelling. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that PBM reduces infarct size, attenuates ventricular dilation, and improves both systolic and diastolic function. Through the absorption of red to near-infrared light by mitochondrial chromophores, particularly cytochrome c oxidase, PBM enhances cellular bioenergetics, modulates ROS production and activates redox-sensitive signalling pathways. These effects promote a shift from detrimental oxidative stress toward controlled ROS signalling and, in turn, facilitate cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic responses. In addition, PBM promotes the mobilization of progenitor cells, contributing to tissue repair and microvascular restoration. Although still limited, the available clinical evidence suggests that PBM may confer modest improvements in cardiac function. However, variability in treatment protocols, delivery methods and study designs currently precludes definitive conclusions regarding its clinical efficacy. In summary, PBM represents a promising strategy for modulating oxidative stress after MI, integrating metabolic, redox and signalling pathways to attenuate cardiac remodelling. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to establish standardized protocols and to clarify its therapeutic potential in cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: A balancing act: Passive ankle exoskeletons alter neuromuscular function and postural stability during balance.
articles.authors: Jemima C N Po, James L Williamson, Jordan Yee et al.
articles.abstract: Spring-loaded passive ankle exoskeletons have the potential to modulate neuromuscular function during standing balance by altering the mechanical demands placed on the muscle-tendon units spanning the ankle joint. This study investigated the effect of exoskeleton assistance on postural stability and neuromuscular function across balance conditions of varying difficulty. We hypothesised that assistance would improve postural stability and reduce ankle plantar flexor muscle activity during balance tasks, although these benefits may vary with balance task complexity. Participants performed standing balance tasks of varying difficulty with and without rotational stiffness provided by spring-loaded ankle exoskeletons. Balance tasks included (i) quiet standing with eyes open (EO), (ii) eyes closed (EC), and (iii) reduced base of support (RBOS). We recorded centre of pressure (COP)-based postural sway measures, lower limb joint kinematics, muscle activation data from the medial (MG) and lateral gastrocnemii (LG), soleus (SOL), and tibialis anterior (TA), and MG fascicle behaviour. Exoskeleton assistance reduced LG and SOL activation but also altered joint kinematics and coordination. Ankle-based adjustments were most evident with assistance during simpler balance tasks (EO and EC), whereas assistance during the most challenging task (RBOS) was associated with increases in COP sway velocity, COP variability and TA activation. Our results suggest that despite the potential energetic benefits from offloading the plantar flexors, passive ankle exoskeletons may induce unintended effects that hinder the control of standing balance, particularly during more challenging conditions. Further work is needed to determine the mechanisms underlying these effects.

articles.title: Combined time-restricted feeding and resistance training enhance tirzepatide-induced improvements in adiposity and whole-body insulin sensitivity in female mice.
articles.authors: Ana Paula Azevêdo Macêdo, Luciana Renata da Conceição de Mattis, Robson Damasceno de Lima et al.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide is a dual agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors with potent effects on body weight regulation, glucose homeostasis and metabolic health. However, its interaction with dietary and exercise interventions as well as its impact on obesity and hepatic metabolic pathways, particularly in females, remain unclear. Here, we tested whether tirzepatide, alone or combined with time-restricted feeding (TRF) or resistance training, modulates energy balance, strength performance, adipose tissue remodelling, insulin sensitivity and hepatic lipid accumulation in female mice. Female Swiss mice after 10 weeks of obesity induction were treated with tirzepatide, TRF or resistance training for 8 weeks. Tirzepatide was administered subcutaneously using a dose-escalation protocol. TRF consisted of a 12 h feeding window, and resistance training was performed as stair climbing on alternating days. Body weight, caloric intake and feed efficiency were monitored longitudinally. Glucose homeostasis was assessed by intraperitoneal glucose and insulin tolerance tests. Adipose depots, skeletal muscle and liver mass were quantified, and hepatic lipid accumulation was evaluated by histology and RT-qPCR of lipogenic metabolism genes. Tirzepatide reduced body weight gain and feed efficiency, consistent with a negative energy balance. When combined with TRF and resistance training, tirzepatide accelerated weight loss, and the addition of resistance training further enhanced this effect, bringing body weight close to control levels. These effects were associated with reduced adipose mass and adipocyte hypertrophy, indicating improved adipose tissue remodelling. Resistance training improved strength performance and increased skeletal muscle mass. Tirzepatide combined with TRF, with or without resistance training, improved glucose tolerance in female mice. All interventions reduced hepatic lipid accumulation. Collectively, tirzepatide, particularly in combination with TRF and resistance training, exerts enhanced metabolic benefits on obesity, insulin sensitivity and metabolic regulation in female mice. KEY POINTS: Tirzepatide combined with time-restricted feeding and resistance training produced greater reductions in body weight and adiposity in obese female mice. Combined interventions improved whole-body insulin sensitivity more effectively than isolated strategies. Resistance training preserved skeletal muscle mass during tirzepatide-induced weight loss. All interventions similarly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and lipogenic gene expression. Tirzepatide-based therapies enhanced systemic metabolic health without additional hepatic benefits from combined interventions.

articles.title: Regional Histological Anatomy of the Supraperiosteal Tissues of the Oral Cavity: Implications for Periodontal Flap Surgery and Periosteal Releasing Incisions.
articles.authors: Joe Iwanaga, Norio Kitagawa, Michitsuna Katafuchi et al.
articles.abstract: Periodontal and implant procedures increasingly involve tissue planes superficial to the periosteum, yet their regional anatomy remains poorly understood. This study conducted a histological investigation of the supraperiosteal anatomy of the oral cavity and its implications for periosteal releasing incisions (PRIs). Intraoral dissection of the mimetic muscle was performed using a fresh anatomical donor. Subsequently, maxillary and mandibular incisor, premolar, and molar regions from five formalin-fixed donors were examined histologically using Masson's trichrome staining. Muscular, neural, vascular, and connective tissue structures within 5 mm of the facial alveolar bone surface were evaluated. Supraperiosteal tissue architecture differed markedly by region. Muscular, neural, and vascular structures showed distinct region-specific distributions. The mental nerve and its branches were identified in the mandibular premolar region, whereas facial and buccal vessels were present near the bone surface in the posterior regions. Muscle attachment and intervening connective tissue also varied regionally. Structures potentially injured during PRI and their associated risks are region-dependent. PRI should therefore be guided by region-specific anatomy and the tissues requiring release for sufficient flap mobility rather than by a predetermined incision depth alone.

articles.title: The gut-muscle-joint axis in osteoarthritis: Mechanistic insights and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.authors: Asima Karim, Firdos Ahmad, Rizwan Qaisar
articles.abstract: Emerging evidence highlights a complex crosstalk between the gut microbiota, musculoskeletal tissues, and the joint microenvironment, revealing osteoarthritis (OA) as a systemic disorder rather than a localized cartilage disease. The gut-muscle-joint interaction integrates microbial dysbiosis, chronic inflammation, and metabolic dysregulation to influence cartilage homeostasis, muscle strength, and neuromuscular stability. Building upon previously described gut-osteoarthritis and gut-muscle interactions, the Gut-Muscle-Joint (GMJ) axis is presented as an integrative framework linking intestinal permeability, microbial metabolites, systemic inflammatory signaling, neuromuscular health, skeletal muscle function, and joint integrity. Perturbations in this axis amplify oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and extracellular matrix degradation across musculoskeletal tissues. Understanding GMJ axis-driven mechanisms offers novel preventive and therapeutic strategies that target microbiome restoration, metabolic reprogramming, and neuromuscular health through probiotics, postbiotics, AMPK-SIRT1 activators, and structured exercise. This integrative perspective positions the GMJ axis as a unifying framework for intervention, enabling precision approaches to preserve joint function, reduce sarcopenia, and attenuate OA progression.

articles.title: Supplementation with fortified balanced energy-protein during pregnancy and lactation and infant growth outcomes in southern Nepal: a community-based 2×2 factorial randomized trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Tsering P Lama, Parul Christian, Yunhee Kang et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Small-for-gestational age birth and infant linear growth faltering are prevalent in South Asia. The World Health Organization recommends balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplementation in pregnancy for undernourished populations, but evidence on the extension of supplementation through lactation to improve infant growth remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine the effect of daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy and lactation on infant mean length-for-age z-score (LAZ) and secondary growth outcomes at 6 months of age. METHODS: MINT (Maternal Infant Nutrition Trial) was a 2x2 factorial, household randomized, unblinded efficacy trial to assess a daily fortified BEP supplement during pregnancy and/or lactation compared to no supplement on birth and infant growth outcomes in Sarlahi, Nepal. A modified intention-to-treat analysis estimated the effects of supplementation on infant growth outcomes using linear and Poisson regression models. Models without and with adjustment for birth size were used to estimate the overall effect and the effect independent of birth size, respectively. RESULTS: Among 1,554 mothers and 1,568 infants randomized after delivery, there was no interaction between pregnancy and lactation supplementation on the primary infant growth outcome. Neither BEP supplementation during pregnancy nor lactation had an effect on mean infant LAZ at 6 months (unadjusted mean difference for pregnancy: 0.01 [95% CI: -0.10, 0.12]; for lactation -0.02 [95% CI: -0.13, 0.09]). Significant differences were not observed for any secondary outcomes: mean weight-for-length z-scores, weight-for-age z-scores, infant weight, length, head circumference, mid-upper arm circumference or prevalence of stunting, wasting, and underweight at 6-months or for a subset of infants at 12-months. Null effects persisted after adjustment for birth size. CONCLUSIONS: In rural Nepal, daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy or early lactation did not improve linear or ponderal growth of infants at 6- or 12-months. To reduce the burden of early infant growth faltering, alternative strategies should be considered. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT03668977. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03668977?term=nct03668977&rank=1.

articles.title: The Role of Physical Preparation in Motorsport Athletes Across Different Vehicle Types: A Narrative Review.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Gabriel Vieira Barros, Ana Ramos, Maurício Facchini et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite motorsport's widespread appeal, early performance models did not consider drivers as athletes, and even drivers often struggled with this classification, which historically contributed to their exclusion from research focused on athletic performance. Slowly but steadily, this paradigm has been changing. PURPOSE: To review the evolution of physical conditioning in land-based motorsports and to examine the specific physiological and physical demands imposed on drivers by different vehicle types. A narrative review was conducted to synthesize historical perspectives, physiological demands, and training approaches in motorsport. Peer-reviewed studies, practical reports, opinion articles, and relevant online materials were analyzed to describe the evolution of the physical conditioning required across racing categories. The physical demands in motorsports are characterized by sustained cardiovascular strain, significant neuromuscular loading, large and sustained G-force exposure, and pronounced thermal stress. These demands vary according to vehicle type. Closed-wheel drivers are particularly exposed to prolonged heat stress and require comprehensive muscular endurance and thermoregulatory adaptation. Open-wheel drivers experience large G-forces, demanding exceptional neck and lower-limb strength. Two-wheel riders require enhanced handgrip strength, dynamic neuromuscular control, and high levels of aerobic capacity. CONCLUSIONS: Tailored conditioning programs addressing the distinct physiological, neuromuscular, and thermoregulatory demands of each motorsport category are closely linked to performance and safety. Further systematic evaluation of the empirical evidence is necessary to enhance the ecological validity of training recommendations and strengthen their application in competitive motorsport.

articles.title: Central and Peripheral Fatigue Following Free-Weight and Smith Machine Squat Training: Neuromuscular Efficiency in Knee Extensors.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Daniel Marcos-Frutos, Antonio Martos-Arregui, Amador García-Ramos et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Free-weight (FW) and machine-guided exercises have been shown to promote similar strength and hypertrophy adaptations. Under such conditions, the exercise modality that induces less fatigue may be considered more efficient and advantageous for training prescription. PURPOSE: To compare the mechanical, perceptual, and neuromuscular fatigue induced by a squat strength training session performed with FW or a Smith machine (SM). METHODS: Nineteen young strength-trained men (age = 23.5 [3.8] y; strength training experience = 4.7 [2.4] y) completed 2 sessions in a randomized order, each involving 4 sets of 9 repetitions at 70% 1-repetition maximum and differing only in the squat modality (FW or SM). Mechanical fatigue was assessed by velocity loss during training and by pre-post changes in isometric force; perceptual fatigue was assessed by subjectively estimated repetitions in reserve and neuromuscular fatigue (ie, peripheral and central fatigue components) via the twitch interpolation technique during isometric unilateral knee extension. RESULTS: No fatigue differences were observed for velocity loss or perceptual fatigue variables (P = .136-.313). In contrast, most peripheral and central fatigue variables showed significant posttraining differences (P < .001-.021), with FW squats promoting greater posttraining peripheral and central fatigue. CONCLUSIONS: Given the comparable adaptations typically reported for FW and SM exercises, the SM squat may represent a more efficient option for promoting strength adaptations while minimizing neuromuscular fatigue in knee extensors.

articles.title: Can Graded Blood Flow Restriction Pressure Enhance and Prolong Postactivation Performance Enhancement Induced by Plyometric Jumps?
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Liang Wang, Chengyu Ke, Olivier Girard et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study investigated whether adding blood flow restriction at graded arterial occlusion pressures (AOPs) during plyometric jumps can enhance and prolong postactivation performance enhancement. METHODS: Twenty-one resistance-trained men completed 40 maximal plyometric jumps under 4 conditions: jumps alone or combined with blood flow restriction at 50%, 60%, or 70% AOP. Countermovement jump (CMJ) and squat jump (SJ) height were assessed at baseline and at 15 seconds, 4, 8, and 12 minutes postexercise. RESULTS: Significant condition × time interactions were observed for both CMJ height (P = .01, ηp2=.13) and SJ height (P < .001, ηp2=.14). The 70% AOP condition produced significant performance improvements across all time points (P < .01, g = 0.36-0.53). At 50% and 60% AOP, performance improved at 15 seconds and 4 minutes (P < .01, g = 0.19-0.40), with CMJ effects persisting to 8 minutes but disappearing by 12 minutes in both jumps. The control condition showed a transient CMJ improvement at 15 seconds (P = .046, g = 0.20) but no SJ change. Compared with other conditions, 70% AOP outperformed control at 4 and 12 minutes for CMJ and at 12 minutes for SJ, and exceeded 50% AOP at 15 seconds in both tests. CONCLUSION: Plyometric jumps combined with 70% AOP produced a greater and more sustained postactivation performance enhancement response than jumps alone, suggesting that blood flow restriction may serve as a potential adjunct to enhance the acute effects of plyometric conditioning activities.

articles.title: Effects of Ballistic and Traditional Half-Squat Training With Light Loads on Strength, Jump, and Sprint Performance in Young Rugby Players: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Santiago Zabaloy, Piotr Zmijewski, Tomás T Freitas et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study examined the effects of two 6-week in-season training interventions using light loads (30%-40% 1-repetition maximum) and contrasting strategies: (1) ballistic jump squat (JS) and (2) traditional half squat on strength, jump, and sprint performance in youth rugby players. METHODS: Twenty-five highly trained players completed the randomized controlled trial, training 3 times per week alongside regular rugby practice and competition. Performance assessments included half-squat 1-repetition maximum, mean propulsive velocity, squat jump, countermovement jump, and 30-m sprint speed at 3 time points. RESULTS: Both groups improved maximal strength and jump performance, with greater gains observed in the JS group (≈7% vs 4% for strength, ≈16% vs 8% for jump performance). The JS group also showed specific improvements in relative strength and heavy-load mean propulsive velocity, whereas the half-squat group improved mean propulsive velocity at lighter loads. A significant group × time interaction was found for countermovement jump, favoring the JS condition. Despite these neuromuscular improvements, sprint performance decreased in both groups, with no between-group differences. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that light-load ballistic training may provide a more effective stimulus for improving strength and power qualities during the in-season period, likely due to its velocity-oriented and fully accelerative nature. However, strength-power gains alone appear insufficient to prevent decreases in sprint performance under congested fixture schedules. From a practical standpoint, incorporating light-load ballistic exercises may enhance neuromuscular performance while minimizing fatigue, but additional sprint-specific training is required to maintain or improve sprint speed in youth rugby players.

articles.title: The Effect of Environmental Temperature on Physical Performance, Physiological and Perceptual Responses in Elite Versus Nonelite Male Beach Soccer Players.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Thiago Carvalho, Vincenzo Rago, João Brito et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: High environmental temperature (Te) is associated with adverse effects on athletes' performance. Whether such effects are comparable across different sports and competitive levels remains uncertain. We explored and compared the physical performance, physiological, and perceptual responses of elite and nonelite beach soccer players during official matches, focusing on the potential effects of Te. METHODS: One hundred fifty-four male beach soccer players were monitored across 13 official matches. Physical performance (locomotor activity and countermovement jump), heart rate, rate of perceived exertion, hydration (liquid intake and fluid loss), and Te were collected. Data were analyzed using multivariate analysis of variance, followed by multivariate analysis of covariance and interaction analyses. RESULTS: Elite players covered greater total distance (∼16%), high-speed running (∼19%), and sprinting (∼60%); performed more sprints (∼60%) and had ∼1-point higher rate of perceived exertion than nonelite players. After adjustment for Te, differences in total distance and rate of perceived exertion between competitive levels appeared attenuated. In contrast, small effects were observed for Vpeak (ηp2=.037) and accelerations (ηp2=.030), and a medium effect was observed for fluid loss (ηp2=.076). As Te increased, elite players tended to cover greater total distance while reducing high-intensity actions, whereas nonelite players showed progressively greater high-intensity efforts, with relatively stable HRpeak and HRmean, while time >85%HRpeak tended to increase. In matches played at Te ≥ 35 °C, elite players experienced ∼34% greater fluid loss than nonelite players. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that elite and nonelite beach soccer players may respond differently as Te increases, highlighting the need for monitoring and hydration strategies tailored to competitive level under high Te conditions.

articles.title: How Fast Is Thin Air? Empirical Altitude Adjustments for Indoor Track-and-Field Performance.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Atle G Guttormsen, Simen Guttormsen
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: In this study, we analyze the effects of altitude on athletic performance for running events and speed-dependent jumping events at indoor meets, and we evaluate whether the NCAA's altitude adjustment process is accurate. METHODS: We analyzed 688,625 running results and 215,933 jumping results from NCAA indoor competitions at 382 different indoor venues. We estimated altitude effects using athlete × season fixed effects. For running events 200 m and longer, we included a banked-track indicator to separate altitude from the mechanical advantage of a banked oval. RESULTS: Altitude improved sprint times by 0.3% to 0.5%/1000 m and jumping marks by 0.5% to 0.7%/1000 m. Pole vault improvements (0.66%-0.69%/1000 m) matched the quadratic speed-to-height prediction (h ∝ v2). For distance events, the altitude penalty (added time) rose from 0.5% to 0.9%/1000 m at 800 m to 2.7% to 3.0%/1000 m at 5000 m; the drag-oxygen crossover lay between 400 m and 800 m. The women's 800 m was penalized approximately twice as severely as the men's (0.92 vs 0.50%/1000 m). NCAA sprint corrections accounted for only 42% to 71% of the observed effects. CONCLUSIONS: NCAA sprint corrections under-correct sharply once track banking is accounted for; the 800 m requires sex-specific adjustments; and the absence of any field-event correction is a clear gap in the existing system.

articles.title: Dimensionality Reduction of Full-Body Strength-Power Metrics to Identify Distinct Strength Domains in Elite Rugby Union Athletes.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Leslie K D Payne, Matthew C Varley, David L Carey et al.
articles.abstract: Payne, LKD, Varley, MC, Carey, DL, Driller, MW, and James, LP. Dimensionality reduction of full-body strength-power metrics to identify distinct strength domains in elite rugby union athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to determine the extent of shared and unique information among strength tests and to evaluate whether factors identified through exploratory factor analysis reflect distinct strength domains in professional rugby union players. Twenty professional male rugby union athletes (age 24.4 ± 3.8 years; height 186.3 ± 5.2 cm; body mass 107.6 ± 10.9 kg) completed a battery of 4 upper-body and 5 lower-body isometric, dynamic, and reactive strength tests. A total of 18 metrics were entered into exploratory factor analysis to identify distinct strength domains. Exploratory factor analysis reduced the data set into 2 upper-body domains (pressing and pulling) and 4 lower-body domains (isometric, dynamic, reactive, and relative). These domains together explained 73% of the variance in the upper-body data and 79% of the variance in the lower-body data. The isometric domain was driven by early-phase force at 100 and 200 ms, while peak force contributed less strongly. The dynamic domain was defined by heavy squat velocity, which diverged inversely from countermovement jump height, reflecting load-velocity differences. The reactive domain was shaped by contact time and countermovement depth, highlighting the role of temporal mechanics. The relative domain was defined by drop jump height and countermovement jump momentum, emphasizing the influence of body mass on ballistic force expression. Eighteen test metrics were successfully reduced to 6 distinct domains of strength in professional rugby union athletes. This framework provides a concise basis for profiling upper-body and lower-body strength to reduce redundancy and retain key information needed for training and monitoring rugby athletes.

articles.title: Menu Evaluation Tools in Food Services: An Integrative Review.
articles.authors: Lívia Bacharini Lima, Emanuele Batistela Dos Santos, Raquel Braz Assunção Botelho et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: The growing demand for meals outside the home has boosted the food service sector, but there are constant concerns regarding the nutritional quality of the meals offered. In this scenario, menus play a strategic role in promoting health and in defining population dietary patterns. OBJECTIVE: This integrative review aimed to identify the instruments used to evaluate menus in food service settings across different contexts and target audiences. DATA SOURCES: This is an integrative review with a systematic search in the LILACS, Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science databases, with controlled and uncontrolled descriptors. Original studies published between 2003 and 2025 that described the development of menu evaluation instruments aimed at healthy food service were included. DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted on the characteristics of the instruments, including target population, food service setting, scope, evaluation approach, assessment perspectives, number of items, country of development, and validation status. DATA ANALYSIS: Data were summarized using descriptive statistics, including absolute and relative frequencies. A total of 29 studies were included, with a predominance of instruments aimed at children's menus (55.2%) and with a qualitative approach (72.4%). Brazil had the largest number of developed instruments, followed by Spain, the United States, and Portugal. Only 58.6% of the instruments presented some type of validation. The instruments varied in scope (menu or menu + context), evaluation method (qualitative, quantitative, or qualitative-quantitative), and the number of perspectives covered, with 10.3% multidimensional (ie, having 4 or more dimensions). CONCLUSION: The review showed advances in evaluating menus for the child population and in incorporating sustainability as an analytical parameter. However, gaps remain in validation and the development of multidimensional instruments, underscoring the need for validated and adapted tools to promote healthier, more sustainable menus.

articles.title: Dietary Polysaccharides for Overweight and Obesity Management: Targeting AMPK via the Gut Microbiota and Metabolites-A Review.
articles.authors: Zhongxing Chu, Zuomin Hu, Baitong Zhu et al.
articles.abstract: Obesity arises from dietary energy intake-expenditure imbalance. 5'-Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), a core regulator of biological energy metabolism, is a key target for obesity research and can be activated by endogenous stimuli, such as cellular stress and physical exercise. As natural active components with diverse sources and biological functions, dietary polysaccharides have shown potential lipid-lowering and antiobesity effects in preclinical studies. This narrative review systematically summarizes their structural characteristics, sources, absorption-utilization mechanisms and structure-activity relationships, focusing on their regulatory effects on obesity via the AMPK pathway. We searched PubMed and Web of Science for publications (2014-2026) using "dietary polysaccharides,""AMPK,""obesity," and "gut microbiota" as key words, screening original studies and reviews relevant to the core topic. Correlative evidence suggests that dietary polysaccharides are associated with altered expression of lipid metabolism-related factors through potential modulation of gut microbiota and its metabolites, with indirect links to AMPK activation. Such AMPK regulatory effects have tissue/organ specificity, and the causal relationship of each link remains to be rigorously established. Notably, the majority of current evidence derives from in vitro and rodent models, and extrapolation to human obesity management requires caution, as high-quality human clinical trials are urgently needed to validate the translational potential of these preclinical findings. This review clarifies the potential mechanism and existing research gaps of dietary polysaccharides in obesity alleviation, providing a scientific basis for the research and development of lipid-lowering functional foods based on dietary polysaccharides.

articles.title: Baseline Testosterone Stratification Reveals Divergent Hormonal Adaptations in Men and Women Undergoing Basic Combat Training.
articles.authors: Nicole M Sekel, Brittany Bozzini, Katelyn Guerriere Aaron et al.
articles.abstract: This study examined whether hormonal and body composition responses to 10-weeks of U.S. Army Basic Combat Training (BCT) differ by baseline testosterone and sex. Methods: Male (n=97) and female (n=105) trainees were stratified at baseline as having LOW (men <10.4 nmol/L; women <0.82 nmol/L) or NORMAL baseline testosterone. We measured serum total and free testosterone, sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG), luteinizing hormone (LH) and estradiol (E2) at weeks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 9 and cortisol weekly; dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) assessed body composition at week 0 and 9. Linear mixed models tested time and group effects; generalized linear models related baseline testosterone status and testosterone area under the curve with changes in body composition. Results: In LOW women, testosterone increased at each timepoint (all p<0.01), reaching concentrations 53% higher at week 9 compared to week 0 (30.2± 7.8 vs 19.7± 3.2 ng/dl). In men, testosterone increased (LOW: +76%; NORMAL: +23%) across BCT (all p<0.05), except at week 2. Among LOW men, concentrations stabilized by week 4 (344.8± 81.4 ng/dl) and remained normal. Cortisol was highest at baseline and declined in all men and in NORMAL women. LH and E2 remained stable in both sexes, while SHBG declined only in women, independent of baseline testosterone. Neither baseline testosterone nor cumulative exposure were associated with changes in lean or fat mass. Conclusions: SHBG and cortisol trajectories differed by sex and baseline testosterone status. Testosterone changes were sex specific, reflecting an anabolic training environment in men and modest increased androgen availability in LOW women.

articles.title: Persistent Skeletal Deficits Following Weight Restoration in a Rodent Model of Anorexia Nervosa.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Malihe Jafari, Daniel J Brooks, Benton Swanson et al.
articles.abstract: Purpose: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is associated with significant changes in bone density and microstructure. However, the extent and nature of skeletal recovery following weight restoration is unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate these changes in bone during simulated AN in rats across short- and long-term recovery. Methods: Female Sprague Dawley rats were exposed to 50-60% food restriction for 30 days to simulate AN, followed by recovery periods of 5, 15, and 30 days. Bone parameters were assessed longitudinally using peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) and micro-computed tomography (µCT). Bodyweight and muscle strength were correlated with bone parameters. Results: AN resulted in significant reductions in total and trabecular bone density, as well as impairments in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture. Even with weight restoration, these deficits persisted and the compensatory responses were not sufficient for bone recovery. Bodyweight showed an association with total and trabecular bone density. Measures of muscle strength also correlated with total and trabecular density and were additive in multiple regression analysis prediction of total and trabecular bone density when combined with bodyweight. Conclusion: Recovery from AN-induced bone disorders is incomplete even after weight restoration and likely requires targeted interventions beyond nutritional rehabilitation. Furthermore, muscle function is an important predictor of bone health when combined with bodyweight.

articles.title: Decoupled and diverse: A morphological examination of the two-jaw system in Mormyridae (Osteoglossiformes).
articles.authors: Kassandra L Ford, Rose Peterson, L Patricia Hernandez
articles.abstract: The tongue-bite apparatus (TBA) is a secondary jaw system found in Osteoglossomorpha and, convergently, Salmonidae. It is thought to have similar prey-processing functions as the pharyngeal jaws, possibly allowing the oral jaws to evolve separately for more efficient prey capture. The TBA is incredibly morphologically diverse, but this diversity has not been well documented across Mormyridae, the most speciose family within Osteoglossomorpha. In this study, we examined shape diversity, levels of evolutionary integration and modularity, and rates of evolution of both the TBA and other associated components of the skull in Mormyridae, both across the family and in its two subfamilies, Petrocephalinae and Mormyrinae. Petrocephalinae, the sister group to the rest of Mormyrinae, is less species rich and has evolved independently from Mormyrinae for approximately 50 million years. This has resulted in disparity across the two groups, not only morphologically but also in terms of electric organ discharges. Results of this study support different models of modularity of the skull for these two subfamilies, with Petrocephalines having two modules as compared to Mormyrine's four modules. In both groups, the TBA makes up its own module, often evolving faster than other components of the skull. We propose that this is an example of a truly decoupled two-jaw system, making it unique compared to the pharyngeal and oral jaws of other well-studied groups, such as cichlids and labrids.

articles.title: Effects of creatine supplementation on lean mass, muscle size and muscle performance during immobilisation and rehabilitation: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Jedd Pratt, Darren G Candow, Eric S Rawson et al.
articles.abstract: Creatine monohydrate (CrM) supplementation has established benefits in exercising populations; however, its efficacy during disuse and subsequent rehabilitation remains unclear. This systematic review assessed the effects of CrM supplementation on muscle size, lean mass and muscle performance (strength, power, endurance) during periods of disuse and rehabilitation. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. Six randomised placebo-controlled trials were included (n = 118, mean ages: 15-24 years, disuse model: 1-2 weeks limb-immobilisation). Two studies reported comparable reductions in quadriceps cross-sectional area (CSA; assessed via CT or NMR imaging) between CrM and placebo during disuse (-5.6% vs. -5.5%; -11.0% vs. -9.4%), whereas two reported smaller reductions from CrM supplementation in lower-limb lean mass (-5.6% vs. -8.9%) or preserved upper-limb lean mass (0.9% vs. -3.7%) (assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) or dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)). These contrasting findings may reflect limitations of BIA/DXA, including hydration effects, rather than preservation of muscle tissue. Effects on muscle performance were inconsistent, with favourable findings from CrM supplementation in upper- but not lower-limb models. Four studies included recovery, three of which used resistance-based rehabilitation. Two reported greater increases with CrM supplementation across quadriceps CSA (21.3% vs. 14.3%), lower-limb lean mass (5.6% vs. 3.8%), power (52.2% vs. 35.2%) and strength (28.7% vs. 22.8%). Current evidence does not unanimously support CrM supplementation as an effective countermeasure to mitigate disuse-induced muscle atrophy, lean mass loss or declines in muscle performance. Whether CrM supplementation meaningfully influences rehabilitation following disuse, particularly in older adults and clinical populations at greater risk of disuse atrophy and incomplete recovery, warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Transient gait instability during the initial phase of the 6-minute walk test in people with stroke: A nonlinear analysis using inertial measurement units.
articles.authors: Yasuhiro Inui, Yusaku Takamura, Shu Morioka
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In people with stroke (PwS), reduced gait speed and trunk acceleration changes in the latter half of the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) have been reported as fatigue-related, but temporal changes in motor control remain understudied. Clinicians often observe instability immediately after gait onset, yet quantitative evidence is scarce. This study used inertial measurement units (IMUs) and nonlinear analysis to examine fatigue-related changes and post-onset instability during the 6MWT in PwS. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 19 PwS and 19 age-matched controls completed the 6MWT wearing IMUs at the L5 vertebra and both ankles. Spatiotemporal parameters and stability indices (root mean square, harmonic ratio, sample entropy, short-term Lyapunov exponent [sLE]) were calculated. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) analyzed the 6-minute period both continuously and by comparing an initial phase (first 60 s) with the subsequent phase. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses were also performed. RESULTS: Continuous-time LMMs showed reduced cadence and increased double-support ratio in PwS. Among stability indices, only mediolateral sLE (sLE-ML) showed a significant group × phase interaction: increasing in the initial phase in PwS but not in controls. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses confirmed this finding was robust and specific to the 60-second cutoff. Initial-phase sLE-ML correlated negatively with Fugl-Meyer lower-extremity scores. CONCLUSIONS: PwS showed fatigue-related gait changes during the 6MWT, while mediolateral local dynamic stability transiently declined during the first 60 s before stabilizing. This instability was associated with motor paralysis, suggesting trunk IMU-based sLE-ML may reveal motor control deficits not captured by walking distance or speed.

articles.title: Complex cervical venous drainage with a common facial-paralaryngeal anastomosis receiving the superior thyroid vein.
articles.authors: Mugurel Constantin Rusu, Adelina Maria Jianu, Laura Octavia Grigoriţă et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Tributaries of the internal jugular vein (IJV) may form common trunks or interconnected drainage pathways. We report a complex right-sided cervical venous configuration involving separate facial and lingual-parapharyngeal-paralaryngeal pathways connected by an anastomotic arch receiving the superior thyroid vein. METHODS: An archived computed tomography angiogram (CTA) of a 68-year-old woman was retrospectively reviewed using Horos. Axial source images and three-dimensional volume renderings were assessed bilaterally, and linear measurements were obtained using the software's calliper tool. RESULTS: The common facial vein and a lingual-parapharyngeal-paralaryngeal channel terminated separately in the right IJV and were connected by an anastomotic arch. The superior thyroid vein originated from the left half of the thyroid isthmus, ascended in a left paramedian position, crossed rightwards posterior to the right anterior jugular vein, and joined the inferior end of the arch. Associated findings included right external jugular vein fenestration (2.23 × 0.58 cm) and a posterior external jugular vein connected to the transverse cervical vein by an anastomotic arch. CONCLUSION: This configuration represents interconnected cervical venous drainage pathways and does not establish duplication of a thyrolinguofacial trunk. Recognition of their tributaries, connections and separate jugular terminations may assist imaging interpretation and surgical planning.

articles.title: Left anterior laryngeal loop of the common carotid artery in a cluster of bilateral cervicothoracic vascular variants: a case report.
articles.authors: Viviana Dincă, Adelina Maria Jianu, Mugurel Constantin Rusu
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The common carotid artery (CCA) normally ascends in the carotid sheath, posterolateral to the larynx and trachea. Anterior or pretracheal CCA courses are rare and have been described mainly on the right, usually in relation to a high-riding brachiocephalic trunk (BCT) or another arch-level anomaly. We report a CTA case with a common-origin left CCA-BCT trunk, a high-riding BCT and bilateral carotid redundancy, including a left anterior laryngeal CCA loop. METHODS: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the aortic arch and bilateral carotid systems was reviewed using multiplanar reformatting and three-dimensional volume-rendered reconstruction. Vessel loops, branching points and relationships to the hyoid-laryngeal framework, thyroid gland and adjacent skeletal landmarks were recorded. RESULTS: CTA showed a common-origin left CCA-BCT trunk with a high-riding BCT measuring 3.27 cm. The right CCA formed a 1.79 cm lateral loop and bifurcated posterolateral to the hyoid-laryngeal framework; the right external carotid artery (ECA) gave rise to a linguofacial trunk and then formed a retromandibular loop. The left CCA formed a 2.15 cm intramediastinal loop and a 1.75 cm anterior laryngeal loop. The left superior thyroid artery arose directly from the CCA. The left ECA showed independent branching and a retromandibular loop. Tortuosity indices ranged from 33.1% to 92.7%; all segments were tortuous and the right internal carotid artery additionally formed a kink (apex angle 87.3°). CONCLUSION: This case documents a rare left anterior laryngeal CCA loop in association with bilateral carotid and external carotid branching variants. The left-sided anterior loop is the main surgical finding because it brings a major cervical artery close to the anterior laryngeal operative field. Recognition of this pattern is relevant before front-of-neck airway access, thyroid surgery, laryngotracheal surgery and central neck procedures.

articles.title: Sex-specific Lower Limb Strength, Flexibility, and Running Biomechanics in Adolescents With and Without Osgood-Schlatter Disease.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Sungwan Kim, Alexandra F DeJong Lempke, Kristin E Whitney et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine sex-specific lower limb strength, flexibility, and running biomechanics in adolescents with and without OSD. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of 100 adolescents (n=25 each group): females with OSD (age=14.6 ± 1.9 y; body mass index [BMI]=21.3 ± 2.1 kg/m2); males with OSD (age=14.4 ± 1.6 y; BMI=21.7 ± 3.2 kg/m2); females without OSD (age=14.8 ± 2.2 y; BMI=21.7 ± 3.0 kg/m2); and males without OSD (age=14.4 ± 2.2 y; BMI=22.0 ± 4.6 kg/m2). We assessed mass-normalized sagittal and frontal hip strength and sagittal knee strength via hand-held dynamometry, and quadriceps femoris (prone knee flexion) and hip flexor (Thomas test) flexibility. Limb crossover, contralateral pelvic drop [CPD], medial knee displacement, and tibial dominant stride were assessed during treadmill running. Group differences were analyzed using a two-way multivariate analysis of variance (continuous outcomes) and logistic regression (categorical outcomes), covarying for age and BMI. Analyses were performed using SPSS (alpha set at p<0.05). RESULTS: Compared with sex-matched healthy peers, females with OSD had impaired hip abduction strength and a greater propensity for CPD and medial knee displacement, though greater hip flexion strength (p≤0.03; Table). Males with OSD had greater hip and knee sagittal plane strength yet impaired flexibility (p≤0.02; Table). Compared with males with OSD, females with OSD had lower hip and knee strength, greater quadriceps femoris flexibility, and higher odds of frontal plane biomechanical deficits (p≤0.02; Table). CONCLUSION: We observed sex-specific differences in lower limb muscular and biomechanical features in adolescents with OSD, suggesting that clinicians should consider sex-specific rehabilitation strategies for adolescents with OSD.
