articles.title: Prolonged rod photoresponse and enhanced cone sensitivity in the transgenic mouse retina lacking arrestin and guanylate cyclase activating proteins.
articles.authors: Shinya Sato, Rikard Frederiksen, Alapakkam P Sampath et al.
articles.abstract: Light activates visual pigments and downstream G protein signalling cascades in rod and cone photoreceptor cells. Timely response inactivation requires visual pigment inactivation by arrestin and restoration of cellular cGMP by guanylate cyclase activating proteins (GCAPs). Using GCAP-deficient mice, we previously showed that apo-opsin produces photoresponse-like signals. To investigate the inactivation of apo-opsin by arrestin, we generated GCAP-deficient mice lacking arrestin (Gcaps-/-Arr1-/-). Using ex vivo electroretinography, we found that the dim flash responses of Gcaps-/-Arr1-/- rods were ∼100-fold slower than those of control Gcaps-/- rods. As a result, even brief dim light exposure during sample preparation resulted in prolonged rod saturation, so that only cone responses were initially observed in Gcaps-/-Arr1-/- retinas. In contrast, rod responses were observed immediately when Gcaps-/-Arr1-/- retinas were dissected under infrared light to avoid rod photoactivation. Microspectrophotometry showed that the rate of production and decay of the active rhodopsin photoproduct, Meta II, was comparable between Gcaps-/- and Gcaps-/-Arr1-/- rods. However, the rate of photoproduct Meta III decay was 3-fold slower in Gcaps-/-Arr1-/- rods, supporting a role for arrestin in accelerating the decay of photoactivated rhodopsin. To evaluate the effect of rod saturation on cone responses, we compared photopic cone responses from wild-type and Gnat1-/- retinas lacking rod signalling. Cone photoresponses were larger and more sensitive in wild-type retinas, suggesting the potentiation of cone function by the saturation of rod phototransduction. Together, our results demonstrate that the very slow deactivation of rod responses in Gcaps-/-Arr1-/- retinas might result in selective and potentiated cone signalling in darkness. KEY POINTS: Arrestin and guanylate cyclase activating proteins (GCAPs) play an important role in inactivation of the phototransduction cascade and termination of the light response in rod photoreceptors. The deletion of arrestin and GCAPs results in ∼100-fold slower dim flash responses in rods so that even brief dim light exposure produces saturation of the rods for tens of minutes. The decay of the rhodopsin photoactivated intermediate Meta III was slowed down 3-fold by the deletion of arrestin in Gcaps-/- rods, supporting a role for arrestin in accelerating the decay of photoactivated rhodopsin. Cone photoresponses were smaller and less sensitive in retinas lacking rod signalling, suggesting potentiation of cone function by the saturation of rod phototransduction. Together, these results demonstrate that the very slow deactivation of rod responses in arrestin- and GCAP-deficient retinas can result in selective and potentiated cone signalling in darkness.

articles.title: Pulsatile Perfusion Therapy Protects Internal Carotid Artery Blood Flow and Cerebrovascular Blood Oxygen Saturation with Simulated Hemorrhage in Humans.
articles.authors: Viet Q Dinh, K Austin Davis, Lindsey Peralez et al.
articles.abstract: Pulsatile Perfusion Therapy (PPT), a method we developed to induce 0.1 Hz hemodynamic oscillations (10-second cycles), protects blood oxygen saturation during ischemia. PPT via oscillatory lower body negative pressure (LBNP) protected cerebrovascular blood oxygen saturation (ScO2) during simulated hemorrhage in humans (induced via LBNP). Thigh cuff compressions are a new approach to achieve similar 0.1 Hz hemodynamic oscillations. We hypothesized that PPT via thigh cuff compressions would attenuate reductions in cerebral blood flow and cerebrovascular blood oxygen saturation during LBNP in humans. Fifteen healthy humans (6F/9M; age, 25.8 ± 4.5 y) completed two protocols of -60 mmHg LBNP. In the PPT condition, thigh cuffs intermittently inflated and deflated in 10-s cycles during the LBNP protocol. In the control condition (CON), the thigh cuffs remained deflated. Internal carotid artery (ICA) blood flow and ScO2 were measured continuously. PPT attenuated reductions in ICA blood flow (PPT: -17.6 ± 11.3% vs. CON: -31.0 ± 11.8%; P=0.02) and ScO2 (PPT: -5.2 ± 2.4% vs. CON: -7.1 ± 3.6%; P=0.07) compared to CON. These data provide evidence for PPT as a potential intervention for the treatment of cerebral hypoperfusion during hemorrhage.

articles.title: The Fibular Artery Communicating Branch and Fibular Artery Dominance: An Anatomical Hazard for Posterior Approaches to the Ankle.
articles.authors: Annabelle Johnston McCarter, Chijioke Orji, Craig Wyatt et al.
articles.abstract: Open reduction of posterior malleolar fractures (PMFs) increasingly employs direct posterior approaches. The posterolateral and posteromedial approaches both develop the deep posterior compartment in the plane between the fibular and posterior tibial arteries, placing the fibular artery communicating branch (FACB) within the operative field; inadvertent injury to this branch has been associated with limb-threatening ischemia. This study quantified the prevalence of the FACB and of fibular artery dominance (FAD), a configuration in which the fibular artery provides the principal distal supply because the posterior tibial artery is atretic or absent, and considered the implications for surgical approach selection. In a single-center cross-sectional study, 916 consecutive lower-limb computed tomography angiograms performed over 1 year were screened; 726 met the inclusion criteria and were assessed by trained reviewers for the FACB, FAD, laterality and clinical indication. An FACB was identified in 280 patients (38.6%, 95% CI 35.1-42.2). Its prevalence varied with clinical indication (χ2 = 33.67, p < 0.001), being highest in peripheral vascular disease (45.1%) and lowest in other vascular referrals (16.4%). FAD occurred exclusively in FACB-positive limbs, in 28 patients (10.0% of FACB-positive limbs; 3.9% of the whole cohort, 95% CI 2.7-5.5), and its distribution did not differ by indication (Freeman-Halton exact p = 0.81). Because the FACB lies within the field of the posterolateral and posteromedial approaches but posterior and lateral to the medial-posteromedial (MPM) approach, the MPM approach avoids the at-risk plane. These findings support anatomically informed approach selection and caution when a posterolateral or posteromedial approach is planned, particularly in patients with peripheral vascular disease.

articles.title: Making sense of touch: Spatial tactile cues promote efficient visuo-somatosensory integration and restore motor accuracy under sensory conflict.
articles.authors: Maria Evangelia Vlachou, Eva Lafaverges, Laurence Mouchnino et al.
articles.abstract: Effective interaction with complex environments relies on the integration of somatosensory and visual signals into coherent spatial representations of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, as during goal-directed hand movements under mirror-reversed visual feedback, motor performance deteriorates. Despite this conflict, the visual mapping between the hand and the environment remains preserved, and visual information typically facilitates motor performance, whereas tactile feedback impairs it. Here, we tested whether providing tactile input with explicit spatial structure renders visuo-somatosensory integration functionally relevant and stabilizes motor behaviour under sensory conflict. Healthy adults performed a mirror-tracing task, tracing a shape's contour with the index finger while tactile feedback conveyed either motion-related cues alone or additional discrete spatial landmarks aligned with the outline. Spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness relative to motion-related tactile input, indicating more effective online motor control. EEG source analyses further revealed that, when spatial tactile cues were present, somatosensory activity increased and functional connectivity was largely restricted to sensorimotor areas. In contrast, when tactile cues did not convey spatial information, sensory conflict was associated with widespread reductions in cortical activity, including in somatosensory and parietal areas, and with a diffuse functional connectivity pattern consistent with elevated sensorimotor uncertainty. Together, these findings indicate that providing spatial structure to tactile input can mitigate the detrimental effects of visuo-somatosensory conflict on motor performance and support more efficient integration of visual and somatosensory information during action. KEY POINTS: Accurate movements depend on combining visual and somatosensory information to estimate the position of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, motor performance usually deteriorates and tactile feedback can become disruptive. We tested whether tactile feedback becomes useful for movement control when it provides explicit spatial landmarks, rather than only motion-related information from finger-surface contact. During a tracing task under visuo-somatosensory conflict, spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness compared with when touch conveyed motion cues alone. Spatial tactile cues were associated with increased somatosensory cortical activity and a more spatially restricted pattern of functional coupling within sensorimotor networks, whereas their absence was associated with reduced somatosensory and parietal activity and a more distributed connectivity profile. Spatial structure in touch promotes multisensory integration, helping stabilize motor control under sensory conflict and highlighting how tactile cue design may improve sensorimotor function.

articles.title: Simultaneous acquisition of maternal and dual-fetal electrocardiography with maternal haemodynamic monitoring in anaesthetized pregnant rats.
articles.authors: Sarah Pribil Pardun, Spencer Duff, Payton Ward et al.
articles.abstract: Experimental approaches that acquire maternal haemodynamics together with direct cardiac signals from more than one fetus remain limited. We developed a standardized in vivo method for simultaneous acquisition of maternal ECG, maternal arterial blood pressure and ECGs from two fetuses in anaesthetized late-gestation Sprague-Dawley rats. The platform combines custom-fabricated needle electrodes with conventional cardiovascular instrumentation and PowerLab/LabChart acquisition. Stable, analysable maternal arterial blood pressure, maternal ECG and dual-fetal ECG were maintained for ≤5 h. The recordings supported beat-to-beat ECG interval and heart rate variability analyses. Fetuses had lower heart rates and longer R-R intervals than dams, and fetal root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), high-frequency power and standard deviation of RR intervals (SDRR) were lower than maternal values. As proof of recording responsiveness, maternal noradrenaline and verapamil administration produced readily resolved maternal haemodynamic changes together with time-aligned fetal heart rate responses. This protocol does not by itself demonstrate maternal-fetal cardiac coupling; rather, it provides synchronized high-resolution signals suitable for future analyses of dynamic maternal-fetal cardiovascular relationships and pharmacological responses.

articles.title: The Effects of Blueberry Consumption on Cerebral Blood Flow and Brain Glutathione Levels in Older Adults: A Double-Blind Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: In-Young Choi, Caitlin Payne, Phil Lee et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Age-related declines in brain antioxidant capacity and cerebral blood flow (CBF) contribute to cognitive decline and increase the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementias. Dietary approaches that enhance cerebral antioxidant defenses and CBF may promote brain health during aging. Blueberries are rich in polyphenols with antioxidant properties, and cardiometabolic and endothelial benefits, and may improve both brain glutathione (GSH), a major endogenous antioxidant, and CBF. However, the effects of blueberry intake on brain GSH and CBF have not been well established. OBJECTIVE: To determine the effects of blueberry consumption on brain GSH and CBF in brain regions vulnerable to aging and neurodegeneration in older adults. METHODS: In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, older adults aged 65-89 years with low berry intake (≤1 serving/week) consumed freeze-dried whole blueberry powder (hereafter "blueberry") equivalent to one cup of fresh blueberries or a matched placebo powder for three months. Brain GSH and regional CBF were measured using multiple quantum chemical shift imaging and pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling MRI, respectively. RESULTS: Sixty participants completed the intervention with adherence exceeding 92% in both groups. Blueberry powder consumption did not alter brain GSH concentrations compared with placebo but significantly increased CBF in the anterior cingulate cortex (P=0.03), a region involved in executive function and cognitive control. Within-group analyses showed increased CBF after blueberry consumption in the anterior cingulate cortex (7%, P=0.03; 95% confidence interval: 1.0%, 14.7%), caudate (7%, P=0.01; 2.9%, 15.8%), and putamen (6%, P=0.04; 0.3%, 13.9%), whereas no significant changes were observed in the placebo group. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with placebo, blueberry consumption increased CBF in the anterior cingulate cortex, a brain region relevant to age-related cognitive decline. No corresponding brain GSH changes were observed, suggesting that the effects of blueberry polyphenols are more consistent with vascular modulation than alterations in cerebral antioxidant status. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NUMBER: NCT05024916 CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05024916.

articles.title: An Empirical Snapshot of Local Nutrition Governance Capacity in the Rasuwa District of Nepal Before the Flood Surge of August 2026.
articles.authors: Patrick Webb, Robin Shrestha, Shibani Ghosh
articles.abstract: On August 26, 2026, flash floods swept through the Rasuwa district of Nepal, causing mass casualties and severe destruction. Research on disasters has led to valuable recommendations on how governments can be more attentive to warning signs and react more rapidly, and how tapping into local capacity and know-how can lead to more effective responses. However, in most crises not much is known about individual or institutional capacities that predated a shock or what resources donors and governments subsequently should bolster to support emergency responses and build resilience. In this Commentary, we draw on the self-reported data of civil servants and other local professionals tasked with implementing the national multisectoral nutrition strategy in Rasuwa. Data collection in 2024 predated the flood by roughly 2 years. The survey measured routine governance capacity, not disaster-response capacity specifically, and yet such data offer some insights into local capacity before the latest disaster and help our understanding of which elements were already under strain. The aim of this Commentary is not to report full survey findings but to highlight observations most relevant to the 2026 Rasuwa flood. Broadly, we suggest that routine governance research on nutrition and other technical topics of relevance can serve as a baseline for disaster recovery and that global calls for the localization of aid require much deeper understanding and measurement of local capacity to act.

articles.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Miguel Gomes, Mara Costa, Pedro Pezarat-Correia et al.
articles.abstract: Gomes, M, Costa, M, Pezarat-Correia, P, and Mendonca, GV. Lower-body strength and hypertrophy adaptations in response to concurrent training in trained young males. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined the interference effect of concurrent training (CT) on maximal and explosive strength and muscle morphology in trained young males. Thirty subjects were randomly assigned to endurance training (E), resistance training (R), or CT for 11 weeks. The intervention comprised 2 mesocycles: weeks 1-5 emphasizing maximal strength, and weeks 6-11 targeting explosive strength. Assessments were conducted at baseline, mid-training, and post-training, and included leg-press maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC), rate of force development (RFD), countermovement jump kinetics, and vastus lateralis cross-sectional area and pennation angle. Maximal voluntary isometric contraction increased only in the R group (18.4 ± 10.2%, p = 0.015). Peak RFD improved in both R (31.8 ± 23.2%) and CT (23.1 ± 27.9%), although with distinct time courses: R improved progressively across both mesocycles, whereas CT improved only during the second. Early-phase RFD (0-50 ms) increased in the R group from mid-training onward, whereas the CT group improved only from mid- to post-training (38.3 ± 40.4%, p = 0.021), accompanied by greater quadriceps electromyographic activity (p < 0.05). No changes in RFD were observed in E during training. Countermovement jump positive impulse improved in both R (12.7 ± 9.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 8.3%, p < 0.05), with no evidence of interference in jump-related explosive performance. Cross-sectional area increased in both R (17.0 ± 13.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 9.4%, p < 0.05). Pennation angle increased in CT (10.1 ± 12.9%) and R (18.6 ± 15.1%). These findings indicate that, although CT may limit MVIC development and delay early-phase RFD adaptations, it does not hinder explosive performance when resistance training is oriented toward rapid-strength development. Thus, CT can be effectively implemented in trained individuals when resistance training is periodized to emphasize neural-driven explosive or hypertrophy-related adaptations.

articles.title: Relationship between muscle pathology and tendon collagen organization in patients undergoing below-knee amputation.
articles.authors: Jennifer A Zellers, Sophia McSpedon, Jeremie L A Ferey et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Muscles and tendons are routinely studied in isolation, limiting our understanding of how treatments or pathologies in one component of the musculotendinous unit affect or co-occur in the other. The purpose of this cross-sectional study was to examine baseline relationships between muscle and tendon components. METHODS: Tendon and muscle specimens were obtained from individuals undergoing lower extremity amputation (age range: 37-65). Tensile mechanical testing with quantitative polarized light imaging quantified tendon mechanical properties and collagen alignment. Muscle biopsies obtained from the same muscle-tendon unit were assessed with histology (i.e. area fractions of extracellular matrix, intramuscular adipose tissue, neuropathy, and centrally nucleated fibers). Relationships in intramuscular/intratendinous lipid were assessed, and distributions of type I and III collagen tendon matrix components were evaluated. RESULTS: Statistically significant bivariate correlations were observed between muscle pathology (extracellular matrix, intramuscular adipose tissue, and neuropathy) and tendon collagen organization. Muscles with greater areas of pathology were connected to tendons with more aligned collagen. Muscle extracellular matrix and intramuscular adipose tissue explained the most variance in tendon collagen organization. There was no relationship between intramuscular and intratendinous lipid, and both lipid and collagen III were primarily within the intrafascicular and perivascular space within the tendon. CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to our hypothesis, muscle-tendon units with greater muscle pathology had tendons with more aligned collagen. These findings highlight the importance of assessing both tendon and muscle characteristics, as dysfunction in one component may not be shared with the other component.

articles.title: An observational study of food-related emotional expectancies, diet quality and comfort eating in the UK adult population.
articles.authors: Jenna R Cummings, Zoé Colombet, Emma Boyland
articles.abstract: According to expectancy theory, people eat food that they expect will bring positive emotions. The present research aimed to identify food and non-alcoholic beverages UK adults most expected to bring positive emotions; test influences of high fat, salt and/or sugar (HFSS) and branding on expectancies; and investigate associations of expectancies with diet quality and comfort eating (i.e. eating induced by negative emotions). A representative sample of UK adults (n 1203; Mage = 47 years; 52 % women; 87 % white) viewed food and non-alcoholic beverage images and completed the Anticipated Effects of Food Scale-Brief, a food frequency questionnaire, and questions about comfort eating and sociodemographic background. We ranked means of positive expectancies, conducted multilevel modelling to test influences of HFSS and branding on expectancies and examined correlations among expectancies, diet quality and comfort eating. Participants more strongly expected eating branded HFSS (e.g. Cadbury Twirl chocolate) v. generic non-HFSS (e.g. prawn curry) would result in positive emotions [b = 0·10, se = 0·04, p = ·02, 95 % CI (0·02, 0·18)]. Greater positive expectancies for HFSS - branded and generic - were associated with worse diet quality, especially positive expectancies for ice cream sundaes, fizzy drinks and chocolate (rs = -0·14 to -0·19, ps < ·001). Greater positive expectancies for HFSS and negative expectancies for HFSS and non-HFSS were associated with more frequent comfort eating (rs = 0·08 to 0·30, ps < ·05). Targeting positive HFSS expectancies through food environment policy and behavioural programmes may be a promising strategy for improving diet quality and reducing comfort eating in the UK adult population. Adults who comfort eat may also benefit from challenging negative expectancies for all foods.

articles.title: Duty factor is a more prominent modulator of external vertical loading than step frequency during running: a within-subject experimental study.
articles.authors: Aurélien Patoz, David Perrinjaquet, Johan Garcia et al.
articles.abstract: Peak vertical ground reaction force (Fv,max) and vertical average loading rate (VALR) are commonly used to characterize external vertical loading during running. Although increasing step frequency (SF) is frequently used to modify these measures, the observed effects may partly reflect concurrent changes in duty factor (DF). This study determined the independent effects of manipulating DF and SF on Fv,max and VALR during level treadmill running. Fifteen healthy runners completed a preferred-condition trial and eight randomized 5-min trials at 11 km/h. DF was manipulated by ± 16% and ± 8% while SF was maintained at its preferred value, and SF was manipulated by ± 12% and ± 6% while DF was controlled. Preferred DF was strongly and inversely associated with Fv,max (R2 = 0.81, p < 0.001) but not with VALR (R2 = 0.21, p = 0.09). Preferred SF was not associated with either loading measure (p ≥ 0.70). DF manipulation affected Fv,max and VALR (both p ≤ 0.001), whereas SF manipulation affected Fv,max (p < 0.001), driven by the - 12% condition, but not VALR (p = 0.11). Normalized within-participant slopes were more negative for DF than SF for Fv,max (-1.03 ± 0.20 vs 0.07 ± 0.20% per 1% relative change; p < 0.001) and VALR (-0.97 ± 0.94 vs 0.32 ± 1.11%; p = 0.02). During level treadmill running at the submaximal speed investigated, DF produced more consistent and quantitatively larger changes in external vertical loading than SF when the other temporal variable was controlled. These findings identify DF as a more prominent temporal determinant of external vertical loading than SF under the conditions investigated and demonstrate, at both the between- and within-subject levels, the importance of DF in modulating vertical loading.

articles.title: Transfemoral bone-anchored limbs alter joint-load-line offset during walking.
articles.authors: Brecca M M Gaffney, Dan W Milius, Danielle H Melton et al.
articles.abstract: Individuals with transfemoral amputation are at a heightened risk of musculoskeletal overuse injuries and reduced stability, largely due to altered joint biomechanics. The position of the ground reaction force (GRF) relative to hip and knee joints directly influences both joint biomechanics and dynamic stability and is influenced both by both movement patterns and prosthetic alignment. However, it is unknown if it is influenced by prosthetic suspension type. Our objective was to determine how the position of the GRF relative to hip and knee joint centers during walking differs between individuals with transfemoral amputation using either a socket prosthesis or bone-anchored limb (BAL). Motion capture data was collected from a convenience sample of 17 participants with unilateral transfemoral amputation during overground walking at two timepoints: before and 12-months following BAL implantation. The distances between the GRF line of action and the hip and knee joints in the sagittal and frontal planes were calculated and compared across timepoints (α = 0.05). The distance between the GRF and hip joint center was less medial (p < 0.001) on the amputated limb and more lateral (p < 0.001) on the intact limb during stance period when using a BAL compared to a socket prosthesis. Closer positioning of the GRF relative to the hip joint may reduce frontal plane compensatory strategies required for hip stabilization, potentially reflecting a biomechanical stable gait pattern when using a BAL.

articles.title: Smartphone assessment of postural sway and prospective falls in older adults: A large community-based study.
articles.authors: Patima Silsupadol, Suzanne R O'Brien, Sara Bautista et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Impaired postural control is a key risk factor for falls in older adults. However, laboratory-based postural sway assessments are costly and difficult to implement in real-world environments. Smartphones may offer a portable, low-cost, and easy-to-administer alternative for quantifying postural sway in large-scale community settings. RESEARCH QUESTION: Can a smartphone-embedded accelerometer quantify postural sway, distinguish retrospective fallers from non-fallers, and predict future falls over 12 months? METHODS: A total of 580 adults aged ≥ 55 years were assessed between 2023 and 2026. Fall history was collected, with prospective falls monitored over 12 months. Sway area and path length were measured using the Physiological Profile Assessment swaymeter during four standing conditions (eyes open/closed, firm/foam surfaces). Concurrently, smartphone-derived accelerometer data were used to compute acceleration trajectory area and path length. Pearson correlations, two-way ANOVA, and multivariable logistic regression examined relationships between instruments, group differences, and fall prediction. RESULTS: Smartphone-derived measures were strongly correlated with swaymeter outcomes for area (r = 0.713, p < 0.001) and path length (r = 0.803; p < 0.001). Both systems demonstrated significant group effects for sway area (p < 0.05), and smartphone-derived acceleration trajectory path length differed significantly between fallers and non-fallers (p = 0.036). Adding smartphone-derived acceleration trajectory path length to established risk factors increased Nagelkerke R² from 0.142 to 0.150, but the acceleration measure was not a significant predictor of future falls. SIGNIFICANCE: Smartphone-based accelerometry quantified postural sway and distinguished retrospective fallers from non-fallers but did not improve future fall prediction beyond established risk factors.

articles.title: The Relationship of Countermovement Jump Performance to Operational Readiness in United States Air Force Special Operators.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Sam T Tomlitz, Jay Dawes, Mark G Abel et al.
articles.abstract: Tomlitz, ST, Dawes, J, Abel, MG, and Potenza, MA. The relationship of countermovement jump performance to operational readiness in United States air force special operators. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Operational readiness signifies the degree to which special operations soldiers are physically capable of accomplishing occupational tasks. The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between selected countermovement jump (CMJ)-derived neuromuscular performance characteristics and operational readiness assessment scores among United States Air Force Pararescuemen (PJs). Thirty-six male PJs (age = 37.06 ± 5.98 years, height = 178.73 ± 6.27 cm, body mass (BM) = 86.51 ± 8.97 kg, body mass index = 27.06 ± 2.24 kg/m2) performed a series of tests, including a CMJ test and components of the tier II Operator Fitness Test (OFT). The CMJ-derived metrics (jump height, concentric impulse (CI), reactive strength modified, peak power (PP), PP/BM, concentric peak force, peak landing force, landing impulse, CI asymmetry, countermovement depth, eccentric PP/BM, force at zero velocity) were correlated with the tier II OFT events using bivariate Spearman's correlations. The significance level of this study was set at ≤ 0.05. A large relationship was found between standing long jump and reactive strength index modified (RSImod) (rs = 0.62, p = 0.012). Multiple power variables correlated with farmer's carry sprint performance, including CI (rs = -0.59, p = 0.038), RSImod (rs = -0.64, p = 0.007), PP (rs = -0.71, p < 0.001), and relative PP (PP/BM) (rs = -0.74, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that specific performance characteristics may serve as useful indicators of task performance in the OFT assessment.

articles.title: 3D development of the mouse pelvic girdle: Insights into the musculoskeletal system and vasculature.
articles.authors: Serena C Fernandopulle, Mark A Wright, Nina St Hillaire et al.
articles.abstract: The mouse (Mus musculus) pelvis features an elongated ilium and triangular pubis and ischium characteristic of a small quadruped, whereas humans possess a short, broad, bowl-shaped pelvis specialized for bipedal locomotion and childbirth. Mice are widely used to model osteoporosis, hip dysplasia, and other pelvic pathologies, yet in utero mouse pelvic development has been incompletely characterized, limiting cross-species interpretation. Here, we integrate 3D micro-CT and histology to generate a comprehensive atlas of mouse pelvic development from embryonic days 12.5-18.5 (E12.5-E18.5), focusing on the ilium, hip joint, and sacroiliac joint. We show that E14.5 is a critical stage, when the hip and sacroiliac joints form. We identify a sequential developmental program in mice in which joint cartilage forms first, followed by muscle-cartilage interaction, and, subsequently, extensive blood vessel growth. In contrast to the transversely oriented, developmentally delayed iliac growth and ossification described in recent studies of the human bipedal pelvis, the mouse ilium follows an earlier, centrally initiated, longitudinal ossification pattern. Overall, our atlas provides an essential quadrupedal reference for interpreting human pelvic development, evolution, and disease models.

articles.title: The Curious History of the External Petrosal Nerve: Did Citations Replace Observations?
articles.authors: Joel A Vilensky, James J Brokaw, Carlos A Suárez-Quian et al.
articles.abstract: Anatomical knowledge is founded on repeated observation, independent verification, and transmission through authoritative texts. Although this process typically strengthens scientific understanding, transmission through textbooks may occasionally perpetuate observations that have not undergone sustained empirical confirmation. The external petrosal nerve (EPN) provides an unusually well-documented historical example of this phenomenon. Primary and secondary sources pertaining to the EPN published between 1834 and 2026, including original German and Latin sources, were critically examined. Historical accounts were compared with modern anatomical, embryological, histological, and microsurgical investigations of the facial nerve and middle cranial fossa. The modern concept of the EPN can be traced directly to Friedrich Bidder's original description published in 1836. Although several of Bidder's contemporaries questioned his interpretation, the structure continued to be described in anatomical textbooks and review articles for nearly two centuries, including recent editions of Gray's Anatomy. In contrast, none of the anatomical atlases we searched, and none of the twentieth- or twenty-first-century anatomical investigations reviewed, provided firm independent evidence supporting the EPN as a distinct anatomical structure. The historical record suggests that acceptance of the EPN resulted primarily from repeated citation rather than independent anatomical verification. Beyond reassessing the anatomical status of the EPN, this study illustrates how scientific authority may accumulate through successive secondary sources despite limited primary evidence. The EPN provides an instructive case study in evidence-based anatomy and highlights the importance of periodically re-examining accepted anatomical observations.

articles.title: Teleanatomy: A Conceptual Framework for Anatomy Across Distance.
articles.authors: Joe Iwanaga, R Shane Tubbs
articles.abstract: For centuries, anatomy has been fundamentally grounded in physical proximity. Anatomical knowledge has traditionally been acquired through direct observation of the human body by dissection, surgery, physical examination, and medical imaging. Advances in imaging, three-dimensional modeling, telecommunication, robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and extended reality have transformed how anatomical information is acquired and applied. Although remote anatomical practices already exist in education, imaging, consultation, and surgery, no unified anatomy-specific framework describes how structural information is acquired, represented, transmitted, interpreted, and applied when the anatomical source and the observer or user are spatially separated. We propose teleanatomy as a framework for this distributed setting. Five foundational pillars are identified: acquisition, representation, transmission, interpretation, and application, and three cross-cutting properties, fidelity, provenance, and latency, are proposed as determinants of whether anatomical information remains reliable and fit for purpose. Teleanatomy is not intended to replace digital anatomy, telemedicine, radiologic anatomy, or surgical robotics, but to define the anatomical layer shared by these increasingly remote practices.

articles.title: Turkish Research Dietitians Prioritize Strengthening Traditional Methods Before Digital Transition: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Merve Guney-Coskun, Michelle Weech, Rosalind Fallaize et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dietary assessment underpins nutrition research and practice. Food Frequency Questionnaires (FFQs) are used in epidemiology yet have limitations. Digital technologies are reshaping dietary assessment, with potential to improve scalability and standardization. Understanding how dietitians appraise traditional and emerging approaches is critical for guiding context-appropriate innovation. OBJECTIVE: This study explored research-focused Turkish dietitians' perspectives on (i) the strengths and limitations of FFQs, (ii) opportunities and barriers in transitioning to web-based FFQs, and (iii) the potential and challenges of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and biosensors, in dietary assessment, with Türkiye-specific considerations where relevant. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten PhD-qualified, research-focused dietitians in Türkiye, purposively sampled for dietary assessment expertise. Interviews were conducted online, transcribed, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Sample size was guided by thematic saturation; recruitment continued until no substantively new themes emerged across successive interviews. RESULTS: Participants valued FFQs as scalable tools for capturing habitual intake but noted limits in person-level detail, portion accuracy, and recall reliability. Culturally adapted food lists and portion imagery were perceived as priorities to improve validity. Web-based FFQs were viewed as a credible evolution offering efficiency and visual supports, though concerns centered on digital literacy, device access, and user guidance. Emerging tools such as AI-assisted image capture and wearable biosensors were considered promising for reducing memory bias and improving objectivity, but adoption was tempered by concerns over cost, usability, cultural fit, privacy, and governance. CONCLUSIONS: The perspectives of the Turkish research-focused dietitians interviewed in this study point to a staged pathway for innovation: first to strengthen FFQ content with cultural adaptation and visual supports; then digitize with safeguards for accessibility and data integrity; and finally pilot advanced technologies cautiously, under robust validation and ethical oversight. This phased approach could offer an acceptable pathway to modernizing dietary assessment while safeguarding credibility and equity.

articles.title: Vitamin D and the treatment of iron deficiency anemia.
articles.authors: Stephen R Hennigar, Manju B Reddy

articles.title: Absorption and Metabolism of Steroidal Alkaloids from Tomato Juice in Healthy Adults: a Pharmacokinetic Study.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Daniel Do, Maria J Sholola, Jessica L Cooperstone
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Steroidal alkaloids may be responsible for some of the health benefits of a tomato rich diet, but little is known about their metabolic fate after consumption. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to elucidate the pharmacokinetic parameters of plasma steroidal alkaloids and to define their bioavailability and metabolism following a single tomato containing meal. METHODS: Healthy subjects (n = 11, 6M/5F) consumed 505 g of tomato juice following a two-week tomato washout and blood plasma were collected post-prandially at 11 time points over 12-hours. Plasma steroidal alkaloids were analyzed using ultra-high performance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. The pharmacokinetic parameters AUC0-12hr, Cmax, and Tmax were calculated using non-compartmental analysis. The quantity of steroidal alkaloids and their metabolites present in plasma were used to calculate a a fractional systemic exposure. Metabolite standards were "bio"-synthesized using the liver microsomes to improve confidence in identification when authentic standards were not available. RESULTS: The fraction of steroidal alkaloids from juice that appeared in plasma intact or as metabolized products was 9.7% ± 5.7% with a range of 2.4-17.9%. Over 99% of steroidal alkaloids present in circulation were metabolized products. The Cmax of total plasma steroidal alkaloids in subjects reached an average 406.5 nmol/L and ranged from 103.7-1145.6 nmol/L. Mean Tmax was 8.9 h (range 6-12 h) and average AUC0-12hr was 2529.0 ± 1644.8 nmol*h/L. Steroidal alkaloids remained above baseline at12 hours so absorption is likely underestimated. Liver S9 enzymatic synthesis of steroidal alkaloid metabolites including trihydroxy-tomatidine and sulfonated dihydroxy-tomatidine improved confidence in compound identification. CONCLUSIONS: This study reports the first pharmacokinetic data for tomato steroidal alkaloids, demonstrating moderate absorption and extensive metabolism after tomato juice consumption. These data provide context for future studies investigating the potential role that these compounds may play in human health. Clinical Trial Registry number and website where it was obtained https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01696773.

articles.title: Effects of acetaminophen ingestion on the torque-duration relationship and fatigability during intermittent exercise in patients with type 1 diabetes.
articles.authors: Nadia Fekih, Amal Machfer, Achraf Ammar et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the effects of acute ingestion of acetaminophen (ACT) on the magnitude of exercise-induced peripheral fatigue (ΔPtw) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D). In a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind design, 22 males (11 T1D and 11 control (CTR) completed 60 maximum voluntary contractions 60 min after ingesting 1 g of acetaminophen (ACT) or 1 g of placebo (PL) on two separate visits. Central and peripheral fatigue were assessed from pre- to post-exercise changes in quadriceps voluntary activation (ΔVA) and potentiated twitch force (ΔPtw), respectively. Critical torque (CT) was defined as the mean force produced during the final 12 contractions, and work performed (W') was computed as the impulse performed above CT. Maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), VA and Ptw decreased after exercise in both groups, with no significant difference between PL and ACT condition. Compared to PL, ACT increased root mean square/Mmax and CT values in the T1D (+21% and 8% respectively) and CTR groups (+40% and +19%; respectively), with significant lower effect in the T1D compared to the CTR group (P < 0.05). No significant effect of ACT was observed for W' in the T1D (+7%) and CTR groups (+4%) (P = 0.68). These findings indicate that acute ACT ingestion increased CT and muscle activation during the repeated-MVC protocol in both groups, although the magnitude of these responses was smaller in the T1D than the CTR group.

articles.title: Physical activity partly inhibits autonomic imbalance, immune dysfunction and quality of life induced by chronic shiftwork in policemen.
articles.authors: Hélida C Aquino-Santos, Jeanne S Tavares-Vasconcelos, Anamei Silva-Reis et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic shiftwork can impair autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune homeostasis. However, the interaction between occupational status and physical activity level in military police officers remains incompletely understood. This cross-sectional factorial study included 102 men stratified according to occupational status and physical activity level: physically active military police officers (PMP; n = 26), physically inactive military police officers (PMNP; n = 26), physically active civilians (CVP; n = 25) and physically inactive civilians (CVNP; n = 25). Quality of life, perceived stress, sleepiness, haematological parameters, cytokines and heart rate variability were assessed. Physical activity improved several Short-form questionnaire (SF-36) domains, particularly Physical Functioning and General Health. Military police officers demonstrated lower mean normal-to-normal intervals and lower high-frequency power than civilians, indicating differences in resting autonomic cardiovascular modulation associated with occupational status. Serum interleukin-10 concentrations were significantly lower in military police officers, whereas interleukin-2, interleukin-17 and interferon-γ did not differ significantly according to occupational status. Haemoglobin levels and platelet counts demonstrated significant occupational status × physical activity interactions. Perceived stress scores were lower in military police officers than in civilians. Chronic occupational exposure to shiftwork was associated with altered autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune regulation in military police officers. Regular physical activity improved quality of life somewhat; however, several physiological alterations remained predominantly associated with occupational status, reinforcing the importance of occupational strategies targeting circadian health and physiological resilience. These findings highlight the physiological complexity of chronic shiftwork exposure in tactical occupational populations.

articles.title: Effects of In-Season Contrast Strength Training on Jump Performance and Sprint Ability in Female Field Hockey Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Ramiro Chilingirian-Padrón, Tania Álvarez-Yates, Oscar García-García
articles.abstract: Chilingirian-Padrón, R, Álvarez-Yates, T, and García-García, O. Effects of in-season contrast strength training on jump performance and sprint ability in female field hockey players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 6-week in-season contrast strength training program incorporating sport-specific tasks on neuromuscular performance in sub-elite female field hockey players. Twenty-five athletes completed a pre-post single-cohort intervention integrated into their regular team schedule. Each session consisted of 3 sequential blocks: (a) a high-load strength exercise targeting maximal strength or hypertrophy (70-85% 1 repetition maximum [1RM]); (b) a biomechanically related explosive action performed at low load (∼30% 1RM) and high execution velocity; and (c) a high-speed sport-specific task. Jump performance was assessed using bilateral and unilateral countermovement jumps (CMJs) and free arm CMJ, whereas sprint ability was evaluated through 10- and 20-m sprints. A mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to determine the effects of the intervention, with Time (Pre, Post) as within-subject factor and Playing Position (defenders, midfielders, forwards) as between-subject factor, with the level of significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Significant improvements were observed in all jump and sprint assessments: jump performance increased by 5.7-29.6%, whereas sprint ability improved by 1.6-1.9%. These findings indicate that 6 weeks of contrast strength training incorporating high-speed sports-specific tasks performed during the competitive season elicited meaningful improvements in stretch-shortening cycle-related jump performance and sprint ability in sub-elite female field hockey players.

articles.title: Maximum Deceleration Is Related to Players' Ability to Repeat High-Intensity Decelerations in a Match in Female Professional Soccer Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: David Martínez-Hernández, Paul A Jones, José M Oliva-Lozano et al.
articles.abstract: Martínez-Hernández, D, Jones, PA, Oliva-Lozano, JM, and Harper, DJ. Maximum deceleration is related to players' ability to repeat high-intensity decelerations in a match in female professional soccer players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was twofold; First, to investigate positional differences in high-intensity decelerations (HID; < -3 m·s-2) and very high-intensity decelerations (VHID; < -4 m·s-2) in elite female soccer players. Second, to examine relationships between maximum deceleration (DMax) and the frequency of HID and VHID throughout competitive match play, reflecting players' capacity to perform these actions repeatedly. Twenty-four professional female outfield players (189 match files) from an English Women's Superleague club were tracked across 27 matches using 10-Hz Global Positioning System devices. Differences in deceleration metrics (DMax, HID, VHID) across positions were analyzed using 1-way analysis of variance and Bonferroni post hoc tests. Pearson's correlations assessed relationships between DMax, HID, and VHID across playing positions. Significant positional differences were observed. Central defenders had the lowest DMax and performed fewer HID and VHID actions than other positions, whereas central midfielder recorded the highest HID values. Maximum deceleration showed moderate-to-large correlations with HID (r = 0.35) and VHID (r = 0.52). Positional and individual variations influenced the strength of these relationships. This study provides novel evidence that maximal deceleration capacity is an important neuromuscular performance quality that distinguishes playing positions in elite women's soccer, with moderate-to-large associations with the ability to perform repeated HID and VHID supporting its relevance to match performance, particularly at higher intensities. These findings suggest that DMax may be an important quality to target through training, with potential implications for repeated deceleration performance. Practitioners should implement position-specific assessments and interventions to optimize deceleration capacity, especially as modern game demands continue to evolve.

articles.title: Comparison Between Concentric-Only and Eccentric-Concentric Load-Velocity Relationships and its Derived Parameters in the Jump Squat and Bench Press Throw Exercises.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Jose L Hernandez-Davo, Rafael Sabido, Pablo Asencio et al.
articles.abstract: Hernandez-Davo, JL, Sabido, R, Asencio, P, and Boullosa, D. Comparison between concentric-only and eccentric-concentric load-velocity relationships and its derived parameters in the jump squat and bench press throw exercises. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to analyze 2 different load-velocity (L-V) assessment protocols (concentric-only [CON] vs. maximal intended eccentric velocity [MAX]) on the L-V relationship in jump-squat (JS) and bench press throw (BPT) exercises, 18 men performed the L-V relationship assessments with loads representing 20, 40, 60, and 80% of one repetition maximum (1RM) on 2 different days. Reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and coefficient of variation (CV%). The mean propulsive velocity (MPV) was used to establish individual L-V profiles, their derived parameters (L0 and V0), and estimated 1RM values in back-squat and bench press exercises. Maximal intended eccentric velocity condition showed high reliability (ICC: 0.70-0.87: CV: 4.2-11.2%), whereas CON condition showed moderate-to-high scores (ICC: 0.61-0.86; CV: 4.8-10.4%). The mean propulsive velocity values were significantly higher in the MAX condition at all loads in the JS (8.9-10.9%) and at all loads except the 20% 1RM in the BPT exercise (6.1-23.3%). When using the MAX condition, L0 values were higher in the BPT exercise (5%), and V0 was greater in both the JS (9.0%) and BPT exercises (3.4%). The estimated 1RM value was higher in the MAX condition for both the squat (124.1 vs. 117.8 kg) and the bench press exercises (89.2 vs. 83.9 kg). High-velocity eccentric actions led to significantly higher MPV values, without compromising reliability values. The L-V profile and their derived parameters are substantially affected by eccentric velocity instructions. Standardized protocols using maximal eccentric velocities are suitable to assess athletes' maximal neuromuscular performances with reliable L-V profiles, which may complement the information obtained through the habitual CON protocol.

articles.title: A dive into the physiological responses to O2- and CO2-tables in freedivers.
articles.authors: Louise Declercq, Sander Lefere, Kasper Van Eetvelde et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Current literature focuses on maximal apneas to improve apnea duration, whereas in practice, apnea training often involves two distinct forms of timed-repeated submaximal apnea protocols: "O2-tables", intended to progressively decrease oxygenation and purportedly train O2 conservation, and "CO2-tables", intended to progressively accumulate carbon dioxide (CO2) and purportedly train hypercapnia tolerance. In apnea novices, O2- and CO2-tables failed to induce strong deoxygenation and CO2 accumulation, respectively. Therefore, the aim of this study was to compare physiological responses to maximal apneas, O2- and CO2-tables in apnea trained individuals. METHODS: After medical screening, fourteen freedivers performed three apnea protocols: maximal apneas, O2-table and CO2-table. During apnea, heart rate (HR), muscle tissue oxygenation index (mTOI) and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) were measured continuously. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) was measured before and after apneas. Capillary partial pressure of CO2 (PCO2) was measured after the fourth and final apnea. Perceived Exertion (RPE) was rated after each protocol. RESULTS: RPE was lower after O2- and CO2-tables than after maximal apneas. Changes in HR and mTOI did not differ between O2- and CO2-tables. CO2-tables elicited greater increases in PCO2 and EtCO2 compared to O2-tables and maximal apneas. Maximal apneas induced greater changes in SpO2 than O2- and CO2-tables. CONCLUSION: These results suggest that, in freedivers, O2- and CO2-tables offer a less mentally and physically demanding alternative to repeated maximal apneas, allowing greater variation in apnea training while still targeting O2 conservation and CO2 tolerance, respectively.

articles.title: A Supplement Dose Is Not a Nutrient Requirement: When the Same Units Answer Different Questions.
articles.authors: Takuya Omura
articles.abstract: Clinical nutrition guidelines often contain numbers that look directly comparable but answer different questions. A supplement dose, a therapeutic total-intake target, and a population reference intake can all be expressed in grams of the same nutrient, yet they do not represent the same quantity. The risk is not that one number is wrong; it is that the wrong inference is drawn from a number that is right. Using the Nutritional Management Guidelines for Sarcopenia and Frailty 2025 as a current illustration, this commentary distinguishes 3 inferential layers: an implementation regimen, a therapeutic nutrition target, and a dietary reference value. The guideline suggests approximately 20-25 g/day of high-quality protein supplementation with exercise when intake is insufficient, while acknowledging that a recommended total daily protein intake for older people with sarcopenia or frailty cannot yet be specified. These statements are compatible, not contradictory. Moving from a tested regimen to a therapeutic total-intake target requires additional evidence on baseline intake, amount consumed, achieved exposure, comparator exposure, co-interventions, modifiers, and safety. Moving further to a dietary reference value requires a broader evidentiary scope focused on usual intake, intake-response relationships, safety, and population applicability. Guidance should therefore state what each number represents and what additional evidence is required before that number is transferred to a different inferential layer.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Probiotics, Prebiotics, and Synbiotics for Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Shiyu Zhang, Yushun Yan, Min Wang et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by impaired social interaction, communication deficits, and repetitive behaviors. Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota may be a potential therapeutic target. However, the relative efficacy of single-strain probiotics, multistrain probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: This network meta-analysis aims to systematically compare the effectiveness of these microbiota-targeted interventions on ASD symptoms. DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted up to June 20, 2025. DATA EXTRACTION: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing single-strain probiotics, multistrain probiotics, prebiotics, or synbiotics in individuals with ASD were included. The primary outcome was the improvement in deficits in core ASD symptoms, such as social communication and interaction and restricted and repetitive behaviors, which were assessed using standardized tools. DATA ANALYSIS: A Bayesian network meta-analysis with random-effects modeling was performed. Seventeen RCTs involving 904 participants were included. Synbiotics showed greater efficacy in improving ASD symptoms compared with placebo (standardized mean difference [SMD]: -1.90; 95% credible interval [CrI]: -2.66 to -1.06), prebiotics (SMD: -2.23; 95% CrI: -3.10 to -1.06), multistrain probiotics (SMD: -1.59; 95% CrI: -2.41 to -0.68), and single-strain probiotics (SMD: -1.52; 95% CrI: -2.40 to -0.60). The sensitivity analyses were generally consistent with the primary findings. CONCLUSION: Synbiotics appeared to demonstrate greater efficacy than probiotics, prebiotics, and placebo in improving behavioral symptoms of ASD. However, given the limited available evidence and modest sample sizes, this finding should be interpreted cautiously and considered preliminary. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. CRD420251078170.

articles.title: Plant Polyphenol-Polysaccharide Complexes for Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Molecular Interactions, Nano-Delivery Design, and Translational Evidence.
articles.authors: Jianhua Mu, Fengling Ma, Xue Zheng et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Plant polyphenol-polysaccharide complexes (PPCs) combine polyphenol bioactivity with the protective, mucoadhesive, and microbiota-accessible properties of polysaccharides. However, the literature often groups chemically distinct polyphenols together, extrapolates structure-function relationships across nonequivalent carriers, and interprets concurrent microbiota or short-chain fatty acid changes as causal mechanisms. OBJECTIVE: This review critically evaluated how molecular interactions and measurable structural attributes of PPCs influence gastrointestinal stability, colon-oriented release, biological effects relevant to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and translational readiness. DATA SOURCES: Targeted searches of PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were completed through July 20, 2026. Peer-reviewed original studies and relevant reviews published in English were considered. DATA EXTRACTION: Evidence was classified as direct PPC evidence, PPC-relevant formulation evidence, or non-PPC mechanistic and engineering evidence. Information on carrier chemistry, payload, structural attributes, release behavior, biological outcomes, and translational considerations was extracted. DATA ANALYSIS: Quantitative findings were compared only when carrier chemistry, payload, test conditions, and outcomes were sufficiently aligned; heterogeneous data were not pooled. Non-covalent assembly and covalent conjugation can alter molecular organization, physicochemical stability, and release, but no universal relationship between degree of substitution and release is supported. Epigallocatechin-3-gallate, quercetin, and anthocyanins require compound-specific carrier selection. PPC and PPC-relevant interventions are associated with changes in NF-κB-related signaling, epithelial-barrier markers, microbiota composition, and individual short-chain fatty acids, whereas receptor- or microbiota-mediated causality remains largely unverified. Responsive platforms also differ in stability, release control, scale-up burden, and clinical readiness. CONCLUSIONS: PPC-based nano-delivery is a promising preclinical approach, but translation requires matched studies linking structure, properties, and release, mediator-level mechanistic validation, standardized characterization, reproducible manufacturing, formulation-specific safety assessment, and comparison with established IBD therapies.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Food Swap Interventions Used in Grocery Store Settings.
articles.authors: Helena Bentil, Edward Hillier, Oliver Huse et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Food swap interventions provide an approach to influence consumer food choices. However, evidence on their design and effectiveness has not yet been synthesized. OBJECTIVE: This review systematically synthesized the literature on food swap interventions in grocery settings by addressing the following questions: (1) What were the key characteristics of the food swap interventions examined in the literature, and what was their intended purpose? (2) Have food swap interventions been effective in changing behavior? DATA SOURCES, EXTRACTION, AND ANALYSIS: A search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science up to January 23, 2025, was conducted to identify food swap intervention trials in grocery settings, with no limits on language or publication year. Covidence was used to screen titles, abstracts, and full-text articles in duplicate. Data were synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Eleven studies, published during 2006-2024, were included in the review. One intervention was implemented in a real grocery store, 3 in real online supermarkets, and 7 in simulated online supermarkets. Most included studies targeted adults with primary or partial responsibility for their household grocery shopping. All the swaps offered healthier alternatives to selected products. Outcomes examined included shopping basket item healthiness, energy content, saturated fatty acid (SFA) content, salt density, and sodium and sugar content. All but 1 study noted evidence that the studied interventions can change behavior. Two studies found significant improvements in overall nutritional quality. Salt/sodium reductions were seen in 2 studies, while reductions in sugar content were seen in 1 study but not in another study. Studies also demonstrated significant reductions in purchased energy content/density, and SFA. CONCLUSION: A range of food swap interventions have been studied, and most of those identified have been found to be effective in improving the healthiness of food purchases. No studies explored the potential of swap interventions to promote sustainable food choices, which could be a topic of future research. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. [CRD42024539803].

articles.title: Intercellular communication networks in the osteoporotic bone microenvironment.
articles.authors: Yihan Li, Xiaofeng Liu, Xinyu Feng et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Osteoporosis is essentially a persistent imbalance between bone resorption and bone formation in the bone microenvironment. Its development is not driven by abnormalities in a single cell type, but is closely linked to dysregulated communication among bone cells, marrow stromal cells, immune cells, and vascular cells, together with altered extracellular matrix (ECM) signaling. Existing studies have mainly focused on individual cell types or single signaling pathways, and systematic integration of evidence on osteoporosis from the perspective of intercellular communication and extracellular matrix signaling is still limited. This review organizes representative pathological evidence into three categories based on the main modes of signal transmission: paracrine and autocrine communication, direct cell-cell communication, and ECM-cell communication. REVIEW FINDINGS: Across these categories, this review highlights communication axes in which source cells, key signals, recipient cells, and bone remodeling outcomes can be linked into relatively clear mechanistic chains. It also considers differences in the strength and completeness of evidence across these axes. CONCLUSION: Integrating these pathological changes may clarify how dysregulated intercellular communication and ECM signaling jointly contribute to bone remodeling imbalance in osteoporosis, thereby helping to identify potential targets for intervention.

articles.title: Intense unimanual contractions increase muscle excitation and local metabolic activity in the resting contralateral forearm.
articles.authors: Lee J Hinkle, Britton C Scheuermann, Carl J Ade et al.
articles.abstract: Intense unilateral muscle contractions evoke measurable activity within the contralateral neuroaxis, which can be detected with surface electromyographic activity in the resting homologous muscle. Physiological mirror activity (PMA), the unintentional increase in contralateral muscle excitation, has been implicated in cross-limb interactions and adaptations. Despite longstanding observations of PMA, it remains unknown whether this low-level muscle excitation influences local muscle metabolism. We addressed this question using a vascular occlusion test in 10 healthy adults. Surface electromyography and near-infrared spectroscopy-derived measures of tissue oxygen saturation and muscle oxygen consumption ( m V . O 2 ) were obtained from the resting left forearm during vascular occlusion at rest and during fatiguing unimanual contractions. PMA in the contralateral resting arm was greater during fatiguing unimanual contractions than during rest (mean difference: 8.9%, 95% CI: 4.1 to 13.8). This increase was accompanied by a steeper rate of tissue oxygen desaturation (mean difference: -0.132% s- 1, 95% CI: -0.227 to -0.037) and greater m V . O 2 (mean difference: 0.188 mL O2 min- 1 100 g- 1, 95% CI: 0.057 to 0.320). Greater PMA was associated with both a faster rate of oxygen desaturation (r = -0.85, 95% CI: -0.96 to -0.46) and greater m V . O 2 (r = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.28 to 0.94). These findings provide the first evidence that PMA is accompanied by increased local metabolic demand, consistent with a coupling between unintentional muscle excitation and oxygen extraction in the resting limb.

articles.title: Pre-season friendly match-play as a double-edged sword: Performance gains and inflammatory cost in semi-professional soccer players (a natural experiment).
articles.authors: Dimitrios I Bourdas, Eleftherios Mylonis, Natalia Kompodieta et al.
articles.abstract: Pre-season training prepares soccer players for competition, but the longitudinal effects of friendly match exposure remain unclear. We investigated whether cumulative late pre-season match-play is associated with physiological adaptation in semi-professional players. Twenty-four male players from a randomly selected semi-professional team competing at national level were assessed at pre-season start, mid-pre-season and pre-competition. Measurements included body composition, physical performance, aerobic fitness and blood markers reflecting muscle damage, inflammation, hormonal status and haematological adaptation. Based on cumulative playing time across eight friendly matches, as determined by coaching staff, players were classified retrospectively into extended play (EP) or limited play (LP) groups. Controlling for mid-pre-season baseline, the EP group showed significantly lower pre-competition values for body mass ( η p 2 = 0.276), body fat ( η p 2 = 0.294) and 35 m sprint time ( η p 2 = 0.129) and higher values for lower-limb power (dominant/non-dominant; η p 2 = 0.219-0.424), velocity at maximal oxygen uptake ( η p 2 = 0.441) and at second ventilatory threshold ( η p 2 = 0.708), serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase ( η p 2 = 0.296), myoglobin ( η p 2 = 0.199), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ( η p 2 = 0.920), interleukin-6 ( η p 2 = 0.893), tumour necrosis factor-α ( η p 2 = 0.937) and red blood cell count ( η p 2 = 0.190) (all P ≤ 0.038). Across all participants, total match-play time was correlated significantly with reductions in body fat (r = -0.47) and increases in lower-limb power (r = 0.44-0.67), second ventilatory threshold (r = 0.55) and inflammatory markers (r = 0.79-0.86) (all P ≤ 0.033). Greater friendly match-play exposure during pre-season was associated with favourable physiological adaptations and a more pronounced physiological and inflammatory response. These findings support friendly match-play as a meaningful physiological stimulus and highlight the importance of balancing match exposure with recovery during pre-season preparation.

articles.title: Validation of the GERY Protein Intake Screening Test among community-dwelling oldest-olds in Finland.
articles.authors: Riikka T Niskanen, Aava Ranta, Heli Salmenius-Suominen et al.
articles.abstract: Protein intake is often suboptimal among older adults, which may lead to protein-energy malnutrition, sarcopenia and frailty. A need exists for a simple, efficient and feasible protein-specific dietary assessment tool. Thus, a novel protein screening test, adapted to the Finnish cultural context, was developed. The aim of this study was to validate a novel protein screening test against a 1-d food record among Finnish older adults. Data were collected as part of the Helsinki Aging Study. The sample (N 140) consisted of Finnish community-dwelling oldest-old individuals (age range 80-100 years) with sufficient cognitive ability for at-home dietary assessment. A 1-d food record and the protein screening test were completed on one habitual eating day. Validity was assessed using the food record as a reference, with suboptimal protein intake defined as <1·2 g/kg BW/d. A Bland-Altman plot and concordance correlation coefficient (0·87, 95 % CI: 0·83-0·91) demonstrated good agreement between the methods. Sensitivity (0·85, 95 % CI: 0·72-0·94), specificity (0·81, 95 % CI: 0·71-0·88), area under receiver operating characteristic curve (0·90, 95 % CI: 0·85-0·95) and positive likelihood ratio (4·40, 95 % CI: 2·86-6·77) indicated strong diagnostic performance of the protein screening test. An optimal cut-off for the screening test to identify suboptimal protein intake was assessed at <1·00 g/kg BW/d. The novel protein screening test has good concurrent validity with the food record in identifying Finnish community-dwelling oldest-olds with suboptimal protein intake. It shows diagnostic potential for identifying individuals with suboptimal intake and to engage in targeted intervention.

articles.title: Dietary Inflammatory Index and cardiorespiratory fitness among older adults living in the community: a cross-sectional analysis.
articles.authors: Bi-Xia Huang, Zi-Hui Huang, Si Chen et al.
articles.abstract: The optimal dietary recommendation for healthy ageing remains unclear. This study examined the association between the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) in Chinese community-dwelling older adults. Data were drawn from the Guangzhou Nutrition and Health Study's 3rd and 4th follow-up visits (2017-2021). DII was calculated from a Seventy nine-item validated FFQ, and CRF was assessed on a cycle ergometer using a submaximal constant work rate protocol. VO2max was estimated via the Åstrand-Ryhming Nomogram with age correction, and relative intensity was expressed as percentage of predicted maximal heart rate (%HRmax). Favourable CRF was defined as sex-specific VO2max in the top quartile or %HRmax < 85 %. Among 906 participants (615 women, 291 men; mean age 65·9 ± 5·4 years), those in the lowest DII tertile (anti-inflammatory diet) had higher VO2max than those in the highest tertile (P-trend = 0·048) and greater odds of favourable CRF (OR 1·81, 95 % CI 1·22-2·70), while no significant associations were observed for %HRmax (P-trend = 0·356; OR 1·31, 95 % CI 0·94-1·84). Associations between lower DII and higher VO2max were stronger among physically active participants (P-interaction = 0·049). Compared with consistently high DII, both transition to a low-inflammatory diet (OR 3·01, 95 % CI 1·20-7·51) and persistent adherence to such a diet (OR 2·49, 95 % CI 1·28-4·87) were associated with favourable CRF. These findings suggest that an anti-inflammatory diet is associated with better CRF in older adults, with potential synergistic benefits from physical activity.Trial registration: This trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT03179657.

articles.title: Comparative digestive function and starch digestion kinetics in broilers and pigs.
articles.authors: Lucas Schmidt Bassi, Aaron J Cowieson, Sebastian Kaczmarek et al.
articles.abstract: This study compared starch digestion dynamics in broilers and pigs. Seven replicates of two broilers (24-d-old) and one pig (50-d-old) each were fed the same maize-based pelleted diet for 10 d, containing both solid (TiO2) and liquid (Cr-EDTA) markers. After 5 h of fasting, animals had 1 h of feed access before being euthanised at 2, 4, 6 and 8 h post-feeding. Digesta was collected from all pre-caecal segments. Jejunum and ileum combined were cut into four equal parts (SI1-4). Broilers had a heavier anterior tract and longer small intestine (SI) relative to live weight (P < 0·05), lower gizzard pH than the pig stomach (P < 0·05) and higher digesta DM. Duodenal digesta of broilers had a greater volume of particles <0·2 mm than pigs (P < 0·05). Apparent starch digestibility was higher in SI1-SI3 of broilers (P < 0·05), indicating more rapid starch digestion than pigs, although both species achieved similar digestibility (about 0·98) in SI4. Marker passage was unaffected by marker type but differed between species. Pigs showed higher proportion of markers exiting the anterior tract at 8 h (P < 0·05) and tended (P < 0·1) to have greater passage out of the SI, suggesting a more continuous flow pattern than broilers. Interval-based analysis showed similar marker passage out of the SI during 0-2 h, after which broilers had a pulsatile pattern, with reduced passage from 2 to 4 h, increased passage from 4 to 6 h and again lower passage from 6to 8 h (P < 0·05). In conclusion, broilers and pigs can attain comparable starch digestibility but rely on different kinetics and physiological mechanisms.

articles.title: Regular Exercise Moderates Age-Related Cognitive Differences in Midlife Women: Domain-Specific Effects on Processing Speed and Working Memory.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Pei-Ling Wong, Yu-Lun Chen, Chi-Hung Juan
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study examined whether regular exercise moderates age-related cognitive differences in midlife women, including reaction time (RT), executive planning, and working memory. We further investigated whether these effects differ across exercise modalities. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included ninety-three women (35-63 years) who completed simple RT, working memory, and executive planning tasks. Participants were categorized by exercise regularity and modality. Time-based outcomes were analyzed via Linear Mixed Models; accuracy via Generalized Estimating Equations. Pairwise comparisons utilized Welch's t-tests with FDR correction. RESULTS: Regular exercise moderated age-related slowing in simple RT (β=-3.083, p=0.032). Resistance training participants exhibited faster RTs than those in the non- regular exerciser, aerobic, and other exercise groups. Regarding working memory, the impact of exercise on response speed was significantly moderated by both age and task difficulty (β = -15.91, p < 0.001). Specifically, exercise-related benefits became more pronounced as cognitive load increased, a trend primarily driven by older participants, whereas these effects were less evident in younger cohorts. However, no modality-specific differences were observed. In contrast, executive planning performance was associated with age, with no significant effects of exercise or exercise-related interactions. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that regular exercise moderates age-related cognitive differences in midlife women, particularly in processing speed and high-demand working memory. These benefits were domain-specific: modality-specific advantages emerged in simple reaction time, whereas working memory benefits were modality-independent. The notable efficacy of resistance training further highlights the importance of exercise modality. Findings identify midlife as a sensitive window for targeted exercise interventions to preserve cognitive health.

articles.title: Large language models for gait classification and treatment recommendation in cerebral palsy.
articles.authors: Meltem Çelik, Sema Ertan-Birsel, Elif Demirci et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Large language model (LLM)-based artificial intelligence systems are increasingly being explored for the interpretation of clinical and biomechanical data. However, their ability to classify cerebral palsy gait patterns and support treatment-related decision-making remains unclear. RESEARCH QUESTION: How accurately can commonly used LLM-based AI systems classify sagittal gait patterns in children with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy using kinematic graphs and three-dimensional skeletal gait videos, and how well do their treatment recommendations agree with expert decisions? METHODS: Fifteen children with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy, including three cases from each Rodda sagittal gait pattern, were retrospectively evaluated. ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude independently classified each case using bilateral sagittal-plane kinematic graphs and three-dimensional skeletal gait model videos and provided treatment recommendations. Expert consensus served as the reference standard. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, together with classification accuracy. RESULTS: Classification accuracy was higher in the graph-based condition than in the video-based condition. Claude showed the highest graph-based performance (73.3% accuracy; κ=0.67), while ChatGPT and Gemini each achieved 46.7% accuracy (κ=0.33). Video-based accuracy decreased to 26.7% for ChatGPT and Gemini (κ=0.08) and 20.0% for Claude (κ=0.00). Inter-model agreement was fair for graph-based classification (κ=0.31) but poor for video-based classification (κ=-0.07). Treatment recommendation agreement was generally low across models and modalities. SIGNIFICANCE: Under the tested conditions, LLMs achieved higher accuracy with kinematic graphs, although the difference cannot be attributed to input modality alone. Graph-based classification showed promising performance; however, limited treatment concordance indicates that current LLMs should be considered supportive rather than independent clinical decision-making tools.

articles.title: Rethinking the application and adoption of NOVA classification in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): a Southeast Asian food systems perspective.
articles.authors: C Jeyakumar Henry, M Aman Wirakartakusumah, E-Siong Tee et al.
articles.abstract: Ultra-processed foods have increasingly been associated with chronic disease risk in global analyses. The NOVA classification is positioned to influence dietary guidelines, food manufacturing, and public health policy worldwide. This paper argues that the NOVA classification, when applied without contextual adaptation, may be inappropriate for Southeast Asian food systems. It could misdirect policy interventions aimed at addressing both the double burden of under- and overnutrition. By labelling foods as UPFs, NOVA may obscure the essential role that certain processed foods play in improving nutritional outcomes and advancing public health. An overemphasis on the negative impact of processed and ultra-processed foods risks oversimplifying complex dietary patterns in Asia and other LMICs. It may also undermine nutritional gains achieved over the past four decades.
