articles.title: Post-Exercise Thermal Interventions and Nocturnal Sleep in Athletes: A Narrative Review of the Potential Underlying Physiological Mechanisms.
articles.authors: Panagiotis G Miliotis, Shona L Halson, Toby Mundel et al.
articles.abstract: Sleep is essential for optimal performance and recovery in athletes. Post-exercise cold exposure, including cold water immersion and cryotherapy, is typically used to enhance recovery, but its effects on sleep remain unclear. Emerging evidence also suggests that post-exercise heat exposure, including sauna and hot water immersion before sleep may improve both objective and subjective sleep outcomes. However, the effectiveness of post-exercise thermal interventions for improving nocturnal sleep in athletes specifically has not yet been comprehensively evaluated. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence and discusses the potential physiological mechanisms by which post-exercise thermal interventions may influence nocturnal sleep in athletes. Despite methodological heterogeneity, existing research indicates that post-exercise thermal interventions may influence the subsequent nocturnal sleep of athletes through multiple and varying interacting mechanisms. For example, cold exposure close to bedtime (< 2 h) may disrupt sleep by reducing the distal-to-proximal skin temperature gradient (DPG), thereby increasing sleep onset latency and shortening sleep duration. In contrast, when applied more than 2 h before bedtime, cold exposure may improve sleep by augmenting parasympathetic tone and/or reducing muscle soreness and associated nocturnal movement. Although it remains unclear whether post-exercise heat exposure improves sleep via autonomic modulation or reduced muscle soreness, existing evidence indicates that sleep may be facilitated by an increased DPG. Moderating factors such as sex, time of day, environmental temperature, bedding microclimate, acclimatization status, and training load may influence the effects of post-exercise thermal interventions on sleep and should be investigated in future studies.

articles.title: Lean Body Mass Accounts for the Sex Dimorphism of the Circulatory System and Aerobic Exercise Capacity in Humans.
articles.authors: Xinyu Liu, Meihan Guo, David Montero
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lean body mass (LBM) strongly associates with the capacity to deliver and consume oxygen in pilot studies performed in adults with low LBM. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to test whether LBM generally accounts for the phenotype of the circulatory system and hence its sex dimorphism in humans. METHODS: Healthy women and men (n = 294, 50% female) matched by age and physical activity throughout the adult lifespan (aged 18-78 years) were included. Body composition (dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry), hemoglobin mass/intravascular volumes (carbon monoxide rebreathing), cardiac structure/function/hemodynamics (ultrasound, continuous blood pressure), and aerobic exercise capacity (cycle ergometry, metabolic cart, power meter) were assessed in standardized conditions. Linear regression analyses assessed the relationship of LBM with study variables in each sex. Sex comparisons were performed in non-LBM-matched (n = 294) and LBM-matched (n = 70) individuals. RESULTS: Lean body mass linearly associated with the majority of hematological, hemodynamic, cardiac, and exercise capacity variables in women and men. The slopes of the regression lines did not differ between sexes, with women falling in the lower and men in the upper range of the overall relationship of LBM with these variables. Accordingly, in non-LBM-matched individuals, marked sex differences were observed in >90% of variables. In LBM-matched individuals, no cardiac-related variable (left ventricular structure and function, blood pressure, systemic vascular resistance, aerobic capacity) differed between women and men. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac structure and function, blood pressure, vascular resistance, and aerobic exercise capacity are statistically accounted for by LBM in humans, irrespective of sex. The sex dimorphism of the circulatory system strongly associates with the metabolically active mass, rather than sex.

articles.title: The internal pudendal artery: a narrative review of proximal origin, accessory supply, distal branches and clinical anatomy.
articles.authors: Mugurel Constantin Rusu, Iulian Brezean
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the internal pudendal artery (IPA) is distributed across studies of internal iliac artery branching, accessory pudendal arteries, distal perineal branches, perforators, anastomoses and clinical applications. OBJECTIVE: To map human anatomical, imaging and surgical evidence on IPA origin, branching, accessory supply and clinically relevant variation. METHODS: This is a narrative review of the human anatomy of the internal pudendal artery. Relevant cadaveric, imaging, angiographic and surgical literature was identified through iterative database searching (PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science and Google Scholar), citation chasing, hand-searching of historical anatomical sources, and standard reference works on anatomical variation. Reports were organised by anatomical domain. Numerical findings were summarised as study-level results and crude aggregate counts; no meta-analysis was performed. RESULTS: The charted evidence base comprises 28 studies across 30 evidence-domain assignments, complemented by additional historical, female and clinical reports discussed narratively. Eleven proximal branching studies contributed 1,403 pelvic sides or halves. The crude distribution was 62.0% for a separate superior gluteal artery with a common inferior gluteal-IPA trunk, 20.0% for separate superior gluteal, inferior gluteal and pudendal arteries, 12.5% for a common superior-inferior gluteal trunk with a separate IPA, 3.2% for a three-artery common trunk, 1.4% for a common superior gluteal-IPA trunk and 0.8% unclassified. Five studies addressed accessory pudendal arteries, six addressed distal branches, perforators, morphometry or anastomoses, and eight provided clinical or contextual evidence. Accessory pudendal artery estimates varied substantially with the detection method. CONCLUSION: Read as a single arterial axis that continues beyond the pelvis into the ischioanal fossa and perineum, the IPA unifies several otherwise separate literatures - proximal branching, accessory supply, distal branches and clinical anatomy - that involve different units of analysis and detection methods. Future systematic reviews should examine proximal branching, accessory supply and selected distal outcomes separately.

articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition

articles.title: A Rare Sugar, D-Allulose, Attenuates Cognitive Impairment and Brain Pathologies in D-Galactose-Accelerated Aging Rats.
articles.authors: Yanmei Huang, Chanisa Thonusin, Donglin Lu et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aging is the major risk factor for cognitive impairment via aging-induced neuronal dysfunction. D-allulose, a low-calorie rare sugar, has been shown to provide beneficial effects in the obese-insulin-resistant brain. However, its beneficial effects on the aging brain have never been investigated. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether D-allulose could attenuate cognitive impairment and brain pathological alterations in a D-galactose-accelerated aging model. METHODS: Thirty-two 5-month-old male Wistar rats were randomly allocated by cage drawing lots into four groups (n = 8 rats/group): control (Con), D-galactose (D-gal), D-galactose + inulin (D-gal + Inu), and D-galactose + D-allulose (D-gal + Allu). The control group received normal saline solution (NSS; 1 mL/kg/day, s.c.), whereas the other three groups received D-galactose (150 mg/kg/day, s.c.) for 20 weeks. Beginning at week 9, the D-gal-treated groups additionally received NSS, inulin (2.0 g/kg/day), or D-allulose (1.9 g/kg/day), respectively, by oral gavage for 12 weeks. Following the treatment, spatial learning and memory were assessed using the Morris water maze. Brain pathological alterations were evaluated using Western blot, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining, mitochondrial functional assessments, and electrophysiological recordings. RESULTS: D-galactose exposure reduced target quadrant entries in the Morris Water Maze (5.6 ± 0.89 vs 7.6 ± 0.42, P = 0.021) and lowered the mean normalized hippocampal fEPSP slope (99.0% ± 1.86% vs 162.0% ± 21.79%, P = 0.009) compared with controls. D-allulose increased target quadrant entries (7.4 ± 0.50 vs 5.6 ± 0.89, P = 0.042) and the mean normalized hippocampal fEPSP slope (155.5% ± 8.95% vs 99.0% ± 1.86%, P = 0.018) compared with the D-gal group. However, inulin did not significantly alter these outcomes. Mitochondrial ROS production and brain MDA levels were also lower in D-gal + Allu group than in D-gal group (P = 0.023 and P = 0.013, respectively). CONCLUSION: D-allulose mitigates aging-associated brain dysfunction and pathological alterations in D-galactose-accelerated aging model.

articles.title: Hydroxyproline Enhances Branched-Chain Amino Acid Effects on Lifespan and Healthspan in Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.authors: Linggao Liu, Ruiyun Wu, Ziwu Gao et al.
articles.abstract: Food-derived protein hydrolysates frequently contain both collagen-associated hydroxyproline (Hyp) and branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), but the biological consequences of their combination remain unclear. This study tested whether Hyp changes the effects of leucine (Leu), isoleucine (Ile), and valine (Val) on lifespan and healthspan-related phenotypes in Caenorhabditis elegans and whether these treatment effects are accompanied by coordinated microbial and metabolic remodeling. Amino acid concentrations that did not strongly disrupt bacterial food clearance were selected for lifespan, stress-resistance, motility, muscle-integrity, biochemical, microbiome, metabolomic, and transcriptomic analyses. Hyp+BCAA combinations improved lifespan- and healthspan-related phenotypes in a BCAA- and dose-dependent manner. The strongest combined treatments enhanced resistance to thermal and oxidative stress, preserved age-associated motility and muscle structure, reduced oxidative and lipofuscin-associated markers, and increased ATP-related readouts. Multi-omics profiling showed that these direct treatment effects were accompanied by distinct C. elegans-associated microbiota signatures, altered NAD precursor-related metabolites including nicotinic acid ribonucleoside (NaR), and a Leu+Hyp transcriptional response enriched for energy metabolism, proteostasis, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Integrated microbiome-metabolome analysis identified a positive association between Rhodococcus abundance and NaR levels. These findings demonstrate that, under the tested culture conditions, Hyp+BCAA exposure improves longevity-related phenotypes and identifies microbial composition, NAD precursor metabolism, and host energy homeostasis as candidate, testable mediators.

articles.title: Maternal Mannan-Oligosaccharide improves intestinal resilience of weanling pigs via enhancing milk-mediated immune transfer.
articles.authors: Siyu Yuan, Zhenting He, Ronghua Yao et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal nutrition during late gestation and lactation influences milk composition and early-life intestinal development. Whether maternal mannan-oligosaccharide (MOS) supplementation enhances offspring resilience during weaning remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: The effects of maternal MOS supplementation on sow physiology, milk quality, offspring growth, and intestinal responses to an acute inflammatory challenge were evaluated. METHODS: Sixty sows received a control diet or 800 mg MOS/kg diet from gestation day 85 to lactation day 21 (n = 30/group). Reproductive outcomes (litter size, birth weight, subsequent estrus, insemination, conception, and farrowing) and litter outcomes (survival, daily gain, and weaning weight at 21 d) were recorded. Sow feces were collected on gestation day 109 for microbiota analysis, plasma and colostrum at farrowing and milk on lactation day 14 for antioxidant, inflammatory, nutrient, and immunoglobulin analyses, as applicable. At weaning, 24 piglets from 12 litters received saline or lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 100 μg/kg). Plasma and intestinal tissues were collected 6 h later for antioxidant, morphology, barrier, and inflammation measurements. Mixed models assessed maternal diet and, in piglets, maternal diet × LPS, with litter accounted for. RESULTS: Compared with controls, MOS increased sow lactation feed intake (5.68 vs 5.21 kg/d; P = 0.036), piglet daily gain (224.22 vs 195.35 g/d; P < 0.001), and weaning weight (6.67 vs 5.91 kg; P < 0.001). Colostral fat and IgA were 5.26% vs 3.80% and 5.37 vs 3.00 mg/mL, respectively; day-14 milk fat and IgA were 7.72% vs 5.19% and 0.43 vs 0.19 mg/mL (all P < 0.05). Relative to LPS-challenged controls, maternal MOS increased jejunal occludin protein (0.78 vs 0.44, normalized to β-actin) and decreased jejunal IL-1β (146.31 vs 169.77 pg/mL; both P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Maternal MOS supplementation improved milk-mediated nutritional and immune transfer and enhanced intestinal resilience of offspring during weaning-associated inflammatory stress in piglets.

articles.title: Impact of minimally processed versus milled whole grains on glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes: A 12-week randomised trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Andrew N Reynolds, Fiona Hood, Ella Iosua et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whole grains are widely promoted within a healthy diet, with dietary advice encouraging the replacement of refined grains with whole grains. However, data from small trials indicates that milling or processing whole grains may influence the glycaemic response. OBJECTIVE: To identify if clinically relevant HbA1c differs with processed (milled) or less processed (unmilled) whole grain intakes in type 2 diabetes management. METHODS: We conducted a 12-week randomised parallel trial in adults with type 2 diabetes. Participants received free and delivered whole grain foods that differed in degree of processing. Each intervention was of four foods from whole grain wheat, rice, and oats, in sufficient amounts (4.5-9kg per fortnight) to accommodate family size. Participants were advised to replace the grain foods they normally consumed with the provided products. The primary outcome was glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c). All analyses were performed using an intention-to-treat approach, with outcome variables investigated using a generalised linear model. RESULTS: 160 adults with type 2 diabetes (mean age 58.5 ± 11.5 years; BMI 33.7 ± 7.3 kg/m2; HbA1c 56.4 ± 14.3 mmol/mol) were randomised, with 143 (89%) providing end-of-intervention blood samples. HbA1c was lower following the less processed whole grain intervention compared with the more processed whole grain intervention (mean difference -2.2 mmol/mol, 95% CI -4.2, -0.1), despite no change observed in body weight between interventions. Whole grain, refined grain, and nutrient intakes did not differ between groups, with intervention foods providing approximately 20% of dietary energy. Among the secondary or exploratory outcomes, improvements were indicated only in self-reported bowel habits with less processed whole grains. CONCLUSIONS: Less processed whole grain foods were associated with improved glycated haemoglobin compared with more processed whole grain foods in adults with type 2 diabetes. These findings indicate that the degree of grain processing influences metabolic outcomes, support food reformulation, and distinguishing between refined grains, milled whole grains (wholemeal), and intact whole grains in dietary guidance, food marketing and labelling. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NUMBER AND WEBSITE WHERE IT WAS OBTAINED: ACTRN12622000060741.

articles.title: Metabolic phenotyping identifies early interindividual variation in infant energy expenditure with implications for obesity risk.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Emily W Flanagan, Abby D Altazan, Leanne M Redman
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric obesity is a major public health crisis. Early identification of metabolic traits that increase individual risk are emerging. As such, identification of variability in early energy expenditure would reveal the need for precision nutritional approaches from birth. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the interindividual variability in components of energy expenditure for the purpose of understanding early nutritional considerations in very young infants. METHODS: Infant participants (<3 months of age) underwent extensive energy expenditure phenotyping using a combination of doubly labeled water for total daily energy expenditure and a novel infant metabolic chamber for sleeping energy expenditure. Descriptive statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients, and univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses were used to assess reliability and characterize variability, predictors, and phenotypes of energy expenditure. We identified interindividual variability in total, mass-adjusted, and fat-free mass adjusted energy expenditures. Energy phenotypes (thrifty and spendthrift) were assigned based on the residuals between measured and predicted energy expenditure from metabolic mass. Discrepancies between measured energy expenditure and predicted by national dietary recommendations for infants (2023 DRI) were evaluated. RESULTS: Total daily and sleeping energy expenditures were 368±60 kcal/d and 250±60 kcal/d, respectively. Energy expenditure related to activity accounted for 21±9% of total measured. Age (r=.59), weight (r=.83), length (r=.75), and fat-free mass (r=.82) were positively associated with sleeping energy expenditure. We identified 40% of measured infants with a thrifty energy phenotype, classified as having sleeping energy expenditure under that predicted by cohort age, sex, and fat and fat-free mass. Mean prediction error of the 2023 DRI from our cohort was 10±7% and was positively associated with the amount of energy expenditure attributed to activity. CONCLUSIONS: These findings warrant further comprehensive metabolic phenotyping studies in young infants to understand how early energy expenditure tracks through the life course and influences obesity risk as well as the thorough evaluation and refinement of infant nutritional recommendations.

articles.title: Almonds and the optimization of immune responses to influenza vaccination, compared to a control snack, in healthy adults: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Alice van der Schoot, Alice C Creedon, Noa Argomaniz et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Certain nutrient supplements enhance immune responses to vaccination; however, no randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have assessed the impact of a whole food. Almonds may benefit immune function through immunoregulatory nutrients and fiber, which interacts with the immune system via the gut microbiota. OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the effect of almonds on the immune response following influenza vaccination, compared to an isocaloric snack, in healthy adults. METHODS: In this RCT, healthy adults (40-64 years) consumed almonds (56 g/d) or an isocaloric control (86 g/d pretzels) for 8 weeks. Participants received seasonal influenza vaccine at week 4. The primary outcome was seroconversion rates for ≥1 strain at week 8. Antigen-specific antibody titers (HI assay) were quantified pre- (week 4) and post-vaccination (week 8), and seroconversion and seroprotection were calculated. The gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), stool output and gut symptoms were measured at baseline, midpoint and endpoint. RESULTS: Ninety participants were randomized (mean age 51 years, 73% females). Seroconversion rate for ≥1 strain was high and not significantly different between groups [almond: 38/41 (93%) versus control: 37/39 (95%), P=1.000], nor were strain-specific seroconversion or seroprotection rates. Almonds resulted in higher antibody titers for A/Wisconsin/67/2022 (H1N1) strain, compared to control [geometric mean (95% CI): almond 359 (146, 881) versus control 110 (51, 235)], and greater fold-change for A/Wisconsin/67/2022 (H1N1) [geometric mean fold change (95% CI): almond 18 (7, 48) versus control 4 (3, 7)] and B/Yamagata [almond 10 (6, 16) versus control 5 (3, 7)]. Absolute abundance of Roseburia hominis was significantly higher in the almond group compared to control (q=0.049). There was no effect on SCFAs or stool consistency. CONCLUSIONS: Almonds increased influenza vaccine antibody titers but did not affect seroconversion in a healthy population where vaccines are already highly effective. This trial was pre-registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05515263 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05515263).

articles.title: From structural repair to biomechanical compatibility: Aortic stiffness after open and endovascular aortic repair.
articles.authors: Thurkga Moothathamby, Matti Jubouri, Fatima Kayali et al.
articles.abstract: Evaluation of aortic repair has traditionally prioritised perioperative safety, exclusion of the diseased segment and durability. As endovascular treatment expands to younger patients, attention is turning towards the biomechanical compatibility of prosthetic grafts with the native aorta. Native aortic compliance supports Windkessel function, whereas grafts create a compliance transition that may accelerate pulse-wave transmission, alter wave reflection and increase left-ventricular load. This narrative review distinguishes established evidence from emerging concepts after open surgical repair, endovascular aneurysm repair and thoracic endovascular aortic repair. Carotid-femoral pulse-wave velocity (cfPWV) is the accepted reference non-invasive measure of regional aortic stiffness; cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived segmental pulse-wave velocity and distensibility provide complementary information. Brachial-ankle pulse-wave velocity, the cardio-ankle vascular index, and augmentation index assess different territories or haemodynamic properties and are not interchangeable with cfPWV. Left-ventricular strain and mass are downstream cardiac outcomes. Clinical evidence generally reports increases in measured arterial-stiffness indices after endovascular repair, whereas findings after open repair are heterogeneous. Treatment length, landing-zone location, oversizing, anatomy and baseline vascular phenotype may be as important as graft fabric or stent-frame category. Conflicting comparisons of polyester and expanded polytetrafluoroethylene arise from small, non-randomised studies using non-equivalent endpoints and do not support a reliable ranking of commercial devices. Emerging 4D-flow CMR, simulation and compliant graft materials illustrate a shift from structural exclusion alone towards compliance-aware repair, but evidence of improved outcomes remains insufficient. Future studies should use standardised longitudinal stiffness, blood-pressure and cardiac assessments and relate biomechanical changes to hypertension, ventricular remodelling and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Non-recurrent laryngeal nerve with dual branch pattern and merging: a rare anatomical variant encountered during right hemithyroidectomy.
articles.authors: Badriya Yussuf, Haissan Iftikhar
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The non-recurrent laryngeal nerve (NRLN) is an uncommon anatomical variant that passes directly from the vagus nerve to the larynx without the usual recurrent loop; it occurs on the right side in around one in a hundred individuals and is considerably rarer on the left. Its recognition is central to safe thyroid surgery, because an unanticipated NRLN lies in an unexpected position and is vulnerable to inadvertent injury. We report a right non-recurrent laryngeal nerve with an unusual dual-branch morphology in which the nerve divided and then re-merged before laryngeal entry. CASE PRESENTATION: A woman in her 50s underwent right hemithyroidectomy for a benign, compressive multinodular goitre of the right lobe. Intraoperatively, no recurrent laryngeal nerve was found in the expected tracheo-oesophageal groove; systematic tracing of the vagus nerve within the carotid sheath revealed a right NRLN that divided into a superior and an inferior branch. The two branches followed separate courses and re-merged into a single trunk approximately 10 mm before entering the larynx through the cricothyroid membrane. Both branches were identified and preserved. The patient was extubated uneventfully, demonstrated normal vocal cord function, and made an uncomplicated recovery with no voice change at early or later follow-up. CONCLUSION: Dual-branch NRLN in which the branches re-merge before laryngeal entry is a pattern we have not found previously described; while extra-laryngeal division of a non-recurrent nerve has been reported, the subsequent re-merging adds complexity to nerve identification and preservation. Awareness that a non-recurrent nerve may branch and re-merge should prompt complete tracing of every fascicle followed from the vagus during thyroid surgery.

articles.title: Bioerosion traces in bones reveal an increase in ethological diversity in the insect exploitation of carcasses in the late Triassic.
articles.authors: Lucca S Cunha, Francesco Battista, Heitor Francischini
articles.abstract: This study presents the first detailed description of bioerosion traces produced by insects in bones from the Santa Cruz Sequence (early Carnian, Santa Maria Supersequence, Brazil). An array of traces is reported, consisting of notches, a tube, trails of grooves attributed to the ichnotaxon Osteocallis mandibulus and ornamented depressions attributed to a new ichnotaxon Osteograptus thanatobios igen. nov. et isp. nov. The traces were likely produced by insects, but a less inclusive taxonomic attribution is currently not possible. The ethological interpretation for the bioerosion structures is that they represent feeding traces. This report increases the contrast between the Middle and Late Triassic bioerosion record, since the latter is significantly more diverse and abundant. Hypotheses related to the onset of the Carnian Humid Episode as well as taphonomic biases are discussed as possible explanations for this contrast.

articles.title: Large Language Models and Applied Surgical Anatomy: Evaluation of Anatomical Reasoning in Expert-Derived Plastic Surgery Scenarios.
articles.authors: Menekşe Kastamoni Başkan, Süleyman Çeçen, Yadigar Kastamoni
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into medical education, research, and clinical decision-support applications; however, their ability to apply anatomical knowledge in clinically relevant surgical scenarios remains insufficiently studied. This study evaluated and compared the performance of six contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, Copilot, and Manus) using 25 expert-derived applied surgical anatomy scenarios relevant to plastic surgery. Scenarios were developed by an expert panel consisting of one associate professor of anatomy and two plastic surgeons. Responses were generated using a standardized prompt and assessed with a structured scoring rubric evaluating anatomical accuracy, clinical reasoning, completeness, and safety, with a maximum score of 10 points per question. Critical errors were additionally assessed. Significant differences in overall performance were observed among models (Friedman χ2 = 43.51, p < 0.001). ChatGPT achieved the maximum aggregate score (250/250), followed by Gemini (248/250), DeepSeek (241/250), Copilot (240/250), Claude (235/250), and Manus (219/250). Critical errors were infrequent and were confined to a reconstructive vascular physiology scenario: DeepSeek, Claude, and Manus each demonstrated one observed critical error, whereas ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot demonstrated none. Although all evaluated models demonstrated excellent performance, clinically significant anatomical misconceptions persisted despite high aggregate scores. These findings demonstrate strong performance by the tested LLMs on this specific scenario-based benchmark, while also identifying clinically meaningful anatomical errors in a subset of responses. Future evaluations should focus not only on overall accuracy but also on clinically meaningful error patterns that may influence surgical decision-making. Importantly, substantial ceiling effects limited discrimination among high-performing models, and the findings should therefore be interpreted as performance on this specific benchmark rather than as evidence of a general hierarchy of anatomical reasoning capability.

articles.title: The Surgical Anatomy of the Lymphatic System of the Stomach.
articles.authors: Catherine Olang, Elizabeth Wagura, Sarah Renna et al.
articles.abstract: The gastric lymphatic system is essential for immune function and the metastasis of gastric cancer. However, variations in lymphatic anatomy, drainage patterns, and staging frameworks complicate surgical planning and oncologic decision-making. This study aims to review the anatomy of the gastric lymphatic system, the history and variation of JCGC and UICC/AJCC TNM gastric lymphatic staging classifications, while also exploring the differences between lymphadenectomy strategies. A PRISMA-guided search across PubMed, PMC, ScienceDirect, Elsevier Science, Wiley, and SpringerLink retrieved eligible studies meeting pre-determined inclusion criteria. Of the 79 entries returned, 40 eligible studies were identified after application of our inclusion and exclusion criteria. The JCGC and UICC/AJCC TNM systems differ in their staging methods. While the JCGC categorizes lymph nodes by their location relative to the tumor, the UICC/AJCC categorizes the N stage by the number of positive lymph nodes detected. Though the UICC/AJCC staging system is dominant in multiple countries, efforts have been made in recent years to align the protocols in both staging systems. As a result, D2 lymphadenectomy is widely practiced in JCGC adhering countries, whereas UICC/AJCC protocols favor selective dissection combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The complexity of gastric lymphatic anatomy and the absence of a globally standardized staging classification can lead to heterogeneous lymphadenectomy strategies and inconsistent oncologic outcomes. This review emphasizes the need for a unified classification system that incorporates anatomical, oncologic, and imaging perspectives to improve staging and optimize surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Shape-based identification of caprine taxa using fragmentary skull regions.
articles.authors: Tomasz Szara, Hasan Hüseyin Arı, Barış Can Güzel et al.
articles.abstract: Fragmentary skull remains are common in zooarchaeological assemblages, yet they pose significant challenges for taxonomic identification because complete skulls are rare. This study investigated whether three resilient cranial regions: the body of the maxilla, the exoccipital region, and the bony palate, retain sufficient shape information to discriminate among caprine taxa. The sample comprised domestic sheep (Ovis aries), wild Marco Polo sheep (Ovis ammonpolii), domestic goat (Capra hircus), and Tatra chamois (Rupicapra tatrica). Three-dimensional landmarks were digitized on surface-scanned skulls. All three regions exhibited significant inter-group shape differences (p: 0.0001). The body of the maxilla provided the strongest discrimination (R2 = 0.520), clearly separating ovine from caprine taxa along an axis linked to the relative position of the caudodorsal facial-orbital region versus the infraorbital and alveolar sectors. The exoccipital region showed intermediate discriminatory power, whereas the bony palate exhibited the weakest group structure and the greatest overlap. Centroid size differed significantly among groups (wild sheep being the largest), but shape differences remained significant after accounting for size. Isolated skull fragments, particularly the maxillary body, retain reliable diagnostic shape information for distinguishing caprine taxa. When analyzed using geometric morphometrics, these fragments can serve as valuable analytical units in zooarchaeological studies, even in highly fragmented assemblages.

articles.title: Virtual cranial endocast of Lotheridium mengi and brain evolution in early metatherians.
articles.authors: Alexander Bi, Byron D Ford, Qian Li et al.
articles.abstract: Very little is known about the early brain evolution of Metatheria, and no brain endocast of this group has been described from prior to the Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) boundary. This has led to great uncertainty regarding the ancestral condition of the therian brain. Here, we aim to fill some of this gap by describing the first brain endocast of a Cretaceous metatherian, Lotheridium mengi from the Late Cretaceous of Henan, China. Lotheridium has an encephalization quotient comparable to the Cretaceous multituberculate Chulsanbaatar and eutherian Asioryctes and reaches the lower range of crown mammals. Together with patterns observed in other Mesozoic mammals, this suggests that increased encephalization evolved independently in several major mammalian lineages. The endocast is characterized by relatively small olfactory bulbs, well-developed petrosal lobules, and a prominent hypophyseal cast, differentiating it from earlier mammals. With the addition of a dorsally exposed midbrain, Lotheridium closely resembles the condition observed in Cretaceous eutherians. We propose that reduced olfactory bulb proportions and increased endocranial volume in Cretaceous eutherians and metatherians reflect a major shift in mammalian brain evolution, from primarily olfactory bulb expansion in the Jurassic to predominantly neocortical, brainstem, and cerebellar expansion in the Late Cretaceous. The endocranial morphology of Lotheridium further indicates that several neuroanatomical features characteristic of Paleogene and extant marsupials, including relatively enlarged olfactory bulbs and a smaller brain size compared to eutherians, are unlikely to represent the plesiomorphic condition for Metatheria. Ultimately, Lotheridium provides crucial new information regarding the ancestral condition of marsupial brains.

articles.title: Heart rate variability and cortisol responses to acute low- and moderate-intensity exercise in stress-related exhaustion.
articles.authors: Jenny Kling, Örjan Ekblom, Robert Persson Asplund et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Exercise is commonly recommended to support stress regulation and mental health, yet it remains unclear whether these benefits translate to conditions characterized by prolonged stress and fatigue. The aims were to examine whether autonomic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis responses to a single exercise bout differ between individuals with stress-related exhaustion and healthy controls, and whether responses vary by exercise intensity. METHODS: In a randomized, counterbalanced crossover design, 30 individuals with stress-related exhaustion (93.3% women; age 46.3 ± 5.89) and 29 healthy controls with a comparable age and sex distribution (93.1% women; age 45.5 ± 5.47) completed two 22-min cycling sessions at workloads corresponding to 40% (low intensity) and 55% (moderate intensity) of estimated maximal oxygen uptake (V̇O₂max) on separate occasions. Heart rate variability (HRV; RMSSD, SD2/SD1, LF/HF) and salivary cortisol were assessed pre-exercise, post-exercise, and 30 min post-exercise, with HRV also assessed during exercise. RESULTS: Compared with controls, individuals with stress-related exhaustion showed lower RMSSD overall, with the most apparent between-group differences observed during the post-exercise period. Within the exhaustion group, moderate- compared with low-intensity exercise was associated with lower RMSSD and higher SD2/SD1 and LF/HF, whereas no intensity effects were observed in controls. No between-group differences were observed in HRV during exercise. Cortisol analyses suggested overall group-related differences, without clear differences across time points. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest altered physiological stress-system regulation in stress-related exhaustion and highlight the post-exercise period and exercise intensity as important considerations when tailoring exercise recommendations for this population. The study was retrospectively registered on 05/30/2024 at Clinical Trials.gov, with trial registration number NCT06429423.

articles.title: One Carbon Metabolism - The Missing Link for Cancer and Sepsis.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Abigail Anderson, Carter Weeg
articles.abstract: One-carbon (1C) metabolism (OCM) is a biosynthetic and physiological process essential to cells. OCM encompasses a multitude of tightly regulated biochemical reactions that are responsible for nucleotide synthesis (purines and pyrimidines), amino acid homeostasis (Met, Ser, Gly), redox balance, and epigenetic regulation. Dysregulations of this pathway have been implicated in the development and progression of cancer and sepsis - two complex pathologies, each with a characteristically high morbidity and mortality rate. OCM changes in the oncogenic state have been extensively investigated, while metabolic pathway changes in sepsis remain more elusive. Given that emerging evidence suggests that 1 in 5 sepsis hospitalizations occur in patients with a cancer diagnosis, and recovering sepsis patients have a higher incidence of cancer diagnosis, our review aims to analyze the known OCM changes that occur in each pathology, highlight commonalities and variations, and suggest clinical implications that explore possible therapeutic targets. Through a novel cross-disease examination, a more comprehensive understanding of OCM metabolic changes in these disease states could inform clinical practice and lead to the development of targeted therapeutic interventions that further our understanding and treatment of one or both conditions.

articles.title: MRI-Compatible Ex-Vivo Tensile Testing for Assessment of Passive Mechanical Properties of Whole Muscle.
articles.authors: Iraj Dehghan-Hamani, Alexander Burden, Stephen H M Brown et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate measurement of the passive mechanical properties of whole skeletal muscle is essential for physiological studies and biomechanical models. However, conventional ex-vivo tensile testing to measure these properties often relies on assumptions for stress and strain calculation. Specifically, strain is typically calculated from grip-to-grip displacement, and stress is found using muscle physiological cross-sectional area (PCSA) based on literature density values. This study aimed to develop a method directly quantifying muscle 3D geometry during stretching to measure its passive elastic modulus. Our MRI-compatible ex-vivo tensile testing framework integrated stepwise testing with high-field (9.4T) MRI. This enabled us to directly quantify whole-muscle 3D geometry, volume, and length during stretching. Ten rat tibialis anterior muscles underwent incremental lengthening (∼6% strain per step) with 4-min stress-relaxation holds while acquiring T2-weighted 3D MRI at each step. Engineering stress-strain data were calculated using MRI-based and conventional measurements. Grip-to-grip strain overestimated muscle strain by 13.7% compared to MRI-derived value, while considering MRI-based volumetric PCSA produced stresses 7.4% higher than the traditional gravimetric approach. These methodological differences increased the estimated passive elastic modulus by ∼40% versus conventional calculations. We also observed progressive muscle volume increases during testing (∼13.7% from slack length to ∼36% strain), with larger baseline volumes in specimens stored longer in Tyrode's solution. Accounting for this volume change, true stress-strain results showed substantially higher modulus values than engineering estimates (1162 ± 519 vs. 745 ± 352 kPa at 30% strain). Overall, MRI-based geometry monitoring improved whole-muscle stress-strain characterization and revealed muscle volume increases during ex-vivo testing.

articles.title: Assessing regional pulmonary response to methacholine and mannitol challenge in asthma patients using hyperpolarized helium-3 magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.authors: Chuan Tai Foo, Kris Nilsen, Peter Noble et al.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ventilation heterogeneity is a feature of asthmatic bronchoconstriction and contributes to airway hyperresponsiveness and disease expression. This study characterized ventilation heterogeneity using hyperpolarized helium-3 magnetic resonance imaging (HP-MRI) in patients with mild asthma following methacholine and mannitol inhalational challenge and determined whether topographical differences exist in the response to these different stimuli. METHODS: Six patients with mild asthma were recruited (1 male, 5 females; age 35.3±11.4 years; BMI 22.8±3.0 kg/m2). Patients underwent HP-MRI and forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) at baseline and following crossover methacholine and mannitol challenge on separate days. Ventilation heterogeneity was assessed qualitatively and using ventilation defect percentage (VDP). Comparisons between the pre- and post-provocation scans, and the difference in regional changes induced by methacholine and mannitol were performed. RESULTS: FEV1 was significantly reduced (p=0.0002) by methacholine (94.9±15.1 vs 70.2±9.7 %predicted) and mannitol (94.5±14.6 vs 73.8±18.1 %predicted). Accompanying this was a significant increase in VDP (p=0.02) from 8.5±4.5 to 19.8±6.9% after methacholine, and 8.4±3.4 to 17.8±6.3% after mannitol challenge. Regional differences were observed between the two provocation agents with methacholine having a larger impact on the peripheral airways (p=0.005) and mannitol on the central airways (p<0.05), despite comparable changes in FEV1 (p=0.62) and VDP (p=0.46). CONCLUSIONS: Regional differences in ventilation heterogeneity exist when asthmatic airways are subjected to methacholine and mannitol challenge. These findings give new insights into the regional pathobiology of airflow obstruction in patients with asthma and highlight the role of HP-MRI as a valuable tool in understanding airway disease.

articles.title: Characterising the Internal and External Load During Warm-Up, Match Play and Training in Soccer Substitutes: A Systematic Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Christopher Curtis, Mark Russell, Samuel P Hills et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Shorter match-play exposure for soccer substitutes relative to those who start matches has implications in the days before, during and following match play concerning their training, preparatory and recovery/compensatory practices. Specifically, characterising the internal and external loading of substitute players throughout a weekly microcycle can facilitate evidence-based recommendations aimed at optimising their performance readiness. OBJECTIVES: This systematic scoping review aimed to map and characterise the internal and external loading associated with warm-up, match play and training in soccer substitutes. METHODS: Prior to literature searches being conducted, a Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Study design (PICOS) statement was formed. Online database (PubMed, SPORTDiscus, Scopus and Web of Science) searches were performed according to PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) protocols. Studies were eligible if internal or external characteristics of soccer substitutes were measured in training or match-play scenarios. After calibration exercises, two authors independently quality assessed each study, with Cohen's kappa undertaken to assess inter-rater agreement. A scoping review methodology was selected because of the methodological and conceptual heterogeneity across studies, which precluded meaningful meta-analysis. RESULTS: A total of 5135 studies were identified, 66 of which met study criteria. Substantive inter-rater agreement was observed (κ = 0.939, p < 0.001) during the quality assessment of included studies. Soccer substitutes' body temperature, and thus several aspects of physical performance, may not be maintained at time of pitch entry (body temperature pre-pitch entry ~ 37 °C vs match play > 38 °C). Substitutes may experience lower absolute physical loading during training and match day (e.g. match-day 'top up' activity: ~ 17 min; total distance: ~ 1700 m) but during match play, substitutes typically cover higher relative total distances (~ 109 to ~ 137 m·min-1), high-speed running (~ 9.8 to ~ 13.5 m·min-1) and sprinting distance (~ 3.8 to 5.0 m·min-1) compared with players who started the match. Substitutes playing in the second-half exhibit increased heart rates compared with full-match players (84% vs 81% maximum heart rate); however, this remains lower than the first-half heart rate responses of full-match players (84% vs 86% maximum heart rate). CONCLUSIONS: This systematic scoping review summarises current evidence and key findings relating to the internal and external characteristics of soccer substitutes during warm-up, match play and training that can be used in practice to inform player welfare and sport science support within these cohorts. Chiefly, during match-day warm-ups, soccer substitutes' body temperature and physical performance responses may not be maintained, despite typical substitute-specific match-day practices being employed. Similarly, soccer substitutes were frequently reported to demonstrate higher relative total distance, high-speed running and sprinting outputs compared with starting players. Further research is needed to better understand performance demands, longitudinal adaptations, contextual influences and female-specific responses in soccer substitutes.

articles.title: High-intensity interval training modulates the SIRT1-P16 pathway, inflammatory markers, and oxidative stress in the liver of D-galactose-treated male rats.
articles.authors: Beydolah Shahouzehi, Homa Jafari, Farzaneh Rostamzadeh
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Aging contributes to progressive hepatic dysfunction, characterized by increased oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and mitochondrial impairment, which collectively exacerbate metabolic decline. This study examined the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on the SIRT1-P16 axis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory markers in a D-galactose (D-gal )-induced aging model in male Wistar rats. METHODS: Twenty-eight rats were assigned to four groups: Control (CTL), HIIT, D-gal, and D-gal+HIIT. Aging model was induced via daily subcutaneous injections of D-galactose (150 mg/kg) for eight weeks, while HIIT was performed on a treadmill five times per week over the same period. Gene expression and protein levels were measured by Real-time PCR and Western blot, respectively. Antioxidant and oxidant, and inflammatory markers were determined via colorimetric and ELISA methods. RESULTS: Gene expression analysis showed that D-gal significantly downregulated the expression of AMPK, SIRT1, and PGC-1α, whereas HIIT was associated with increased expression of these markers. Western blot analysis confirmed a reduction and elevation in SIRT1 and P16 protein, respectively, in the D-gal group, which were reversed following HIIT. HIIT also ameliorated the increase in the levels of malondialdehyde, IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α and the decrease in the SOD and GPx activities. CONCLUSION: Concurrent HIIT attenuated D-galactose-induced hepatic molecular and biochemical alterations associated with aging. These effects were accompanied by changes in SIRT1-P16-related markers, improved redox balance, and reduced inflammatory responses, supporting the potential of HIIT as a non-pharmacological strategy for promoting liver health during aging.

articles.title: "Markers of benefit": the influence of physiological and physical factors on the relationship between slow-paced breathing and heart rate variability.
articles.authors: Rabeea Maqsood, Susie Schofield, Anthony Michael James Bull et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Slow-paced breathing (SPB) improves autonomic balance and increases heart rate variability (HRV). The influence of combat-related traumatic injury (CRTI), baseline respiratory rate (RR), and physical function/activity on the relationship between SPB and HRV has not been examined previously and was the aim of this study. METHODS: We analysed the first follow-up data from the ongoing ArmeD serVices trAuma rehabilitatioN outComE (ADVANCE) Cohort study. Short-term HRV was measured using a single-lead electrocardiogram during five minutes of spontaneous breathing, followed by five minutes of SPB (six breaths/minute). We examined the effect modification of SPB on HRV by CRTI (yes/no), RR during spontaneous breathing (< 15/≥15 breaths/minute), weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire and physical function (6-minute-walk-distance; 6MWD). Linear models for panel data were run, adjusting for age, sampling rank, ethnicity, and cardiovascular and respiratory medication. RESULTS: A total of 962 male participants (median age: 37.6 years; n = 487 injured, n = 495 uninjured; mean 11years post-injury/deployment) with paired spontaneous-SPB HRV data were included. All short-term HRV measures increased during SPB when compared to spontaneous breathing. CRTI, 6MWD and MVPA did not significantly moderate the effect of SPB on HRV, but baseline RR ≥ 15 breaths/minute did, with Root-Mean-Square-Of-Successive-Difference (RMSSD) increasing from 15.57ms to 21.89ms (p < 0.001) during SPB. CONCLUSION: SPB improves HRV regardless of CRTI status. Those with higher baseline RR are more likely to obtain a significant improvement in HRV during SPB. SPB-based interventions may be introduced for the rehabilitation of military personnel following injury/deployment.

articles.title: The ascending aorta and vascular profile in recreational masters runners: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Wioletta Sacharczuk, Rafał Dankowski, Dagmara Tritt et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Endurance exercise remodels the large arteries, but whether a recreational training dose is sufficient to induce such remodelling is unclear. Masters recreational runners over 40 years are under-represented in this research. We compared the ascending aortic diameter and vascular profile of these runners with sedentary controls of similar age. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 42 masters recreational runners (at least 20 km per week for at least one year) and 27 sedentary controls, all over 40 years, free of cardiovascular disease and without bicuspid aortic valve or connective tissue disorder. We measured the ascending aortic diameter and left ventricular function by transthoracic echocardiography, and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and the ankle-brachial index (ABI) by oscillometry. Circulating collagen-turnover markers (CTX-I, MMP-2) were assayed. The aortic diameter was compared between groups by regression. RESULTS: The ascending aorta was wider in runners (3.25 vs. 2.90 cm; p = 0.001; Cliff's delta 0.45). The difference persisted after adjustment for age, sex and height (beta 0.31 cm; p = 0.001) and in sensitivity analyses. No aortic diameter reached 4.0 cm; all remained within normal limits. The ABI was higher in runners (1.07 vs. 1.03; p = 0.007), and baPWV did not differ (p = 0.069); both stayed within normal limits. CTX-I and MMP-2 did not differ, and left ventricular function was preserved. CONCLUSION: These findings are consistent with modest, exercise-associated aortic remodelling rather than overt aortopathy in recreational masters runners over 40 years.

articles.title: Creatine supplementation effects on cognition, sleep, and menopause symptoms in response to six weeks of high-intensity resistance training in perimenopausal females.
articles.authors: Paul A Baker, Gabrielle M DelBiondo, Caroline G Kelly et al.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Perimenopause (PERI) women experience cognitive dysfunction, sleep disturbances, and menopause-related symptoms, yet few accessible and time-efficient interventions have been evaluated. The purpose of the current study was to determine the impact of creatine monohydrate (CM) during six weeks of high-intensity resistance training (HIRT) on cognition, sleep, and menopause symptoms in PERI females. METHODS: PERI females (n = 51; Age: 46 ± 5 yrs) were randomized to CM (n = 18), placebo (PLA) (n = 20), or a non-training control (CON) group (n = 13). CM and PLA groups completed a 5-day loading phase (20 g·day⁻¹) followed by six weeks of maintenance (~ 4.5 g·day⁻¹) combined with twice-weekly progressive HIRT. Cognitive performance (Stroop, Rey 15-item memory test) and prefrontal oxygenation via functional near-infrared spectroscopy were assessed at baseline (BASE), pre- (PRE), and post-training (POST). Sleep and self-reported menopause symptoms (temperature sensitivity, fatigue, soreness, brain fog, and bloating) were monitored daily using a WHOOP wearable wristband. RESULTS: Stroop reaction time improved over time (congruent: p < 0.001; incongruent: p = 0.004) with no group differences. Prefrontal oxygenation during the Stroop test increased with CM at POST (+ 0.32 ± 2.01%) compared to a decrease with PLA (- 1.62 ± 2.01%; p = 0.003). Sleep consistency showed a time × treatment interaction (p < 0.001), with higher consistency in CM than PLA at week 6 (baseline-adjusted mean difference: +7.4% points, p = 0.015). CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory analysis, CM combined with HIRT was associated with greater prefrontal oxygenation, higher sleep consistency, and fewer self-reported temperature sensitivity days relative to PLA in PERI females.

articles.title: Reliability and analytical validity of the MX3 hydration testing system during exercise in the heat.
articles.authors: Xiujing Zhao, Brendon P McDermott, Zachary J McKenna et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The MX3 Hydration Testing System provides portable saliva osmolality (SOsm) measurements, but its between-day reliability and analytical validity against a laboratory reference osmometer remain unclear. This study evaluated MX3 reliability and analytical validity and examined whether measurement performance differed between direct tongue and collected-saliva sampling approaches. METHODS: Twenty healthy, physically active adults (10 females) completed one 30-min familiarization trial and two 120-min self-paced exercise trials in the heat. SOsm was measured using MX3 directly from the tongue and from collected saliva samples and compared with a laboratory freezing-point depression osmometer (OSMO1). Between-day reliability was evaluated using the coefficient of variation (CV), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Bland-Altman analysis. Analytical validity was assessed using linear regression, CV, and Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: Direct tongue measurements demonstrated poor between-day reliability (CV = 31-35%; ICC = - 0.003-0.053), whereas collected-saliva measurements demonstrated lower variability and moderate reliability (CV = 17-18%; ICC = 0.618-0.663). Collected-saliva measurements were strongly related to OSMO1 across all measurement conditions (R2 = 0.570-0.821; all p < 0.001), with mean biases ranging from - 23.9 to - 25.9 mOsm/kg and 95% limits of agreement (LoA) ranging from - 75.4 to 27.1 mOsm/kg. In contrast, direct tongue measurements showed weaker and less consistent relationships with OSMO1 (R2 = 0.001-0.282; p = 0.005-0.804), greater variability (CV = 36-51%), and larger negative biases (- 31.3 to - 52.0 mOsm/kg), with 95% LoA ranging from - 134.4 to 30.4 mOsm/kg. Agreement between the two MX3 sampling approaches was limited, particularly following exercise. CONCLUSION: Collected-saliva MX3 measurements demonstrated better between-day reliability and analytical performance than direct tongue measurements, although systematic disagreement with the reference osmometer remained. MX3 measurement performance differed between saliva sampling approaches, supporting further validation of the collected-saliva approach.

articles.title: Age and ethnicity influence serum holotranscobalamin ('Active' B12) and methylmalonic acid concentrations, two markers of vitamin B12 status assessment.
articles.authors: Agata Sobczyńska-Malefora, Maheen Siddiqui, Dominic J Harrington
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Serum vitamin B12 and holotranscobalamin (holoTC) are biomarkers of vitamin B12 status, often used with confirmatory tests such as methylmalonic acid (MMA). Serum B12 concentrations vary by age and ethnicity, but the impact of these factors on holoTC is unclear. METHODS: HoloTC was measured in 61,193 samples from an ethnically-diverse hospital population in London (Jan 2022-Oct 2023). HoloTC <25, 25-70 and >70 pmol/L were classified as deficient, indeterminate and replete, respectively. MMA was measured in 12,233 patients with holoTC 25-70 pmol/L. RESULTS: HoloTC concentrations differed significantly by ethnicity. Ethnic differences were minimal in children but became apparent in adulthood, with Black patients showing the highest holoTC concentrations, Asians intermediate, and White the lowest (p < 0.001). Overall, 1.7% of patients were holoTC deficient and 25.3% indeterminate. Among patients with holoTC 25-70 pmol/L, elevated MMA occurred in 32.7% of White, 14.8% of Black and 34.1% of Asian patients (p < 0.001) using age-specific MMA cut-offs ( > 280 nmol/L for ≤65 years; >360 nmol/L for >65 years). Using a higher MMA cut-off ( > 750 nmol/L), prevalence fell to 4.0%, 1.2%, and 4.7%, respectively. The overall prevalence of vitamin B12 deficiency in the entire cohort was 7.8% or 2.4%, depending on the MMA threshold. Compared with White patients, Black patients were 34.6% less likely to have elevated MMA. CONCLUSIONS: HoloTC and MMA concentrations vary significantly by age and ethnicity. Black adults exhibited higher holoTC and lower MMA concentrations, suggesting better B12 status or differences in metabolism. Age- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges for holoTC and MMA should be considered.

articles.title: Age-dependent role of BMP13 in cartilage homeostasis.
articles.authors: Vianna G Martinez, Pranav Rastogi, Alisha Gupta et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Age is a primary risk factor for osteoarthritis (OA) development, which is characterized by articular cartilage destruction. However, age-related changes leading to altered cartilage homeostasis and increased susceptibility to OA development need further elucidation. Thus, this study aimed to assess bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)13 age-dependent effects on cartilage extracellular matrix (ECM) homeostasis. METHODS: Both juvenile and adult cartilage explants were treated with BMP13 and both transcriptomic and biochemical changes were assessed to determine effects on ECM homeostasis. Dorsomorphin and U0126 were utilized to inhibit the SMAD1/5/8 and ERK1/2 pathways, respectively, to investigate their role in mediating BMP13 effects. RESULTS: Exogenous BMP13 upregulated MMP3 in adult and, to a much lesser extent, juvenile cartilage. BMP13 also upregulated NOS2 and MMP13 in adult cartilage. At the biochemical level, BMP13 induced catabolic responses only in adult cartilage, reducing sGAG content and upregulating matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) activity and nitric oxide (NO) production. In juvenile cartilage, BMP13 activation of the SMAD1/5/8 pathway resulted in low levels of MMP activity. Conversely, in adult cartilage, BMP13 activation of SMAD1/5/8 induced NO, while BMP13 activation of ERK1/2 signaling upregulated total MMP activity. CONCLUSIONS: We provide novel findings that age leads to differential activation of BMP13 signaling pathways that regulate pro-inflammatory and catabolic mediators in adult cartilage. These findings suggest a potential age-dependent mechanism in response to BMP13 that promotes alterations in ECM homeostasis and could increase susceptibility to OA development.

articles.title: Characterization and analysis of osseous changes in murine jaws induced by chronic metabolic acidosis.
articles.authors: Emily L Shadron, Laura Doherty, Mikayla M Moody et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Chronic metabolic acidosis (MA) is a growing clinical concern linked to the rising prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD). While MA is known to cause systemic bone loss, its specific effects on craniofacial tissues and the role of sexual dimorphism remain under-investigated. METHODS: Male and female mice were subjected to a chronic acid challenge to model clinical MA. Raman spectroscopy and MicroCT were employed to evaluate the structural and compositional integrity of the maxilla and mandible, focusing on mineral crystallinity, carbonate content, and bone volume fraction. RESULTS: Site-specific analysis revealed the maxilla to be significantly more vulnerable to acid perturbation than the mandible. This compositional shift is consistent with physicochemical mineral dissolution and may reflect alterations in bone remodeling. In contrast, the mandible's denser, more crystalline structure provided relative resilience to acid-induced changes. Furthermore, a significant sexual dimorphism was observed. Females demonstrated greater compositional sensitivity and a more pronounced decrease in mineral:matrix ratio compared to males. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the limitations of applying long-bone models to the craniofacial complex and underscore the need for clinical monitoring of oral health in patients with chronic metabolic disturbances.

articles.title: Arboreal signals in the skeletal proportions of the Gorilla foot.
articles.authors: Elliot G Greiner, Christopher B Ruff, Andrea Lukova et al.
articles.abstract: Postcranial skeletal proportions in living apes have been linked to patterns of arboreal behaviors within and between populations, offering a comparative baseline for interpreting arboreal behavior in fossil hominoids. We quantified metatarsal and proximal phalangeal lengths across all five pedal rays in Gorilla, comparing western lowland gorillas (Gorilla gorilla gorilla), low- and high-elevation Grauer's gorillas (Gorilla beringei graueri), and two ecologically distinct mountain gorilla (Gorilla beringei beringei) populations: those of Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, Uganda, and the Virunga Massif (Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda). The Bwindi sample, assembled from individuals recovered by the Mountain Gorilla Skeletal Project between 2017 and 2025, represents the first substantial pedal dataset for this population. After separately scaling element lengths by estimated body mass and hindlimb length, Bwindi gorillas' third and fourth metatarsal lengths fell consistently between those of the more arboreal western lowland and highly terrestrial Virunga gorillas, while proximal phalangeal and hallux lengths varied little across populations. Additionally, Virunga gorillas showed longer second metatarsals compared to other populations, a feature we link to their strongly terrestrial locomotor habits. In comparing relative manual and pedal element lengths from the same individuals, metacarpals were relatively longer than metatarsals across all populations in rays 2-5, with this pattern reversed in the hallux; among these, only the second ray showed a significant interpopulation difference, with western lowland gorillas exhibiting relatively longer metacarpals than all other groups. Though interpopulation differences in the lengths of pedal elements were generally weaker than those found in the manual elements of the same individuals, these findings suggest that habitat-associated variation in foot morphology can be detected between populations of gorilla subspecies, underscoring the value of fine-grained, population-level skeletal comparisons for refining locomotor inference in the hominoid and hominin fossil record.

articles.title: Suction-feeding performance in invasive alien giant salamanders within the functional framework of Andrias.
articles.authors: M López-Pachón, S Hayashi, J Fortuny et al.
articles.abstract: Hybridisation between Andrias japonicus and A. cf. davidianus lineages is a major conservation concern in Japan, but whether hybrid individuals retain the suction-feeding pattern described for non-hybrid Andrias remains unclear. We analysed suction feeding in six hybrid giant salamanders using 20 captive feeding events recorded with lateral and frontal high-speed videography. Skull, lower jaw, hyobranchial and prey movements were digitised to quantify trajectories, velocities and accelerations during the active expansion phase of prey capture. The hybrids displayed the characteristic suction-feeding sequence described for cryptobranchids, including mandibular opening, hyobranchial expansion, prey acceleration and capture once suction was initiated. Event-level variation occurred in relation to prey position, attack configuration and individual morphometrics, highlighting the flexibility of suction feeding performance among hybrid specimens. Overall, hybrid specimens retained suction-feeding kinematics within the functional pattern previously described for Andrias, suggesting that hybridisation does not disrupt the core biomechanical organisation of prey capture within the functional range examined here. When compared with published data for non-hybrid A. davidianus and A. japonicus, these results indicate a broadly conserved suction feeding mechanism rather than a distinct hybrid-specific feeding mode. Therefore, any potential ecological advantage of hybrids is unlikely to result from a fundamental change in the suction feeding sequence alone.

articles.title: Effects of cues to walk softly and quietly on gait mechanics during load carriage.
articles.authors: Caleb D Johnson, David J Zeppetelli, Cole A Dempsey et al.
articles.abstract: Walking with load carriage is a routine and necessary activity for many occupations and recreational athletes, however it induces significant physical strain, resulting in high rates of musculoskeletal injury. Gait alteration cues to run softly/quietly have been shown to reduce external forces related to injury in runners. However, the effects of these cues have yet to be explored for load carriage. 38 participants completed testing on an instrumented treadmill while kinematics were tracked via optical motion capture. Participants first completed a habitual load carriage trial (HAB) at a self-selected pace (1.23 ± 0.12 m/s) while carrying an 18 kg weighted vest. They were given a 5-min warm-up followed by data collection. Participants were then cued to modify their gait by walking "quietly and softly" (SOFT), using the same pace as for HAB. Outcome variables were averaged across 20 strides, including peak hip/knee/ankle joint internal sagittal and frontal plane moments, peaks/excursion in joint angles, double-stance time, stride length, and cadence. The SOFT condition resulted in decreased second peak hip abduction and peak knee flexion moments, and second peak vertical forces, but increased peak knee extension moments and first peak vertical forces (p < 0.05, Cohen's d≥0.5). Further, the SOFT condition resulted in increased peak flexion angles (hip/knee) and reduced extension/plantarflexion angles (hip/knee/ankle). Given the conflicting changes in external forces, the results do not support SOFT as a modification to reduce overall musculoskeletal injury risk during load carriage.

articles.title: Open and closed-chain shoulder joint position sense: inter-day reliability and normative profiles in male contact sport athletes.
articles.authors: Matthew Slopecki, Edel Fanning, Stacey Kung et al.
articles.abstract: The purpose was to determine inter-day reliability and normative values for open and closed-chain shoulder joint position sense (JPS). Male contact and collision sport athletes (18-40 years) participated in two study phases. Sixteen athletes completed open- and closed-chain JPS tests on two occasions (2-9 days apart) to determine inter-day reliability. Twenty-eight athletes completed the same protocol on one occasion to establish normative profiles. Open-chain JPS was assessed in a standing position using shoulder flexion to pre-defined angles with a laser pointer (55°, 90° and 125° of humerothoracic flexion; no haptic target); closed-chain JPS was assessed in a push-up position by reproducing target positions (chest lowered onto a hurdle at 16.5 cm [low] or 30.5 cm [high]; an initial haptic target). Three-dimensional kinematics quantified repositioning errors. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and standard error of measurement (SEM) were calculated for reliability. Pearson correlations were calculated between open and closed-chain errors. Open-chain tests demonstrated moderate reliability across both arms (ICCs = 0.71-0.74), with better reliability on the dominant limb (ICCs = 0.68-0.90) compared to the non-dominant (ICCs = 0.43-0.55). SEM values ranged from 0.70 to 2.03°. Closed-chain tests showed poor reliability at the high target (ICC = 0.49) but good reliability at the low target (ICC = 0.81, SEM = 10.2 mm). Normative data indicated greater repositioning errors at low targets in open-chain tasks and at high targets in closed-chain tasks. Correlations between open- and closed-chain errors were weak to absent. Open-chain JPS testing demonstrated acceptable reliability, whereas closed-chain reliability was dependent on target height. The two tasks appear to assess distinct aspects of proprioception. The open-chain test reflects predominantly single-joint (glenohumeral) position sense, whereas the closed-chain test reflects multi-joint, composite position sense. These findings establish initial reference values for JPS in male contact athletes.

articles.title: Longitudinal Analysis of Skeletal Muscle and Cardiometabolic Risk During the Menopause Transition.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Hannah E Cabre, Kaja Falkenhain, Steve R Smith et al.
articles.abstract: We assessed longitudinal changes in body composition and cardiometabolic risk in those with normal-weight and overweight/obese women across the menopausal transition. We examined a 10-year longitudinal analysis of 81 healthy women in the prospective Healthy Transitions cohort. Body composition measures were obtained via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Skeletal muscle was estimated using a validated prediction model: 1.12 × appendicular lean mass- 0.63. Serum sex steroid hormones and cardiometabolic factors were quantified in fasting blood. Participants were stratified by BMI into normal weight (n=41) and overweight/obesity (n=40) groups. Changes within and between BMI groups across the menopause transition were assessed with linear mixed models. At menopause onset, compared to those with normal weight, participants with overweight/obesity had lower sex hormone-binding globulin (-30.9±10.3 nmol/L; p=0.01), greater percent body fat (13.1±1.3%; p<0.001), greater skeletal muscle mass (2.5±0.6 kg; p<0.001), and worse cardiometabolic risk factors (p<0.001). In the 5 years before menopause, participants with overweight/obesity gained skeletal muscle (+1.2 kg) and fat mass (+3.5 kg), while participants with normal weight increased percent body fat (+1.5%) only. At menopause onset, women with overweight/obesity exhibit distinct alterations in body composition, hormonal profiles, and cardiometabolic risk that exist in the years preceding menopause, highlighting the importance of early, targeted interventions to mitigate adverse health trajectories during the menopause transition.

articles.title: Acute Sodium Bicarbonate Supplementation Enhances 10-km Outdoor Track Running Performance in Recreational Female Runners.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Selin Aktitiz, Yasemin Güzel, Muhammed Mustafa Atakan et al.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the effects of acute sodium bicarbonate (SB) supplementation co-ingested with a carbohydrate-rich meal on 10-km running performance and gastrointestinal symptoms in recreational female runners under field-based conditions. Twenty-one healthy women (33.6 ± 4.6 years; body mass index 20.8 ± 1.3 kg/m; maximal oxygen uptake 48.6 ± 2.0 ml·kg-1·min-1) completed two 10-km outdoor track running time trials (TTs) in a randomized, double-blind, crossover design. Participants ingested either SB (0.3 g/kg body mass [BM]) or placebo (PLA; 0.03 g/kg BM table salt), together with a standardized carbohydrate-rich meal (1.5 g/kg BM), 90 min before exercise during the same phase of the menstrual cycle. Blood pH, bicarbonate [HCO3-], and [lactate] were measured before, and 1, 3, 5, and 7 min after the TTs; performance time was recorded. Gastrointestinal symptoms were recorded at 30, 60, and 90 min after SB and PLA ingestions. Blood pH (7.47 ± 0.03 vs. 7.42 ± 0.04, p < .001) and [HCO3-] (27.7 ± 1.4 vs. 22.2 ± 1.5 mmol/L, p < .001) were higher at rest and remained elevated postexercise following SB compared with PLA (p < .05 for all time points). TT completion time improved after SB compared with PLA (3,046.1 ± 208.7 s vs. 3,078.4 ± 206.8 s; p = .011). No significant differences in gastrointestinal symptoms scores were observed between conditions (p > .05 for all). In conclusion, acute co-ingestion of 0.3 g/kg of SB with a carbohydrate-rich meal is a practical and well-tolerated strategy to achieve higher resting blood [HCO3-] and pH as well as to improve 10-km TT running performance in recreational female runners.

articles.title: Neuromuscular Fatigue and Recovery: Are Marathon and Trail Running Different?
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Mélanie Metra, Léonard Féasson, Antoine Ravel et al.
articles.abstract: Although trail and road are two running disciplines, they have distinct characteristics potentially leading to different physiological impacts that have never been examined. The aim of the present study was to compare neuromuscular fatigue and recovery between a marathon and two trail runs of equivalent effort (29 km; ± 1,400 m). Forty-one trained runners, specialized in either road or trail running, performed a simulated treadmill marathon (MARASIM), a simulated treadmill trail run (TRAILSIM), or a trail run in natural conditions (TRAILNAT), depending on their speciality. Neuromuscular fatigue, i.e. changes in maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), voluntary activation (VA) and peak twitch (Tw) of the knee extensors (KE) and plantar flexors (PF), blood markers of muscle damage, jump performance, and force-velocity profile (FVP) were assessed before (PRE), immediately after (POST), one (+1 day), two (+2 days), and seven days (+7 days) following the runs. Muscle pain questionnaires were administered at PRE and during the month following the run. MARASIM showed significantly greater decreases in KE VA (-23.5% vs. -9.2% vs. -13.0%) and jump height (-11.7%; +11.4%; +5.9%, for squat jump), and significantly higher increases in blood markers of muscle damage (+1,726 UI.L -1; +641 UI.L -1; +363 UI.L -1; at +1 day) compared to TRAILSIM and TRAILNAT, respectively. The return to baseline occurred later in MARASIM for KE VA and jump height. Muscle soreness values also returned to baseline earlier in TRAILNAT and TRAILSIM compared to MARASIM. No differences between groups existed in KE Pt and MVC, in any PF neuromuscular fatigue variables, and FVP. Overall, marathon running appears to induce greater acute neuromuscular alterations than trail running, mostly on KE, with a slower return to baseline values.

articles.title: Morphological plasticity in the dentition of the lungfish Gnathorhiza from the Permian of Brazil: A population-level geometric morphometric analysis.
articles.authors: Mauro B S Lacerda, Gustavo H N Petreca, Gabriel E B de Barros et al.
articles.abstract: Dental plates are pivotal in the lungfish paleontological record, constituting highly mineralized structures resilient to diagenetic processes. This study provides a detailed description and quantitative shape analysis of 95 newly discovered Gnathorhiza sp. dental plates from the Middle-Late Permian Corumbataí Formation, Brazil. The analyzed sample comprises both upper and lower dentition morphotypes, sharing diagnostic generic features such as straight, sharp, and narrow conical ridges, an obtuse angle between the first and last ridges, a slightly conical lingual border, deep sulci, and an occlusal surface displaying reticulated ornamentation with distinct petrodentine cores. Taphonomic systematization suggests distinct preservation histories for each morphotype, explaining the overrepresentation of upper plates relative to lower ones. To quantitatively evaluate structural variation, landmark-based geometric morphometrics was applied to both upper and lower tooth plates; however, due to a significantly larger sample size, the upper dentition yielded the most robust and biologically significant results. The geometric morphometric analyses revealed substantial morphological variance, particularly localized in the first ridge and first sulcus of the upper plates. Rather than resulting from strict ontogenetic developmental paths or sexual dimorphism, we hypothesize that these predominant morphological differences reflect high phenotypic plasticity within this isolated population. This study confirms the high abundance of Gnathorhiza in the Corumbataí Formation, provides a rigorous assessment of key morphological features in late Paleozoic dipnoan dental plates, and offers insights into the population dynamics of these specialized durophagous predators within a complex Permian mega-lake paleoenvironment.

articles.title: Cardiovascular dietary guidance at an inflection point: the 2025-2030 US dietary guidelines versus the 2026 AHA scientific statement.
articles.authors: Luiz Fernando Sella, Daniela Kanno

articles.title: Fish intake and mortality in Japan, a high fish-consuming country: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies.
articles.authors: Kaori Yokoi, Hyeon-Ki Kim, Ayaka Kato et al.
articles.abstract: Fish consumption has been linked to decreased mortality risk in several prospective studies. However, most existing evidence is based on multi-regional analyses, and the dose-response relationship in populations with high habitual fish intake remains insufficiently characterised. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies among Japanese adults to assess the associations between fish consumption and all-cause and cause-specific mortality and to investigate potential dose-response relationships in a high-fish-intake population. We systematically searched the MEDLINE and Ichushi-Web databases. Prospective cohort studies conducted in Japan that reported hazard ratios or relative risks for fish intake and mortality outcomes were included. The protocol was registered a priori in the PROSPERO database (CRD42025635066). Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled estimates by comparing the highest and lowest intake categories.
