Dose-response relationships were evaluated using generalised least-squares trend estimation and restricted cubic spline models. A total of 113 articles were assessed for eligibility, and 16 studies met the inclusion criteria, and nine were eligible for meta-analysis. Higher fish intake was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.89-0.98) and cardiovascular disease mortality (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.80-0.91), with low heterogeneity. According to the GRADE framework, the certainty of evidence was rated low. Visual inspection suggested that mortality risk reduced with increasing fish intake up to approximately 100 g/day, after which the decline slowed, implying a plateau effect at higher intake levels. Among Japanese adults, high fish consumption was associated with a lower risk of all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality. Further research is required to clarify the dose-response relationship in populations with high fish consumption.

articles.title: Strategies to Manage Missed Appointments in Private Physical Therapy: A National Cross-Sectional Study of Use and Perceived Effectiveness.
articles.authors: Franck Peter, François-Régis Sarhan
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Missed appointments disrupt outpatient care and may be particularly consequential in private physical therapy, where continuity of care, appointment management, and fee-for-service remuneration are closely linked. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify strategies used by private physical therapists to manage missed appointments and assess their perceived effectiveness. DESIGN: This study used a national cross-sectional online survey design. SETTING: The study was conducted in private outpatient physical therapist practice in France. PARTICIPANTS: Participants were physical therapists working in private outpatient practice who completed an anonymous online questionnaire. EXPOSURE: The strategies examined included organizational, communication, and digital reminder strategies used to manage missed appointments. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes included the perceived effectiveness of strategies assessed using a 4-point Likert scale; responses to 3 predefined statements concerning relational and emotional effects; and exploratory association between digital reminder use and perceived overall effectiveness. RESULTS: A total of 1246 physical therapists participated. Online booking platform reminders were rated as effective or very effective by 78.9% of users (95% CI = 74.1%-83.2%), and SMS reminders by 77.7% (95% CI = 72.4%-82.9%). In-clinic posters received lower ratings (20.0%; 95% CI = 16.6%-23.4%). Digital reminder use was weakly associated with higher perceived overall effectiveness (Cramér V = 0.105). Respondents frequently agreed that missed appointments affected their relationship with the patient concerned (82.9%) and that they had experienced frustration or anger after a missed appointment (91.3%); 46.2% agreed that these feelings influenced their interactions with patients more generally. Exploratory content analysis of open-ended responses identified financial deterrents, organizational and reminder strategies, attendance rules, communication and patient education, and restriction or discontinuation of care after repeated absences. CONCLUSIONS: Digital reminders were perceived as the most effective strategies for managing missed appointments, but objective attendance outcomes were not assessed. Relational and emotional findings should be interpreted cautiously because they were based on 3 directionally framed, nonvalidated statements. RELEVANCE: Future studies should evaluate strategies using objective attendance data and balanced measures.

articles.title: Effect of Pain Science Education and Behavioral Graded Activity on Pain in Survivors of Breast Cancer: A Study Protocol for a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Astrid Lahousse, Eva Roose, Laurence Leysen et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Pain affects up to half of survivors of breast cancer and is one of the most common long-term consequences of cancer treatment, yet it remains under-recognized and undertreated. Pharmacological options often provide limited relief and may cause adverse effects. Evidence from other pain populations supports a biopsychosocial approach combining pain education and physical activity. OBJECTIVE: The objective is to evaluate whether pain science education (PSE) with behavioral graded activity (BGA) versus usual care (UC), reduces pain intensity and interference in survivors of breast cancer with pain. Secondary aims include assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and central pain modulation. DESIGN: This study is a multicenter, two-arm, assessor- and statistician-blinded, randomized controlled superiority trial. SETTING: The trial will be conducted in Belgium, with interventions delivered in hospital and academic research settings. PARTICIPANTS: Two hundred women with a history of breast cancer and persistent pain will be recruited. INTERVENTIONS: Participants will be randomized to either (1) PSE (1 session) plus 5 BGA sessions delivered by a trained physical therapist, or (2) usual care with a standardized biomedical pain information leaflet, over a 12-week period. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome will be pain intensity and interference (Brief Pain Inventory). Secondary outcomes will include HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30) and central pain modulation (Quantitative Sensory Testing). Exploratory outcomes include sleep, fatigue, pain-related cognitions, and health care utilization. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and at 3-month (primary endpoint), 1-year, and 2-year follow-ups. CONCLUSIONS: This trial will determine whether a structured PSE+BGA program improves pain and HRQoL in survivors of breast cancer, offering a potential scalable non-pharmacological treatment. RELEVANCE: These findings may guide targeted rehabilitation strategies and strengthen the role of physical therapists in managing post-cancer pain, particularly in light of the growing population of survivors of breast cancer and the increasing prevalence of persistent symptoms.

articles.title: On "Effects of sub-symptom threshold aerobic exercise on persistent postconcussion symptom burden and exercise intolerance: a randomized controlled trial." Valaas LJ, Soberg HL, Rasmussen MS, et al. Phys Ther. 2026;106(6):pzag049. https://doi.org/10.1093/ptj/pzag049.
articles.authors: Cyril James Williamson

articles.title: Critical appraisal of D3-creatine dilution method for skeletal muscle mass measurement.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Sri Lakshmi S Devarakonda, Carla M Prado, Steven B Heymsfield
articles.abstract: The D3-creatine dilution method is gaining rapid momentum as a tool for quantifying skeletal muscle mass (SMM), with emerging discourse positioning it as a reference standard and influencing peer-review and funding decisions. A critical appraisal of the method's current stage of development is therefore timely and necessary. We reviewed the current D3-creatine dilution method as now widely applied, its foundational assumptions, available validation studies comparing estimates against magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and sources of measurement error, including variability in the assumed skeletal muscle creatine concentration and isotope spillage correction. Only 4 studies with 102 total adult participants varying in sex (78 males), age, activity level (49 athletes), and health status have evaluated the current D3-creatine dilution SMM prediction model against MRI as the reference; mean group differences ranged from -13.8% to 20.9%, lending scant support for the validity of the current approach. The one longitudinal validation study (n = 14) reported wide limits of agreement, ±7 kg for D3-creatine compared with ±1.5 kg for MRI, raising concerns about the method's sensitivity to detect small changes in SMM. Isotope spillage correction algorithms, developed in 1 sample (n = 36), similarly require additional development and validation. Although D3-creatine dilution has potential as a new approach that can add to the multiple currently available SMM estimation methods, characterization as a reference standard for quantifying SMM is premature. Validation studies across well-defined cross-sectional and longitudinal samples varying widely in sex, age, diet, and health characteristics are needed to establish the D3-creatine dilution method's accuracy and generalizability.

articles.title: Blood lactate concentrations are associated with markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Regis C Pearson, Destiny P Hamilton, Nicholas T Broskey et al.
articles.abstract: The ability to detect metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy can impact the health of mother and infant(s). Lactate may serve as a biomarker to predict metabolic dysfunction risk. The purpose of this study was to determine if fasting or postprandial blood lactate concentrations were related to established markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy. Overnight fasted healthy women between 32-38 weeks gestation underwent a high-fat meal test. Fasted and postprandial (1h, 2h, and 4h) venous blood glucose, insulin, and lactate were collected. Fasted and postprandial (2h and 4h) respiratory exchange ratios (RERs) were assessed by indirect calorimetry. HOMA-IR and Matsuda indexes were calculated. Participants were categorized into lean (18.5-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), or obese (≥30.0 kg/m2) based on pre-pregnancy body mass index. To determine the impact that weight status may have on postprandial lactate concentrations, a repeated-measures analysis of variance was performed on log-transformed data. Spearman's rank-order correlation coefficients were used to assess associations between outcome variables. 52 participants were included in the analysis (lean, n = 29; overweight, n = 11; obese, n = 12). Postprandial lactate was higher in women with obesity compared to women who were lean (1h, p = 0.024; 2h, p = 0.025; 4h, p = 0.010). Among all women, higher lactate area under the curve (AUC) was associated with higher insulin AUC, higher HOMA-IR index, lower Matsuda index, and higher RER AUC (p ≤ 0.003). These findings suggest that postprandially elevated lactate may serve as a useful biomarker for identifying metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy.

articles.title: Discharge Decision Making and the Contemporary Weighting of Clinical and Contextual Factors: A Survey of Acute Care Physical Therapists.
articles.authors: James P Crick, Thomas Gus Almonroeder, Tricia Widenhoefer
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Physical therapists routinely make discharge recommendations for patients in the hospital, yet the reasoning that drives these decisions is poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to describe contemporary acute care physical therapists' discharge reasoning and examine associations between reasoning constructs and recommended discharge intensity. DESIGN: This study used a cross-sectional clinical vignette-based survey. Therapists provided a discharge recommendation and supporting rationale. Free-text rationales were analyzed using directed content analysis, and quantitative associations between coded reasoning constructs and discharge recommendation intensity were examined using regression modeling. SETTING: The survey was conducted electronically with United States physical therapists practicing in hospitals. PARTICIPANTS: Participants were eighty-nine acute care physical therapists who completed discharge recommendations and free-text rationales for 10 vignettes. INTERVENTIONS: none. MAIN OUTCOMES: The three main outcomes for this study included: (1) Frequency and co-occurrence of coded reasoning constructs; (2) therapist-level reasoning profiles; and (3) associations between constructs and discharge intensity. RESULTS: Across 1604 construct code applications, 3 constructs dominated discharge reasoning: therapist prior experience (29.6%), patient functioning and disability (26.3%), and patient life context (25.3%). The majority (69.7%) of therapists demonstrated mixed reasoning patterns while less than one-third demonstrated a dominant reasoning profile. Patient functioning and disability was the only construct statistically associated with recommending more intensive post-acute care in ordered (OR = 1.70; 95% CI = 1.22-2.39) and binary (OR = 2.21; 95% CI = 1.30-3.74) models. CONCLUSIONS: Acute care discharge reasoning concentrates on functional status, professional experience, and patient life context, with other domains functioning mainly as situational amplifiers. RELEVANCE: A refined framework for discharge reasoning may support clearer interdisciplinary communication, inform targeted education, and guide efforts to optimize post-acute care utilization.

articles.title: Extrinsic risk factors for tendinopathy: bridging the basic and clinical research divide.
articles.authors: Tyler C Williams, Grant E Garrigues, Lisa G M Friedman et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Tendon injuries frequently affect the Achilles, rotator cuff, and the tendons of the wrist extensors originating at the lateral epicondyle. Until recently, terms for tendon degeneration, disease, and injuries were debated between the basic research and clinical communities, creating barriers to advances in knowledge. Aside from acute traumatic rupture in healthy tendon, in the current 'omic age, most tendon disease, including ruptures in chronic disease, exists along a tendinopathy spectrum. While intrinsic factors such as sex, genetics, and aging are unmodifiable, extrinsic factors impact tendon health, and have been extensively evaluated in both basic and clinical research. However, these fields do not always ask aligned research questions, leading to unanticipated gaps in understanding the impact of extrinsic factors on tendon health. The aim of this study was to provide a detailed and cohesive review of these gaps between current clinical and basic science research. METHODS: We analyzed extrinsic risk factors for tendinopathy by searching PubMed utilizing search terms related to tendinopathy, various anatomic sites, and various extrinsic risk factors. Reviewed literature was separated into basic science and clinical research. Current knowledge was summarized and gaps identified between fields. RESULTS: Several extrinsic risk factors are directly connected to the onset of tendinopathy whether through upregulation of systemic inflammatory mediators or direct effects on tendon structure and function. CONCLUSIONS: There is much work to be done to explain the mechanisms of action highlighted by clinical data, particularly when considering the complexity of disease and associated comorbidity.

articles.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation interventions for kinesiophobia after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Hongbo Wen, Ting Zhang, Tingting Xie et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Affecting 21-35% of patients after total knee arthroplasty (TKA), kinesiophobia critically impedes postoperative rehabilitation. Whether exercise-based interventions reduce kinesiophobia more effectively than routine postoperative rehabilitation remains unclear. METHODS: We systematically searched 11 databases from inception to July 11, 2026, for RCTs comparing exercise-based rehabilitation with routine postoperative rehabilitation in adults undergoing primary TKA. The primary outcome was kinesiophobia. Secondary outcomes included knee function, pain, balance, mobilization time, and adherence. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Eleven RCTs (N = 1,096) were included. Exercise-based rehabilitation was associated with a reduction in kinesiophobia (SMD = - 1.22, 95% CI [- 1.72, - 0.72]; I2 = 93%; low certainty) and improvements in knee function (SMD = 1.19, 95% CI [0.67, 1.71]; I2 = 93%; low certainty). For pain, the ≤ 4-week pooled estimate (SMD = - 1.09, 95% CI [- 2.03, - 0.14]; I2 = 94%) was not interpretable due to extreme heterogeneity and was not robust: after exclusion of the single acute in-hospital trial, the confidence interval crossed zero (SMD = - 1.09, 95% CI [- 2.28, 0.09]). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses otherwise supported the directional conclusions for kinesiophobia and knee function, although effect sizes were unstable and certainty remained low. CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that exercise-based rehabilitation may be associated with reductions in kinesiophobia at ≤ 4 weeks and an interpretable 12-week improvement in knee function after TKA; the ≤ 4-week and ≥ 24-week functional subgroup estimates were not interpretable because of extreme heterogeneity, and the early pain signal was possible but non-robust. Effect sizes should be interpreted with caution due to substantial heterogeneity, risk of bias, and sensitivity to outlying studies. Well-designed, multicenter RCTs with rigorous blinding and standardized protocols are urgently needed.

articles.title: Fluid Balance, Sweat Na+ Losses and Carbohydrate Intake in Elite Male Soccer Players Training in Cool Environments.
articles.authors: Vlad Sabou, Heather Z Macrae, Kevin Mulholland et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Hypohydration increases physiological strain and reduces physical and technical soccer performance. Nonetheless, there are limited data on fluid balance responses in elite soccer players training in cool environments. This study investigated sweat and fluid/carbohydrate intake responses in elite male professional soccer players training at a high intensity in cool environments. METHODS: Fluid/sodium (Na+) losses and ad libitum carbohydrate/fluid intake of thirty-six elite male soccer players were measured as part of four training sessions, with each player completing the measurements once. Data were collected under the following conditions classified by ambient temperature (11.3 ± 2.1 °C), wet bulb globe temperature (9.8 ± 3.0 °C), and relative humidity (76.8 ± 10.2%). Mean duration of training sessions was 70 ± 4 min and included soccer-specific training, with players covering a mean total distance of 7054 ± 654 m and 104 ± 9 (m·min-1). Before and after exercise, players were weighed in minimal clothing. During training breaks, players had ad libitum access to carbohydrate beverages and water. Sweat [Na+] (mmol·L-1) was measured by absorbent patches positioned on the upper back. RESULTS: Two out of eleven players displayed a USG score indicative of 'minimal hypohydration' (1.022 and 1.022, respectively). Seventeen percent of players experienced hypohydration > 2% of pre-exercise body mass. Mean sweat rate was 1.5 ± 0.4 L·h-1, with individual sweat rates ranging from 0.4-2.2 L·h-1 (outfield players, n = 33). Goalkeepers mean sweat rate was 0.7 ± 0.2 L·h-1 (range 0.6-0.9 L·h-1, n = 3). Sweat [Na+] also varied substantially between players (range 21-49 mmol·L-1), with a mean sweat [Na+] of 35 ± 6.8 mmol·L-1. There was a significant positive correlation between sodium chloride loss and intensity of play (m·min-1) covered during training (rs = 0.368, p = 0.049). Carbohydrate ingestion during training varied between individuals (range 0-25 g·h-1). CONCLUSIONS: Sweat rate and sweat sodium chloride loss varies in elite soccer players during high-intensity training in cool environments. Hypohydration exceeded 2% pre-exercise body mass in 17% of players. The ad libitum carbohydrate intake of the players was below recommendations given the intensity and duration of the training sessions.

articles.title: How to Implement a Ketogenic Diet Therapy in Developing Countries: Colombian Consensus on Ketogenic Diet Therapy Use in the Management of Adults with Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
articles.authors: Jean Paul Vergara-Aguilar, Angélica Lizcano, Adriana Martinez-Perez et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Drug-resistant epilepsy affects up to one-third of patients with epilepsy and is associated with higher morbidity, mortality, trauma events, psychosocial challenges, and decline in quality of life. In Latin America, disease burden is high and access to advanced therapies remains limited. Ketogenic Diet Therapy (KDT) has been shown to be beneficial in adults, but its implementation requires standardized protocols and experienced multidisciplinary teams. This study aimed to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations to guide the indication, implementation, and follow-up of KDT in adults with drug-resistant epilepsy through expert consensus in Colombia. METHODS: A modified version of the Nominal Group Technique was used to develop, discuss, and vote on management concepts. Clinical questions were structured using the PICO framework. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed and EMBASE for articles published since 2015, and the evidence was integrated with the experience of a multidisciplinary expert panel. RESULTS: Twelve recommendations were issued, covering commercial formulas, induction and follow-up protocols, individualized dietary interventions, safety, diagnostic support, nutritional supplementation, and drug-diet interactions. The consensus highlights the need for interdisciplinary teams, structured education, early adherence strategies, and close follow-up, and the role of enteral emergency formulas in intensive care settings. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence around KDT shows it can be implemented safely as an adjunctive treatment for adults with drug-resistant epilepsy and is reasonable to consider following the failure of two adequate antiseizure medications. Structured implementation may reduce seizure frequency, improve quality of life, and reduce the pharmacological burden. Multicenter prospective studies are needed to further assess efficacy, safety, and resource utilization. These recommendations contribute to closing the gap between evidence and clinical practice.

articles.title: Self-Related Cognitive Schemas, Negative Self-View, and Perceived Psychosocial Burden in Adults with Celiac Disease: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Kinga Kot, Ola Sobieska-Poszwa, Agnieszka Dobrowolska et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Self-related cognitive schemas may influence psychological adaptation to chronic illness. However, their role in adults with celiac disease (CD) remains poorly understood. We aimed to assess cognitive schemas and depressive symptoms in adults with CD compared with healthy controls, and to examine their associations with perceived disease burden. Methods: This cross-sectional comparative study included 96 adults with CD and 96 healthy controls. Participants completed the Cognitive Triad Inventory (CTI) and Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), and sociodemographic and clinical data were collected. Perceived disease- and diet-related burden was assessed using investigator-developed single-item measures. Results: The mean age at CD diagnosis was 33.6 (SD 13.4) years, and the mean duration of symptoms before diagnosis was 5.4 (SD 5.1) years. Adults with CD reported higher depressive symptom scores than healthy controls (8.4 (SD 7.9) vs. 6.6 (SD 8.0); Mann-Whitney U = 3850.5, Z = 1.99, Cohen's d = 0.29, p = 0.046). No significant between-group differences were observed in total CTI scores or its Self-view, World-view, or Future-view subscales. After adjustment for age, sex, educational level, marital status, and employment status, neither BDI nor CTI scores were independently associated with group membership. Exploratory bivariate analyses within the CD group showed that higher Self-view scores were associated with lower perceived negative impact of gluten-free diet requirements on family life (rS = -0.29, p = 0.004) and lower perceived impact of CD symptoms and disease exacerbations on everyday life (rS = -0.31, p = 0.002). These associations remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Conclusions: Adults with CD reported slightly higher depressive symptom levels than healthy controls, whereas cognitive schemas did not differ significantly between groups. The observed associations between CTI Self-view and selected indicators of perceived disease- and diet-related burden warrant further investigation, but do not establish a causal contribution of self-view to disease burden.

articles.title: Baseline Food Supply-Based Dietary Scores and Ischemic Heart Disease Mortality: A Longitudinal Cross-Country Study.
articles.authors: Saya Nosaka, Fumiya Kawase, Tomoko Imai et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: National food environments may be associated with cardiovascular risk, but how their association with country-level ischemic heart disease (IHD) mortality differs across diet-quality indices remains unclear. We compared six food supply-based dietary scores calculated using 2010 food data in relation to annual IHD mortality from 2010 to 2021. Methods: We conducted a longitudinal study of 148 countries with populations ≥ 1 million. Using 2010 FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheet data, we calculated the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) score, the Alternative Healthy Eating Index (AHEI), Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS), Traditional Japanese Diet Score (TJDS), Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI), and Quantitative Index for Dietary Diversity (QUANTIDD). The outcome was age-standardized IHD mortality during 2010-2021. Associations between time-invariant baseline dietary scores and annual IHD mortality were assessed using multivariable-adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Effect sizes were expressed as mortality rate ratios (MRRs) per 1-standard deviation (SD) higher score; model fit was compared using Akaike information criterion (AIC) weights and marginal R2, and effect estimates were compared pairwise. Results: Higher DASH and AHEI scores were associated with lower IHD mortality. MRRs per 1-SD higher score were 0.914 (95% confidence interval, 0.849-0.983) for DASH and 0.908 (95% confidence interval, 0.838-0.985) for AHEI. No significant associations were observed for MDS, TJDS, PHDI, or QUANTIDD. DASH had the highest AIC weight (0.434), followed by AHEI (0.341), with a slightly higher marginal R2 for DASH. Pairwise comparisons showed no statistically significant differences in effect estimates between DASH and AHEI or between either of these scores and the other dietary scores. Conclusions: Higher baseline DASH and AHEI scores were associated with lower IHD mortality during 2010-2021, with similar effect estimates per 1-SD higher score and broadly comparable model fit. However, direct pairwise comparisons revealed no statistically significant differences in standardized effect sizes between these scores (DASH and AHEI) and the other dietary scores. These findings suggest that the relevance of dietary scores may depend on the outcome and analytic context rather than the superiority of a single index. Because this was an ecological study, these findings should not be interpreted as individual-level causal effects.

articles.title: Use of Botanical Ingredients Relevant to Premenstrual Symptoms and Dysmenorrhea Among Elite Female Athletes: Evidence from Doping Control Forms.
articles.authors: Dominika Granda, Andrzej Pokrywka, Maria Karolina Szmidt et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) and dysmenorrhea can impair training performance in female athletes. Botanical ingredients are commonly used to manage these conditions in the general population, but it is unknown whether elite female athletes do so. This study aimed to identify botanical ingredients evaluated in studies for PMS and dysmenorrhea and determine whether elite female athletes declared them on Doping Control Forms (DCFs). METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted to identify botanical ingredients evaluated in studies for PMS and dysmenorrhea. Then, DCFs completed during routine anti-doping testing among elite athletes in Poland (2018-2023) were analyzed for declarations of these ingredients, both directly and as components of multi-ingredient products. The proportion of DCFs containing these ingredients was compared between female (n = 4451 DCFs) and male athletes (n = 9068 DCFs; reference) using chi-squared tests. RESULTS: The review identified 8 and 21 botanical ingredients with evidence for PMS and dysmenorrhea, respectively; of which 9 were detected in DCFs. The most commonly declared ingredients among female athletes were ginger and turmeric/curcuminoid (1.75% and 1.26%, respectively, both studied for PMS and dysmenorrhea). Chasteberry, on the other hand, with the most extensive, albeit low-confidence evidence, for PMS, was rarely declared (0.22%). Direct declaration of ginkgo, valerian, evening primrose oil, and chasteberry was significantly more common among female than male athletes (0.22% vs. 0.02%, 0.36% vs. 0.03%, 0.47% vs. 0.03%, 0.22% vs. 0.02%; adjusted p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Declarations of botanical ingredients studied for PMS and dysmenorrhea were infrequent on DCFs completed by female athletes. Because DCFs do not record the reason for use, these data cannot establish whether declarations reflected treatment of menstrual symptoms; studies assessing indication, symptom status and motivation are needed.

articles.title: Transition from open surgery to ultrasound-guided minimally invasive surgery for insertional Achilles tendinopathy: similar patient-reported outcomes and substantially lower treatment costs.
articles.authors: Louise Lindén, Håkan Alfredson, Maziar Mohaddes et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy is commonly treated surgically when conservative management fails. Traditionally, open central-splitting surgery (OCS) has been the standard approach, but minimally invasive ultrasound-guided techniques have recently been introduced. This study compared patient-reported outcomes and treatment costs following a transition in surgical practice from open central-splitting surgery to ultrasound- and colour Doppler-guided minimally invasive wide-awake local anaesthesia no tourniquet (WALANT) surgery. METHODS: This retrospective historical cohort study included fifty-two consecutive patients with insertional Achilles tendinopathy. Twenty patients underwent OCS surgery during 2017-2019, followed by thirty-two patients who underwent US-/CD-guided WALANT surgery during 2020-2022. The primary clinical outcome was the SEFAS score at 12 months. Between-group differences in the 12-month SEFAS scores were analysed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for baseline SEFAS score, age, sex, and BMI. Direct medical costs were estimated from the resource use observed across the two treatment pathways. RESULTS: The mean SEFAS score improved from 18 at baseline to 40 at 12 months in the US-/CD group and from 23 to 41 in the OCS group. In the adjusted analysis, the mean difference in the 12-month SEFAS was 0.62 points in favour of US-/CD (95% CI, - 3.50 to 4.73). Estimated direct medical costs were $1,432 per patient for US-/CD and $3,343 for OCS, corresponding to an absolute reduction of $1,911 per patient and approximately 50% lower costs with the US-/CD treatment pathway. CONCLUSIONS: Following a transition in surgical practice, US-/CD-guided surgery was associated with similar 12-month patient-reported outcomes and approximately 50% lower direct medical costs compared with OCS surgery. These findings suggest that minimally invasive US-/CD-guided surgery under local anaesthesia may offer a less resource-intensive alternative for the surgical treatment of insertional Achilles tendinopathy. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Preoperative factors associated with quadriceps strength 1 year after total knee arthroplasty: a prospective longitudinal study.
articles.authors: Per Sjöström, Lena Nordeman, Ola Rolfson et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Quadriceps strength is highly related to physical function following total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Preoperative factors associated with long-term postoperative strength remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this exploratory study was to investigate preoperative factors associated with normalized quadriceps strength (NQS), changes in NQS and limb symmetry index (LSI) 1 year after TKA in patients with uncomplicated recovery. METHODS: A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Measurements took place at three primary care rehabilitation facilities in Region Västra Götaland, Sweden. The final analysis included 39 participants aged 65 years or older who underwent elective fast-track primary TKA due to knee osteoarthritis and had an uncomplicated recovery. Preoperative factors associated with NQS in the operated limb after 1 year (n = 39), changes in NQS from preoperative testing to 1 year after TKA (n = 39), and LSI (n = 35) were analyzed in three separate exploratory multiple linear regression models. Preoperative factors included age, sex, NQS, the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), and the LSI. RESULTS: Preoperative NQS (B = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.40 to 1.0, p < 0.001) and LSI (B = - 0.17, 95% CI: - 0.29 to - 0.037, p = 0.013) were significantly associated with NQS 1 year after TKA. LSI was the only preoperative factor significantly associated with changes in NQS (B = - 0.19, 95% CI: - 0.32 to - 0.059, p = 0.006) and LSI 1 year after TKA (B = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.15 to 0.68, p = 0.004). CONCLUSIONS: In this selected and relatively small sample, greater normalized quadriceps strength in the operated limb and higher LSI 1 year after TKA appeared to be primarily associated with higher preoperative normalized quadriceps strength in the operated limb and higher preoperative LSI, respectively, whereas strength gains appeared to be associated with lower preoperative LSI. The findings should be considered exploratory and primarily applicable to older adults with uncomplicated recovery after TKA. Confirmation in larger studies is warranted. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Retrospectively registered February 9, 2022 ( http://clinicaltrials.gov , ID: NCT05248815).

articles.title: Comparing the coherent point drift algorithm to sliding semilandmark and weighted spherical harmonic whole-bone three-dimensional shape analyses.
articles.authors: Christine M Harper, Isabella F X Araiza, Deanna M Goldstein
articles.abstract: The ability to quantify 3D morphologies is critical for anatomical research; however, setting up high-density landmark sets and positioning them on all specimens can represent a substantial challenge. The coherent point drift (CPD) algorithm, a technique for registering two point clouds based on the Gaussian mixture model, was recently used to investigate human variation; however, its performance has yet to be compared to other 3D shape analysis methods. Here we compare the results of a CPD analysis to a sliding semilandmark and weighted spherical harmonic (SPHARM) analysis of the same 60 human and African ape calcanei and a CPD analysis and SPHARM-sliding analysis (a combination SPHARM and sliding semilandmark analysis) of 40 primate third manual proximal phalanges (mPP3s) to determine methodological comparability. Additionally, we run a CPD analysis on a small but wide-ranging sample of primate ulnae to demonstrate its utility for proximodistally long and mediolaterally narrow long bones. All specimens were surface or micro-CT scanned. All calcanei were subjected to a CPD analysis with 2000 semilandmarks, a sliding semilandmark analysis with 1007 semilandmarks, and a SPHARM analysis. All mPP3s underwent a CPD analysis with 2500 semilandmarks and a SPHARM-sliding analysis with 2562 semilandmarks. For the ulna, a CPD analysis with 1252 semilandmarks was run. Shape variation for all analyses was summarized using (separate) principal component analyses (PCAs). Results of the respective analyses for the calcaneus and mPP3 were compared by calculating the maximum and root mean square distances (RMSD) between average taxon shape configurations (scaled based on centroid size) generated from each analysis. All three calcaneus analyses separate taxa along the first two PCs, with humans separating from African apes along PC1 and chimpanzees and gorillas separating across PC2. For the two mPP3 analyses, the three great ape taxa consistently separate along PC1, and Papio separates from the other taxa along PC2. The average RMSD between CPD and sliding semilandmark analyses for the calcaneus was 0.24 mm, and 0.21 mm between CPD and SPHARM analyses. For the mPP3, the average RMSD between CPD and SPHARM-sliding was 0.14 mm. These results indicate that CPD is a comparable 3D shape analysis method to these other approaches. The CPD analysis was also able to place a semilandmark set on primate ulnae ranging from gorillas to tarsiers and capture morphological variations including shaft curvature, relative olecranon process length, and overall robusticity. CPD analyses are less time intensive than sliding semilandmark analyses; however, the sliding semilandmark analysis was better able to capture variation surrounding the borders of the articular facets (although differences were relatively minor), suggesting that these analyses may be better suited when the researcher is interested in a specific anatomical feature. CPD did capture edges better than SPHARM analyses; however, this is likely not an issue for small, relatively round bones such as carpals and most tarsals. In sum, CPD produces similar results to sliding semilandmark, SPHARM, and SPHARM-sliding approaches and has benefits for analyses of long bones with complex morphologies or among taxa that exhibit large amounts of morphological variation.

articles.title: What characteristics are associated with meeting the Canadian physical activity guidelines for people with multiple sclerosis? A retrospective chart review.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jillian Scandiffio, Sarah Munce, Sarah J Donkers et al.
articles.abstract: Meeting multiple sclerosis-specific physical activity guidelines (PAGs) has been associated with numerous benefits in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). However, the characteristics of PwMS predictive of meeting PAGs are unknown. This study aimed to examine which sociodemographic and clinical characteristics are associated with meeting the Canadian MS PAGs. A retrospective chart review of all PwMS referred to physiatry at the largest Canadian tertiary MS clinic between December 2021-December 2023 (n=455) was conducted. Physical activity, sociodemographic, and clinical characteristics were collected. Physical activity levels were categorized into one of three groups: no activity, some activity but not meeting PAGs, and meeting PAGs. Physical activity was further categorized by type of activity (aerobic and strength training). Associations between characteristics and physical activity levels were examined using multinomial logistic regression. PwMS who did not drive (OR=0.53, 95%CI=0.29-0.97) and were non-ambulatory (OR=0.34, 95%CI 0.11-0.99) were significantly less likely to meet PAGs. Higher Expanded Disability Status Scale (OR=0.80, 95% CI=0.70-0.91), gait aid use (OR=0.55, 95%CI=0.34-0.88), incoordination (OR= 0.52, 95% CI=0.33-0.82), progressive MS phenotype (OR=0.60, 95% CI=0.37-0.95), and smoking (OR=0.31, 95% CI=0.13-0.76) were associated with lower odds of doing any aerobic activity. Those with cognitive symptoms (OR=1.93, 95%CI=1.22-3.04) and greater muscle strength (OR=1.04, 95% CI=1.01-1.07) were more likely to do aerobic activity. Only employment status was associated with strength training, with those employed more likely to do some strength training (OR=1.73, 95% CI=1.04-2.89). Physical disability, cognitive symptoms, adverse health behaviours may drive which type and amount of activity a PwMS participates in.

articles.title: Determining the association between gender-related factors and the perception of exertional dyspnoea in healthy males and females.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jasvir K Dhaliwal, Jack R Dunsford, Gracie O Grift et al.
articles.abstract: The perception exertional dyspnoea is greater in females than males at absolute, but not relative, levels of minute ventilation (VE). The mechanisms of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea are unclear, but since dyspnoea perception is influenced by psychological, social, and cultural factors, it is possible that gender-related characteristics confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea. We sought to determine the association between gender-related characteristics and dyspnoea during exercise in males and females. Forty-six healthy adults (n=22 males, n=24 females) completed the Stanford Gender-related Variables for Health Research questionnaire to assess their gender-related characteristics (i.e., caregiver strain, work strain, independence, risk-taking, emotional intelligence, social support, and discrimination), spirometry, and an incremental cycle exercise test. Throughout exercise, standard cardiorespiratory parameters were monitored, and dyspnoea perception was assessed using the Borg scale. Females had significantly higher scores than males for emotional intelligence (p=0.029) and social support (p=0.049); whereas other gender-related characteristics were similar between the sexes (all p>0.05). Females reported significantly higher dyspnoea intensity and unpleasantness ratings than males at a V̇E of 80 l·min-1 (both p<0.05); however, males had higher dyspnoea intensity ratings at 20 and 40 % of maximum voluntary ventilation (MVV; both p<0.05). After adjusting for sex, height, body mass, and age, emotional intelligence was significantly associated with dyspnoea intensity at a V̇E of 50 l·min-1 and 50 %MVV (R2=0.14-0.18, all p<0.05). Our findings suggest that gender-related characteristics influence the perception of exertional dyspnoea, and may confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea perception.

articles.title: Surgical Profiles of Elite Female Athletes and Their Association with Long-Term Musculoskeletal Health: Findings from the Women's Soccer Health Study.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Kai-Lun Law, Polly de Mille, Heidi Prather et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the career and post-career surgeries in female elite-level soccer players and evaluate their association with long-term musculoskeletal health. STUDY DESIGN: This is a cross-sectional study. METHODS: Surgical data (the number and type of surgeries during and after the career) from an anonymous online survey was obtained from a previously published cohort of 560 retired elite women's soccer players. Correlation coefficients were used to evaluate the relationship between the number of surgeries and physical activity levels (UCLA activity scale), joint function (SANE), and physical and mental health (PROMIS-10), which were all collected on the same survey. RESULTS: The average number of career surgeries was 1 (SD=1.6), and the average number of post-career surgeries was 0.5 (SD=1). The most common career surgery sites for women's soccer players were knee (39%), foot/ankle (12%), and leg (4%). The most common knee procedures involved ligament reconstruction, primarily of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), followed by meniscus and cartilage surgery. The most frequent post-career surgery sites were knee (24.0%), foot/ankle (5.1%), and leg (3.2%). Knee ligament and meniscus surgeries were equally reported. More career and post-career surgeries were associated with lower SANE knee scores (p<0.001). Lower SANE knee scores (p=0.017) were associated with lower UCLA activity levels. CONCLUSIONS: The locations of career and post-career surgeries were similar, suggesting a possible association with long-term musculoskeletal impairment, particularly to the knee, in a cohort of mostly White collegiate former players. Having more soccer-related surgeries was associated with reduced joint function and activity levels after retirement, though the correlations were weak or moderate. These findings suggest the need for the development of preventive interventions that address the specific needs of female athletes, implementation of injury prevention programs and strategies to maximize adherence, and long-term musculoskeletal assessments of players after retirement.

articles.title: Dietary Supplement Use and Beliefs Among Athletes at the 2025 Canada Games.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jana Daher, Adriah Kate Sahajpal, Vijay Sahajpal et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary supplement use is widespread among athletes; however, limited data exist regarding supplement use and beliefs among Canadian youth athletes. This cross-sectional online study aimed to examine dietary supplement use and related beliefs among athletes competing at the 2025 Canada Games in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador. A total of 473 respondents participated in the survey. Of the 473 participants, 385 completed responses to the dietary supplement (DS) questions. Among participants who reported their sex, 125 were male and 189 were female. Overall, 36% of participants reported current dietary supplement use. Supplement use was significantly higher among males than females (47% vs. 23%, p < .001) and increased with age (p = .001). The most commonly reported supplements were protein powder (49%), sports drinks (46%), and creatine (45%). Primary reasons for use included maintaining good health (76%), increasing energy (54%), and promoting recovery (50%). Coaches (50%) and healthcare professionals (49%) were the most frequently reported information sources. Supplement users demonstrated significantly stronger positive beliefs regarding benefits of dietary supplements compared with non-users (all p < .001). Ordinal logistic regression showed that supplement users had greater odds of stronger agreement that supplements improve performance (OR = 5.50, 95% CI: 3.31-9.13, p < .001). These findings highlight the use of dietary supplements among Canadian youth athletes and support the need for targeted nutrition education to promote informed decision-making.

articles.title: Passive Hyperthermia Increases Neural Recruitment, Thereby Reducing Processing Efficiency During Executive Task Performance.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Manabu Shibasaki, Shigehiko Ogoh, Kanoko Ito et al.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Heat-induced hyperthermia impairs cognitive performance and contributes to central fatigue during exercise and environmental heat exposure. Electroencephalographic event-related potential (EEG-ERP) studies consistently show reduced P300 amplitudes under heat stress, whereas functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies often report expanded blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) activation. PURPOSE: This study examined how passive hyperthermia influences task-dependent neural activation and cognitive processing using both fMRI and EEG-ERP within comparable paradigms. METHODS: Eighteen healthy adults (ten males and eight females) performed Go/No-go and Flanker tasks under normothermic and hyperthermic conditions during fMRI. Passive heating increased external ear canal temperature (Tear) by approximately 1.1°C above baseline. Sixteen participants completed an additional EEG-ERP session with the Flanker task. Behavioral responses, regional BOLD activation, and P300 amplitude and latency were assessed. Cervical arterial blood flow was measured by using a color-coded ultrasound system. RESULTS: The mean heating duration was 53.9 ± 9.2 min across all subjects. Hyperthermia increased heart rate and Tear while reducing internal carotid and vertebral artery blood flow. Reaction times decreased in both tasks, with no change in error rates. fMRI showed expanded activation in bilateral frontal, parietal, temporal, and subcortical regions. Task subtraction analyses (Flanker minus Go/No-go) revealed greater frontal and parietal activation during the complex task. In contrast, P300 amplitude was reduced during hyperthermia. CONCLUSION: Passive hyperthermia expands the spatial extent task-related BOLD activation while reducing P300 amplitude, suggesting reduced processing efficiency. However, the BOLD findings should be interpreted with caution because cerebral perfusion was also reduced. These findings suggest increased neural strain under heat stress, contributing to central fatigue and potentially impairing decision-making in sport and occupational setting.

articles.title: Joint-specific kinematic deviations in asymptomatic flatfoot using biplane fluoroscopy.
articles.authors: Andrew C Peterson, Tradd Rector, Elizabeth K Bowman et al.
articles.abstract: Asymptomatic flatfoot (AFF) is characterized by structural features of a medial arch collapse in the absence of pain, yet its dynamic biomechanical characteristics remain understudied. This study aimed to quantify and compare three-dimensional, multi-joint foot and ankle kinematics between individuals with AFF and healthy controls during walking and heel rise tasks using biplane fluoroscopy. Twenty-three participants (13 controls, 10 AFF) underwent weightbearing computed tomography to generate subject-specific bone models. Dynamic in vivo kinematics of the tibia, fibula, talus, and calcaneus were captured using biplane fluoroscopy during walking and heel rise. Joint kinematics for the tibiotalar, subtalar, tibiofibular, and talofibular joints were calculated using model-based tracking and analyzed using statistical parametric mapping. Range of motion (ROM) was also compared between groups. No significant differences in joint kinematics were observed between groups during walking. Walking ROM differences were observed only before FDR correction and were therefore interpreted as exploratory. During heel rise, AFF maintained a more everted subtalar position after SPM FDR correction and demonstrated reduced sagittal plane ROM at the tibiotalar and talofibular joint after ROM FDR correction. These findings indicate that significant group differences were detected during heel rise but not during walking within separate task specific analyses. These task dependent differences provide insight into biomechanical adaptations associated with AFF morphology, although longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these differences are related to future symptom development or deformity progression.

articles.title: Platelet Mitochondrial Bioenergetics in Adolescents at Risk of MASLD Following High-Intensity Interval Training.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Jeny E Rivera, Emir Tas, Craig Porter et al.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent cardiometabolic disorder in adolescents with obesity associated with insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Platelets contribute to inflammatory and vascular processes implicated in cardiometabolic disease, yet little is known regarding platelet mitochondrial bioenergetics in adolescents at risk for MASLD or their response to exercise training. This study characterized platelet mitochondrial respiration in adolescents at risk of MASLD and examined the effects of four weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) according to MASLD status (n=10 MASLD; n=17 non-MASLD). MASLD was defined as intrahepatic triglyceride (IHTG) content ≥5% by magnetic resonance imaging. Platelet mitochondrial respiration was assessed at enrollment and after four weeks of supervised HIIT using high-resolution respirometry. Associations with cardiometabolic and fitness markers were examined using Spearman correlations, and longitudinal changes following HIIT were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models. Adolescents were 15.4±1.5 years old and 48% were boys. At enrollment, adolescents with MASLD had higher IHTG than those without MASLD (7.39±2.67% vs. 3.02±1.13%, p=0.0002). Maximal electron transfer capacity was positively associated with IHTG (rho=0.50, p=0.008) and HOMA-IR (rho=0.44, p=0.021) and inversely associated with leptin (rho=-0.60, p=0.001). Adolescents with MASLD exhibited higher NADH-linked respiration (β=0.053, p=0.033) and succinate-supported respiration (β=0.070, p=0.012). Significant time-by-MASLD interactions demonstrated reductions in both respiration measures following HIIT only in adolescents with MASLD. In conclusion, platelet mitochondrial respiration was associated with hepatic fat content and markers of metabolic dysfunction in adolescents with obesity. HIIT was associated with differential platelet bioenergetic adaptations according to MASLD status.

articles.title: Acute and Chronic L-Carnitine Supplementation Enhances Endurance Performance Without Consistent Effects on Substrate Oxidation in Active Individuals: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Hilal Eryiğit, Yasemin Güzel, Süleyman Bulut et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aims to systematically evaluate the effects of acute and chronic L-carnitine supplementation on endurance performance and substrate oxidation during exercise among active individuals. METHODS: This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. A total of 647 studies were initially retrieved from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Ovid MEDLINE, EBSCO Open Dissertations, EBSCO Academic Search Ultimate, and SPORTDiscus databases, with searches conducted from database inception to February 1, 2026. Randomized placebo-controlled crossover and parallel-group trials were eligible for inclusion. Studies meeting the inclusion criteria were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, with the crossover-specific version applied to randomized crossover trials. RESULTS: A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. Overall, 15 (83%) studies were rated as having some concerns, three (17%) were classified as having a high risk of bias, and none were judged to be at low risk of bias. Ten studies investigated acute L-carnitine supplementation (2-15 g), seven studies examined chronic supplementation (2-3 g/day for 2-24 weeks), and one study evaluated both acute and chronic supplementation (3 g on a single day and over 2 weeks). Both acute and chronic L-carnitine supplementation were associated with improvements in endurance performance following acute supplementation and chronic supplementation. By contrast, no significant changes in fat oxidation during exercise were reported after either acute (2-4 g ingested 120-180 min before exercise) or chronic supplementation (2 g/day for 2-4 weeks). CONCLUSIONS: L-carnitine may enhance selected endurance performance outcomes among active individuals; however, its reputation as a "fat-burning" ergogenic aid is not supported by current evidence, following short-term supplementation.

articles.title: Summary of the 2026 Professionals in Nutrition for Exercise and Sport "10 Questions/10 Experts" Session-Are Sports Nutrition Guidelines Too Elite Focused for Recreational Athletes?
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Thorben Aussieker, Louise M Burke, Judith Haudum et al.
articles.abstract: This article provides a synopsis of the 10 Questions/10 Experts session at the 2026 American College of Sports Medicine Annual Meeting, which examined whether sports nutrition guidelines are equally applicable from recreational to elite athletes. Each speaker considered the validity of a given common "myth" statement and provided an evidence-based opinion to support, bust, or qualify propositions addressing the following questions: (a) Are sports nutrition guidelines based primarily on studies of elite athletes, and are they too serious for recreational athletes? (b) Do recreational marathon runners need the same in-race carbohydrate recommendations as elite marathon runners? (c) Must recreational athletes consume 1.6 g·kg-1·day-1 of protein to benefit from exercise training? (d) Does nitrate supplementation benefit elite and recreational athletes equally? (e) Do recreational athletes need a structured fluid intake plan? (f) Is sodium bicarbonate loading relevant only to elite athletes? (g) Do recreational and elite athletes require more micronutrients than suggested by the Recommended Dietary Allowances? (h) Is eating after 8:00 p.m. detrimental to performance or recovery in recreational athletes? (i) Are recreational athletes at greater risk for suboptimal vitamin D status because indoor occupations reduce sunlight exposure? and (j) Should recreational athletes train with low carbohydrate availability to amplify adaptation? This article describes the content of each presentation, including the most important evidence, practical implications, and conclusions identified by the presenters.

articles.title: An Acute Alcoholic Beer Dose Impaired Exercise Performance: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Crossover Trial.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Felipe De Russi de Lima, Vitor de Salles Painelli, Raul Canestri et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: We investigated whether a small dose of alcoholic beer ingested before a running exercise bout impaired performance and changed psychophysiological responses to exercise. METHODS: After three sessions of familiarizations, 16 healthy and physically active men (25.8 ± 5.1 years, 175.0 ± 5.4 cm, and 76 ± 6.5 kg) performed a 30-min running time trial in a double-blind and placebo-controlled crossover design, after ingesting either beer (alcohol 4.8% v/v; 0.3 g/kg) or nonalcoholic beer (placebo). Performance, cardiopulmonary (oxygen consumption, ventilation, respiratory exchange ratio, and heart rate), and perceptual (perceived exertion, affect, and motivation) variables were assessed throughout the trial and averaged every 5 min during exercise. Running economy was assessed during steady-state running at 8 km/hr. The data were analyzed through t tests and repeated-measures mixed models (p < .05). RESULTS: The ingestion of beer significantly decreased the average speed by 4.7% (p = .04; d = 0.21) and total distance covered by 4.3% (p = .007; d = 0.26) when compared with placebo. The ingestion of beer also impaired the running economy by 1.1% (p = .01; d = 0.39) and increased respiratory exchange ratio throughout the exercise bout (p = .004, d = 1.07). No beer-by-time interaction effects were detected in cardiopulmonary outcomes (p > .05). CONCLUSIONS: A small dose of alcoholic beer reduced the exercise capacity of healthy individuals, likely due to an impairment in running economy.

articles.title: Anabolic inequality among whole protein foods.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Nicholas A Burd, Žan Zupančič, Daniel R Moore et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary protein consumption in optimization strategies for supporting muscle are shifting from isolated nutrient models to integrated food-first frameworks. This perspective examines the role of food matrix integrity in regulating the primary locus of control of muscle mass in health adults: muscle protein synthesis (MPS). We propose that food processing techniques alter the matrix's physical and chemical architecture, thereby modulating the anabolic potential of whole protein foods. Consequently, identifying optimal feeding strategies requires combining mechanistic insights with food-first approaches, acknowledging that food matrix integrity is a regulatory variable in MPS regulation in support of muscle health.

articles.title: Where are the female participants in resistance training and muscle hypertrophy research? A review of gender/sex representation.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Nathalia F Dias, Deivid G Silva, Julio Benvenutti Bueno de Camargo et al.
articles.abstract: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the representation of female participants in resistance training (RT) studies investigating hypertrophy and to assess associations between participant sex, methodological features, authorship, and temporal trends. This review included RT studies published in peer-reviewed journals that assessed hypertrophy outcomes in young adults. Reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on participant sex, menstrual cycle phase reporting/consideration, use of molecular or biopsy analyses, and gender/sex of first and last authors. A total of 570 studies were included. Of these, 72.2% recruited male participants, 11.0% female participants, and 16.8% included both sexes. Among studies including female participants, 8.5% reported or accounted for menstrual cycle phase, while 87.3% did not mention it. Molecular analyses were nearly four times more frequent in studies with only male participants (23.6%) than those including female participants (6.5%; χ²=9.45; p<0.009). No association was found between participant sex and use of muscle biopsies or author gender/sex. A 10-fold increase in RT publications occurred in the 21st vs. 20th century, yet the sex gap persisted. Studies published in 2020-June 2023 showed modest improvement versus 2001-2019, with fewer male-only and more female-only and mixed-sex samples (χ²=16.43; p=0.00027; Cramér's V=0.18). Despite growing evidence that females and males exhibit broadly similar relative hypertrophy and molecular responses to RT, substantial sex bias persists in hypertrophy research. Although studies published since 2020 show modest improvement in sex-inclusive recruitment, male-only designs still predominate, and limited menstrual cycle phase reporting/accounting continues to constrain transparency and generalizability.

articles.title: The impact of work-related foot pain on work and personal life: an interview study.
articles.authors: Ann-Sophie Hörnell, Anncristine Fjellman-Wiklund, Åsa Svedmark et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The occurrence of foot pain is high, especially in those with physically demanding occupations. Work-related foot pain has been shown to impact work performance, family life, and leisure activities. While prevalence across various sectors is documented, research exploring experiences and total life impact of work-related foot pain remains limited. AIM: The aim of this study was to explore experiences of living with foot pain among individuals employed in highly demanding physical occupations, and occupations characterised by prolonged standing or walking. METHODS: A qualitative, semi-structured interview-based approach was chosen. Twelve individual interviews were conducted with nine women and three men, and analysed using Qualitative Content Analysis. RESULTS: One main theme, Walking a fine line - Balancing challenges in multiple aspects of life due to work-related foot pain, and three sub-themes were identified, describing how external work-environment factors and internal experiences of autonomy impact an individual's overall life situation, including impact on family life and the mental toll of living and working with foot pain. The sub-theme Struggling with increased pain due to work conditions and environment highlights how factors such as certain types of floors, physical work demands, time spent on the feet, walking, heavy lifting, and inadequate footwear directly exacerbate pain. The sub-theme Feeling like just another cog in the machine due to limited control over workplace organisation reflects difficulties for employees in influencing work tasks, planning daily work tasks and responsibilities, a lack of recovery during the workday, and communication within the workplace. The sub-theme Experiencing inequality and low quality of life outside of work describes the consequences for individuals' personal lives, including restricted social participation, strained family relations, negative emotions, and sleep disturbances. Overall, the individuals expressed a sense of resignation, feeling that they had to "grit their teeth" and continue working despite the pain. CONCLUSION: The central findings of this study are negative experiences and struggles, during both work and leisure time. Understanding the experiences of individuals with work-related foot pain can help employers and healthcare providers to identify work-related risks and consider preventative measures, although further research on this topic is needed. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Dynamical systems-based metrics reveal fatigue-related biomechanical changes during running in endurance-trained male and female runners.
articles.authors: Yiyang Chen, Jill Emmerzaal, Gleydciane A Fernandes et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Linear and nonlinear metrics derived from a small number of accelerometers provide global insight into fatigue-related changes and injury risk. RESEARCH QUESTION: This study aimed to determine the effects of fatigue on movement dynamics estimated from lower-back accelerometry between endurance-trained male and female runners. METHODS: Thirty-two endurance-trained runners (16 females) performed a fatiguing running task until volitional exhaustion (20 on the Borg CR20 scale), while wearing one inertial measurement unit (IMU) placed on their pelvis/lower back. Step and stride regularity (unbiased autocorrelation), root mean square (RMS)-based measures of variability (absolute RMS and RMS ratio), complexity (Sample Entropy), jerk-based measure of smoothness (Log Dimensionless Jerk; LDLJ), and stability (short- and long-term Lyapunov Exponent) were calculated from the raw accelerations. RESULTS: Significant main effects of fatigue were observed across both sexes for gait regularity, with an 8% reduction in anteroposterior step regularity and an 11% reduction in stride regularity. Fatigue also altered variability characteristics, resulting in a 12% increase in mediolateral absolute RMS, a 13% increase in anteroposterior absolute RMS, a 2% decrease in vertical RMS ratio, a 6% increase in mediolateral RMS ratio, and an 8% increase in anteroposterior RMS ratio. Fatigue increased movement complexity, as evidenced by a 14% increase in vertical Sample Entropy and an 11% increase in anteroposterior Sample Entropy. In addition to these overall fatigue effects, RMS-based measure of variability showed sex-specific responses. Interaction effects showed that males exhibited a 4% increase in the vertical absolute RMS of lower-back acceleration with fatigue, whereas females did not. SIGNIFICANCE: Both male and female endurance-trained runners may adopt a less regular and less predictable whole-body movement pattern with fatigue, while RMS-based variability showed sex-specific responses, with increased fatigue-related changes in males. These findings highlight the importance of considering both general and sex-specific adaptations when monitoring fatigue.

articles.title: A multimodal deep learning model for classifying early- versus late-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head on biparametric MRI.
articles.authors: Siyuan Li, Huimin Huang, Yetong He et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Precise early- versus late-stage stratification of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is critical for hip-preserving treatment selection, yet conventional MRI interpretation suffers from interobserver variability and limited objectivity. This study aimed to develop a multimodal deep learning model integrating biparametric MRI (STIR and T1-FSE) with clinical parameters (including age, sex, affected side (left, right, or bilateral), and etiology) to differentiate early- from late-stage ONFH and provide objective imaging evidence. METHODS: This retrospective study included 530 patients with ONFH, yielding imaging data from 851 hips. The collected data comprised STIR sequences, T1-FSE sequences, and clinical information, including age, sex, and etiology. The dataset was randomly divided at the patient level into a training set (424 patients, 675 hips) and a test set (106 patients, 176 hips) at an 8:2 ratio. Seven models were constructed: a clinical model, a STIR model, a T1-FSE model, a bpMRI model, a STIR-clinical model, a T1-FSE-clinical model, and a bpMRI-clinical model. Early- and late-fusion strategies were used for multimodal integration. The diagnostic performance of the seven models for classifying early- versus late-stage ONFH was systematically compared, with particular emphasis on their ability to identify borderline cases at the transition between clinical stages. Model interpretability was assessed using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). RESULTS: The early-fusion bpMRI-clinical model achieved the highest AUC of 0.944 (95% CI 0.905-0.973), accuracy 90.9%, sensitivity 89.0%, and specificity 92.9%, significantly outperforming single-sequence models (all P < 0.05). The confusion matrix showed that the model misclassified 10 late-stage cases as early-stage and 6 early-stage cases as late-stage. Grad-CAM visualizations indicated that the model primarily focused on clinically relevant regions, including the necrotic lesion boundary, areas of bone marrow edema, and subchondral structural abnormalities. These attention patterns were highly consistent with the core imaging features used for early- versus late-stage ONFH stratification. CONCLUSION: This study presents an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework that integrates dual-sequence MRI with clinical parameters. The framework accurately differentiates early- from late-stage ONFH according to the ARCO classification and provides objective evidence for determining the critical threshold for hip-preservation decision-making. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No: ChiCTR2300075354. Sep 1, 2023).

articles.title: An anatomically based functional upper cervical spinal unit tested under low quasi-static loading for use in an omnidirectional surrogate neck.
articles.authors: Sarah Romani, Paris Vakiel, Peter A Cripton
articles.abstract: Safety devices designed to prevent spinal cord and traumatic brain injuries are often evaluated using anthropometric test devices (ATDs). However, commonly used ATD necks lack biomechanical fidelity under multiplane loading, particularly during low-speed head impacts and axial loading. This study aimed to develop an anatomically-accurate upper cervical spine (UCS) surrogate that exhibits biofidelic kinematic responses under quasi-static flexion-extension, lateral bending, and axial torsion-a preliminary step toward a full neck surrogate capable of simulating complex multiplane loading. CT scans of a healthy 31-year-old male were used to generate vertebral geometry. Based on similarity to cadaveric ligament properties, woven cotton was selected as a ligament surrogate material. Anatomical landmarks were used to define ligament attachment points, and an adjustable attachment system enabled in-situ tensioning. The resulting UCS model was evaluated against post-mortem human subject data under quasi-static loading, assessing neutral zone (NZ), range of motion (ROM), repeatability, and helical axis of motion (HAM) using the CORA method. ROM and NZ values across all joints and degrees of freedom were within one standard deviation of literature values. The model demonstrated excellent repeatability (CORA:0.87-0.97), good biofidelity in flexion-extension (CORA:0.69-0.75; C0-C1 unloading:0.47), good-to-excellent in lateral bending (CORA:0.75-0.94), and fair-to-good in axial rotation (CORA:0.44-0.65). The mean HAM location aligned with cadaveric data in axial rotation and was slightly anterior during flexion-extension. Overall, the UCS model exhibited strong repeatability and biofidelity, supporting its potential as a preliminary component of a full cervical spine surrogate for future multiplane biomechanical research.

articles.title: News from the Foundation for Physical Therapy Research, October 2026.
Individual Calibration of a Multiinput Wearable Device Improves Exercise Energy Expenditure Estimation During Intermittent High-Intensity but Not Resistance Exercise in an Athletic Female Population.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Rebekka Frazer, Christopher D Askew, Amy-Lee Bowler et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the accuracy of a multiinput wearable device (Actiheart 5) and commercially available accelerometer (GENEActiv) in the estimation of exercise energy expenditure (EEE) during intermittent high-intensity and resistance exercise sessions among 31 trained females. Data were collected over two testing sessions involving (a) measurement of resting metabolic rate, physique and a graded exercise test on a treadmill to enable individualized calibration of the wearables, and (b) A modified Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test followed by a resistance exercise session. GENEActiv and Actiheart EEE-derived measures, using both generic and individually calibrated algorithms, were compared against (a) indirect calorimetry for Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test and (b) indirect calorimetry plus the estimated anaerobic energy contribution based on blood lactate responses for resistance exercise. Equivalence was evaluated using predefined bounds of ±10% mean indirect calorimetry EEE. The use of individually-calibrated Actiheart algorithms improved estimation of EEE during Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test (mean bias 4.5 ± 60.4 kcal) compared with individually-calibrated GENEActiv algorithms (mean bias 69.5 ± 86.6 kcal), and equivalence with indirect calorimetry was achieved, although substantial individual error remained (95% limits of agreement -113.9 to 122.8 kcal and intraclass correlation coefficients, .62 [.34 to .80]). Individualized Actiheart algorithms provided equivalent group-level estimates of EEE during intermittent high-intensity exercise, whereas neither Actiheart nor GENEActiv demonstrated acceptable validity or equivalence against the reference method for resistance training, suggesting Metabolic Equivalents of Task may be a more practical method of estimating EEE.

articles.title: Axial Complex of Deep-Sea Acorn Worm Quatuoralisia malakhovi (Hemichordata, Enteropneusta, Torquaratoridae).
articles.authors: Olga V Ezhova, Anastasiya I Lukinykh, Vladimir V Malakhov
articles.abstract: The axial complex (proboscis complex or heart-kidney) is well-studied for the shallow-living enteropneusts that burrow into the sediment and use the muscular proboscis as the primary locomotor organ. However, the deep-sea enteropneusts in the family Torquaratoridae are epibenthic surface-dwellers with a dispersed, poorly developed proboscis musculature. There is little data on the structure of their axial complex (AC). We have studied in detail the microscopic anatomy of the AC of three specimens of torquaratorid Quatuoralisia malakhovi Ezhova et Lukinykh, 2022. The proboscis of Q. malakhovi is widely fused with the collar along the entire dorsal side rather than being connected by a narrow stalk. The AC includes the buccal diverticulum (stomochord), pericardium, glomerulus (axial organ) and associated blood vessels, perihaemal coeloms, and proboscis skeletal elements. The latter are two separate symmetrical plates supporting the buccal diverticulum laterally. The buccal diverticulum is elongated in transverse direction and packed with large, vacuolated cells without a lumen. It is completely separated from the main course of the gut. The pericardium lies on the dorsal side of the buccal diverticulum. The heart is absent. The glomerulus consists of two symmetrical extensions separated by the confluence of the dorsal blood vessel. The latter is accompanied by the perihaemal coeloms and splits into several branches resembling the mouth of a river, which then flow into the glomerulus. Two buccal blood vessels with folded walls run from the sides of the glomerulus to the ventral blood vessel. A protocoelomic coelomopore is absent, however we found a pair of mesocoelomic coelomoducts and coelomopores. The torquaratorid AC demonstrates varying degrees of reduction. None of the previously studied species of Torquaratoridae possesses a complete set of AC components characteristic of shallow-living enteropneusts. Torquaratoridae are derived in terms of structure and composition of the AC compared to non-torquaratorid hemichordates.

articles.title: Biological Insights From the Osteohistology of a Nile Crocodile.
articles.authors: Ayanda Buso, Maria Eugenia Pereyra, Anusuya Chinsamy
articles.abstract: While long bones are mostly utlised for skeletochronology of extant and extinct vertebrates, among crocodilians, dermal bones have also been studied. However, there is a lack of a systematic and comprehensive study of the variation in osteohistology and skeletochronology of limb, axial, and dermal bones of extant crocodilians. Here, we undertake a comprehensive assessment of the histology of multiple postcranial elements of a single, captive adult Crocodylus niloticus (with approximately known age) to assess their utility for skeletochronology. We document the intraskeletal histological variability in the skeleton and show that despite the gastralia recording the highest number of growth rings, the radius, ulna, and fibula are more reliable for skeletochronology. We show substantial variation in the histology of the osteoderms depending on the plane of sectioning, as well as their location on the body of the crocodile. Additionally, we report that anteriorly sectioned dorsal osteoderms preserved the highest number of growth marks. Our study provides important information regarding intraskeletal variation in osteohistology and presents key information regarding the choice of skeletal elements for reliable life history reconstruction of C. niloticus.

articles.title: Functional Adaptations for Load-Bearing in a Dermal Bone: The Pectoral Fin Spine of the Russian Sturgeon (Huso Gueldenstaedtii).
articles.authors: Esteban Marroquín-Arroyave, Joshua Milgram
articles.abstract: Dermal bone, which forms a variety of skeletal structures and persists in a wide range of extant vertebrates, evolved prior to endochondral bone which forms all mammalian load-bearing long bones. Sturgeons (Acipenseriformes) are an early-diverging extant lineage of actinopterygians that retain prominent post-cranial dermal skeletal elements. They retain a long robust spine at the leading edge of the pectoral fin, called the pectoral fin spines (PFS). PFS are bone elements that are present in many extinct and extant species of non-tetrapod jawed fish.
